News.title: Dad left with brain damage & ‘looking like Homer Simpson’ after 5kg steel plate smashed through windscreen
News.content:
D'OH DEAR Dad left with brain damage & ‘looking like Homer Simpson’ after 5kg steel plate smashed through windscreen

A DAD was left with brain damage and “looking like Homer Simpson” after a 5kg steel plate flew off a lorry and smashed through his windscreen.

Anthony Moore, 51, was left fuming after the driver who left him with life changing injuries only received three penalty points and a £100 fine.



The dad-of-three from Heath Hayes, Staffs, said: “My life has been destroyed because somebody failed to do one basic thing – secure a load properly.”

The 51-year-old’s facial injuries and swelling were so bad that his wife later said it left him looking like “Homer Simpson”.



The driver was prosecuted by police for driving with an unsecured load – but Anthony said the punishment is “an insult to every road user”.

Now, after suing the driver’s employer and parent company, Anthony has secured a substantial six-figure out-of-court settlement.





Anthony said: “I wasn’t speeding. I wasn’t taking risks. I was simply driving home from work to my family.

“Within a split second everything I had worked for disappeared. I have lost my career, my independence, my health, and the life I had built with my wife and children.”

He added that his wife has had to give up her job to care for him full time, and the family have spent the last three years trying to rebuild their life.

Anthony said: “I don’t want sympathy. I want accountability. I want companies to understand that securing a load properly isn’t paperwork or box-ticking.

“It is the difference between somebody getting home safely or spending the rest of their life disabled.”



Anthony was minutes from home when the 5kg solid steel plate crashed through the windscreen of his Ford Ranger in September 2023.

It struck his head and his 4×4 careered underneath the same truck and was dragged for almost half a mile before the driver stopped.

The driver was slapped with an £100 fine, three penalty points and a a four week licence suspension from the regional Traffic Commissioner.



Before the crash, Anthony was a senior manager for an events specialist and a devoted dad to his three children, nine, 15 and 21.

His wife Rachel, 45, said: “When I saw Tony I barely recognised him. His face was massively swollen, his eyes were bulging, everything was black and purple.

“He honestly looked like Homer Simpson because the swelling was so severe. There was blood everywhere. It was absolutely horrific.”

Anthony suffered a traumatic brain injury with brain bleeds, and multiple fractures to his skull and face, including a broken eye socket and cheekbone, a fractured right hand, and significant mouth injuries.

After initially surviving his injuries, he developed severe paranoid delusions caused by his brain injury, believing hospital staff were trying to kill him.



He spent just two weeks in hospital, being moved between different wards before eventually being discharged home.

With specialist NHS brain injury rehabilitation limited, the family turned to catastrophic injury lawyers at Express Solicitors for expert help.

They secured funding for intensive neurorehabilitation, psychology, physiotherapy, occupational therapy and specialist support workers while pursuing a legal claim against the driver’s company.

While the case was referred by police to the HSE, they were unable to take any action against the company due to the incident happening on the motorway and the Traffic Commissioner took no further action.

The family later obtained a six-figure settlement against Joseph Ash Galvanizing, a subsidiary company of parent company Hill & Smith PLC.



This will fund Anthony’s future rehabilitation, specialist medical treatment and long-term care.

Catastrophic injury solicitor Nina Ramsden, of Express Solicitors, said: “Tony sustained life-changing injuries in an entirely preventable accident.

“His life changed forever during an ordinary journey home from work.

“His injuries are very complex, but this settlement will ensure Tony can continue receiving the specialist rehabilitation and support he requires while providing financial security for his family’s future.”

A spokesperson for Staffordshire Police said: “A summons was sent to the driver for the insecure load, with a traffic commissioner referral made in relation to the company.



“The driver received points on his licence as well as a fine.

“The Health and Safety Executive was also informed, though no further action was taken by them, due to the incident taking place on a road and not a business premises.”

The West Midlands Traffic Commissioner wrote to the company involved, but took no enforcement action in relation to load security, as policies in place were correct.

The driver attended a conduct hearing and had his vocational licence suspended for 4-weeks.

Hill and Smith PLC – parent company of Joseph Ash Galvanizing – said: “Hill & Smith confirms that Mr Moore sustained a serious injury as a result of a regrettable incident in 2023, with a lorry belonging to its Joseph Ash Galvanizing subsidiary.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The matter has been subject to the appropriate legal and regulatory processes, and we can confirm a settlement was reached, acknowledging the serious nature of the injury.

“We take health and safety across our group extremely seriously and continue to review and strengthen our procedures to help prevent incidents of this nature.”

News.title: Jailed female prison officer, 25, promised to wait until drug kingpin lover served sentence in gushing Valentine’s card
News.content:
'LOVE YOU ALWAYS' Jailed female prison officer, 25, promised to wait until drug kingpin lover served sentence in gushing Valentine’s card

A PRISON officer promised to wait out her drug kingpin lover’s 12-year sentence in a gushing Valentine’s Day card found in the lag’s cell.

Jai Gascoyne, who has since been jailed following her affair, wrote to Dil Nawaz: “Anyone can say I love you but not everyone can wait and prove it”.



The card continued: “Happy Valentine’s Day D, here’s to the first of forever and I can’t wait for the future.”

The 25-year-old prison guard at HMP Buckley Hall signed off “love you always”.



Her heartfelt card was found when Nawaz’s cell was searched after prison anti-corruption officials received intelligence.

Officers also found the 30-year-old wearing a silver bracelet engraved with a “J”, a match to a “D” necklace Gascoyne was wearing when she was searched.

The former prison guard claimed this was for her dad, but she was also found with a second necklace engraved with Arabic script that she could not explain the meaning of.



Manchester Crown Court heard how it was thought to be an Islamic prayer for protection.

Officers later discovered the prison guard had ordered two bracelets and two necklaces with pendants on Amazon.

In Gascoyne’s car officer’s found a ring in a box alongside a love letter also signed off “I love you always”.

The same investigation also uncovered that Nawaz’s brother Haq Nawaz, 32, was involved in an affair with another prison officer, Elle Walron, 27.

The brothers were both locked up for heading a OCG gang with their other brother Asim Nawaz.



It is believed the gang distributed between £2.15m and £3.1m worth of crack cocaine and heroin over a 12-month period.

On top of Haq and Dil Nawaz’s sentences – 13 years and 10 months and 12 years respectively – the pair will now serve an additional 12 months for their secret relationships.

The prison officers were also sentenced on August 7, Gascoyne was handed a 16- month sentence while Walton will serve 13 months



Gascoyne, of Dukinfield, Greater Manchester, pleaded guilty to two counts of misconduct in public office.

She also had inappropriate contact with a further two prisoners, Manchester Crown Court heard.

Walton, of Bacup, Lancashire, pleaded guilty to one count.

Alongside the cards and jewellery, the couples sent hundreds of messages and exchanged gifts and money.

Gascoyne and Dil Nawaz even declared their “love” for each other in their messages and he discussed “wanting to have sex”.



The court heard how he suggested the prison officer could take him to the chapel or “open his door and go in his room.”

Dil Nawaz said he wanted “companionship” as he struggled with his mental health following a prison attack, the court heard.

Meanwhile, his brother had “‘wanted someone to talk to” due to feeling isolated from his family.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Recorder Ben Lawrence said their case “strikes at the heart of the public faith in the prison system”.

He added that the sentences would be a “deterrent” for “the next young female prison officer who considers starting a relationship with a prisoner.”

News.title: Huge fire breaks out at London industrial estate as 100 firefighters flood scene and plumes of smoke seen for miles
News.content:
A FIRE has broken out at an industrial estate in London sending clouds of black smoke into the sky.

Around 100 firefighters raced to the scene to battle the blaze on Ripple Road, Barking.



Thick plumes of smoke can be seen billowing into the sky for miles.

One resident said on X that a strong smell of smoke could be smelt across east London.



London Fire Brigade said they received at least 15 calls about the fire from 12.47pm.

A spokesperson for the service said: “Fifteen fire engines and around 100 firefighters have been called to a fire on Ripple Road in Barking.

“A section of the A13 has been closed as crews carry out firefighting operations. Traffic will be heavily impacted as we work to bring the fire under control.

“The fire is producing a large amount of smoke. Where possible, residents in the local area should keep doors and windows closed.

“The Brigade’s Control Office took the first of 15 calls at 1247 and mobilised crews from Barking, Dagenham, Ilford and other surrounding fire stations to the scene.

“The cause is not known at this stage.”



Local residents have been told to to shut their windows and doors as the fire service warned there was a “large amount of smoke”.

News.title: Moment furious dad BOOTS gorilla mascot who knocked over child – as costumed bloke is sent flying and unable to get up
News.content:
THIS is the moment a furious dad kicks a man in a gigantic gorilla suit to the ground after he accidentally knocks over a child.

The disoriented mascot was sent tumbling to the ground and unable to stand back up due to the huge suit as dozens of shocked people watched on.



Resurfaced footage shows a group of children playing with the towering grey gorilla in a busy Shaanxi province in north-central China.

One of the young boys appears to start wildly swinging his arms as a concerned adult drags him away.



The giant great ape then appears to stumble forwards as the man inside runs into the group of kids and even manages to kick over the man’s child.

Fuming at the mascot for sending his young boy flying, the man responds by running up to him and kicking him directly in the stomach.

The gorilla goes flying as people dash to get out of the way from the falling beast.

He hits the ground and is left sprawled out with the size and weight of the suit making it almost impossible for the mascot to get back up.



The mascot was filmed writhing around on the floor for several painful seconds as no one intervened.

No injuries were reported as the mascot eventually got back to his feet safely.

Several people online quickly commented on the video as they argued over who was at fault for the brawl.

Some defended the ape mascot saying: “It was an accident. It’s difficult to see or move in those costumes.”

Others even joked: “That gorilla should press charges for assault.”

News.title: ‘Hellish’ life in UK’s vape shop capital where 54 eyesore stores pack two streets – but will PM’s crackdown REALLY work?
News.content:
RESIDENTS of UK’s “hellish” vape shop capital where 54 stores are packed across two streets are left wondering if the Prime Minister’s crackdown will really work.

Andy Burnham has announced plans to clampdown on vape stores and rogue operators to restore “unrecognisable” high streets.



It means planning permission would be needed for outlets selling e-cigarettes, and the definition of a vape shop will be tightened to stop businesses side-stepping new rules by claiming to be a convenience store.

The Cheetham Hill area of Manchester – Burnham’s former mayoral patch – has been overrun with a whopping 54 vape shops crammed into two streets.



Resident Sterling Jones, 27, shops at nearby electronic stores and believes there are “far too many” vape shops in the area.

He said: “Nobody needs this many vape shops. It all seems a bit dodgy.





“It spoils the character of the area to be honest. Whenever I drive past, it looks hellish.”

Hailey Wu, 24, said the vape shops have “taken over’ the area.

She added: “They dominate everything else. I think they should all be licensed. But they probably don’t like too much regulation.”

Sonia Khan, 30, who lives nearby in Ratcliffe, Bury, comes to the area to buy toys for her online business.

“A lot of these shops appeal to youngsters because they’re colourful and sell a lot of different vape flavours,’ she said.



Sonia claims she has seen “frequent” cop raids in the area since Greater Manchester Police‘s launched Operation Vulcan which blitzed Cheetham Hill and Strangeways, known as “the counterfeit capital of Europe“.

The Prime Minister recently praised the initiative for clearing the area of counterfeits and proving what could be achieved when multiple agencies work together.

Manchester City Council said that they and the police have worked hard to “shut down known counterfeit shops, prevent criminals returning, and then work to regenerate the area so that people can feel safe in their communities”.



Seana Parkinson, 55, who lives locally and is a vape user, has to go to the area to collect her granddaughters from a dance class.

She said: “I agree high streets need to be cleaned up. You come here and it does look a bit of an eyesore. It’s ridiculous there are 54 shops.

“Although I’m a vape user myself, I always go to the same shop near my home because it’s someone I can trust and I know it’s legit.”

However, Mr Singh, 40, owner of Smoke Zone Ltd, which sells vapes and other smoking products, said he was just providing what his customers wanted and was “100% legal”.

He said: “Everything I do is legal. They shouldn’t make more rules which make it more difficult for vape shop owners.



“We’re just here providing products to our customers in the same way any shop would.”

Junaid Safdar, 25, manager of the nearby Vape Boyz, said vape shops “were not the problem”.

He said: “Too much regulation will impact shop owners really badly. From October, we’re already going to pay more duty on the products we import from China.



“And these costs will have to be passed on to the customer. So it’s a bad idea to make vape shop owners apply for planning permission – it will kill a lot of business.

“And more regulation would be definitely be bad news for us.”

The Centre for Social Justice has reported that since 2016, nearly 1,800 pubs and bars have closed across the UK, while the number of vape and tobacco shops has risen to nearly 2,200.

Mr Burnham said: “For many people, the high streets they grew up with have been hollowed out and become unrecognisable over decades of decline.

“The rise of vape shops, betting shops and rogue operators have replaced the shops, services, and community spaces that people are crying out for.



“That’s not on. I said we would improve Britain’s high streets, and that’s exactly what we are starting to do.”

However, the PM has been accused of tarring betting shops with the same brush as crooks – after lumping them in with dodgy dealers.

The Betting and Gaming Council said: “It is wrong to lump highly regulated, licensed betting shops together with rogue or criminal businesses.”

A spokesperson for Manchester City Council said: “Over the past three years a significant amount of effort has gone into forcing out criminal elements from communities in North Manchester.

“Through Operation Vulcan the Council and Greater Manchester Police have worked to shut down known counterfeit shops, prevent criminals returning, and then work to regenerate the area so that people can feel safe in their communities once more.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Work has continued through the Trading Standards team to gather intelligence on businesses suspected of illegal activity, and we have a track record of taking action through the courts to shut these businesses down.

“Alongside this we continue to foster relationships with businesses throughout the area, the vast of which trade legally and who are run by members of the community who are keen to see their area prosper.”

News.title: Woman, 23, charged with murder after man found dead in block of flats following ‘assault’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FLAT HORROR Woman, 23, charged with murder after man found dead in block of flats following ‘assault’

A WOMAN has been charged with murder after a man was found dead in a block of flats following an “assault”.

Craig Mintram, 45, was discovered in the early hours of Sunday morning in Southampton, Hampshire.



Katie Linin appeared at Southampton Magistrates’ Court today charged with murder.

The 23-year-old spoke to confirm her name and date of birth during the brief hearing.



She was remanded into custody ahead of a hearing at Southampton Crown Court tomorrow.

A 54-year-old man was arrested in connection with the horror but has been released from custody without any further action.



Hampshire Constabulary said it was called to the block of flats at around 4.21am following reports of an assault.

A spokesperson added: “Officers attended the property but Craig was sadly pronounced deceased at the scene.

“His family were notified and continue to be supported by specially trained officers.”

News.title: Man rushed to hospital after being bitten by shark on boat off Co Waterford coast
News.content:
SHARK HORROR Man rushed to hospital after being bitten by shark on boat off Co Waterford coast

A MAN has been rushed to hospital after being bitten by a shark off the coast of Co Waterford.

Rescue crews were alerted to the incident after a report of a shark bite on board a small fishing vessel south of Ardmore at around 4:15pm yesterday.

The man suffered a leg injury after being bitten by the shark while on the boat yesterday evening.

The Irish Coast Guard confirmed the incident, adding that the man was taken to Cork University Hospital, where he remains in treatment.





Ballycotton RNLI and Youghal RNLI responded to the incident and the rescue 117 helicopter was tasked to the scene.

Ballycotton RNLI’s all-weather lifeboat was deployed at 4:30pm yesterday in calm seas and good visibility.

Arriving on scene at approximately 5:10pm, crew members launched a major rescue operation before transferring the man for emergency evacuation to Cork University Hospital.

In a statement, a RNLI spokesperson said: “At 4.16pm, Ballycotton RNLI was requested to launch by Dublin Coast Guard to assist a 5-metre pleasure craft with five people on board, approximately four miles off Ram Head, Ardmore.



“The call formed part of a coordinated response involving Ballycotton RNLI, Youghal RNLI and Irish Coast Guard Helicopter Rescue 117.

“Both lifeboats remained on standby while the casualty was winched from the vessel by Rescue 117 and transferred for emergency evacuation to Cork University Hospital.

“The remaining members of the group did not require assistance, and the casualty vessel subsequently returned safely to Dungarvan. Both lifeboats were then stood down.

“Ballycotton RNLI returned to harbour at approximately 6.15pm, where the lifeboat was refuelled before the volunteer crew continued with their scheduled weekly training session.”



Coxswain on duty, Eolan Walsh, described the operation as a “well-coordinated multi-agency response.”

Walsh also urged the public to take extra caution on the water, warning that”conditions at sea can change quickly” and safety should be a priority.

Walsh added: “This was a well-coordinated multi-agency response, with Ballycotton RNLI, Youghal RNLI and Rescue 117 working together to ensure that the casualty received urgent medical assistance as quickly and safely as possible.

“Our crew were pleased to be able to support the operation and remain on scene while the casualty was transferred for emergency treatment and we wish the casualty a full recovery.”

“Incidents such as this are a reminder that conditions at sea can change quickly and that anyone heading offshore should make safety a priority.



“Ensure your vessel is suitable for the conditions, wear a properly fitted lifejacket or personal flotation device, carry a reliable means of communication, and make sure someone ashore knows your plans.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“If you get into difficulty at sea, call for help early — contacting the Coast Guard at 999 or 112 can make all the difference.”

The Ballycotton RNLI crew involved in the rescue were Eolan Walsh (Coxswain), Alan Cott (Mechanic), Conor Philpott (Navigator), Eolan Breathnach, Áine Flynn, Stephen Sloane and Ronan Lynch.

News.title: French diplomat in Africa ‘invited “parade” of locals half his age for sex at official home’ – sparking security alert
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SLEAZY PALACE French diplomat in Africa ‘invited “parade” of locals half his age for sex at official home’ – sparking security alert

A SENIOR French diplomat has been accused of hosting a succession of local African women at his official home for sex, triggering a major security alert.

The Ambassador for the Central African Republic (CAR), Bruno Foucher, 65, allegedly hosted young women – aged between 20 and 30 – at the embassy in Bangui.



Foucher welcomed the “endless parade” of at least 30 locals through his doors over a four-year period, according to Le Canard enchaîné.

An official report seen by the French magazine states that Mr Foucher admitted to sex with at least two of the women who were local Africans.



He also reportedly confessed to allowing one of the women to stay in his residence while he was away carrying out official duties.

The report alleged the diplomat ambassador received about 15 visits per month.

The visits – dating from January 2020 to March 2024 – have sparked major security concerns over Russian influence in the area.

Alarms were subsequently raised within the GIGN – France‘s elite counter-terrorism and special operations unit.



The Russian paramilitary group Wagner is known to have a significant presence in the CAR.

The group are said to ensure the security of President Faustin-Archange Touadéra.

Touadéra is known to be in receipt of cash from Moscow, which has been used to finance his election campaigns.

A French Foreign Ministry spokesman said: “At the ministry’s initiative, an administrative inquiry was conducted in Bangui in 2026.

“Upon receipt of the mission’s findings, and at the Foreign Minister’s request, the Ministry initiated disciplinary proceedings against the Ambassador. These proceedings are ongoing.”



Paris regularly accuses Russia of stoking hostility towards western countries including France in CAR, mainly through disinformation campaigns on social media.

Relations between France and CAR have improved since 2024, however, and in March French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot visited the African country.

It was the first high-level French visit to CAR since 2018, and Mr Barrot spoke of “a full restoration of relations”.

France colonized the region as Ubangi-Shari in 1903 and grouped it into French Equatorial Africa.

The CAR gained formal independence from France in 1960.



Foucher is a career diplomat who joined France’s foreign service after studying at ENA, the country’s elite administrative school.

He faces dismissal from the foreign service or a severe reprimand.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He has not commented publicly on the scandal.

The Wagner Group, officially known as PMC Wagner, is a Russian paramilitary organisation that was founded in 2014.

News.title: Three ways to watch the solar eclipse safely without glasses
News.content:
With most online orders not able to arrive in time and shops running out of stock, it may be too late to buy eclipse glasses for Wednesday evening.

But you can still safely watch the spectacle using some household items.

People in the UK will see a partial eclipse - rather than the total eclipse that will be seen in parts of Spain, Greenland and Iceland - but it is the country's most significant eclipse since 1999.

Experts say enthusiasts should not look directly at the Sun without specialist glasses.

And you shouldn't be tempted to try using sunglasses or dark goggles instead.

They often don't give enough UV protection when looking directly at the Sun and you could end up seriously damaging your eyesight, according to The Royal Astronomical Society.

Here are some viewing methods to try instead.

News.title: Burnham says disposable BBQ ban under consideration
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said the government is considering a ban on disposable barbecues amid increased wildfire risk driven by this summer's droughts.

The prime minister told reporters single-use grills had been behind a number of recent blazes and people should not be using them "at this moment in time".

Some retailers have already decided to voluntarily stop selling the devices, which have previously attracted warnings from fire chiefs.

It comes as Burnham chairs an emergency Cobra meeting on the government's response to record temperatures in recent months.

Nearly three-quarters of England and all of Wales have been officially declared in drought, creating conditions rife for fire to spread.

The Met Office has issued a rare amber extreme heat warning for Thursday, with temperatures peaking in the mid-to-high 30s across the Midlands and south-east of England, and a high of 38C possible.

Speaking during a visit to Stevenage, Burnham said a disposable barbecue ban was something the government was "certainly going to consider".

"I do want to leave the meeting today with a loud and clear message that we do want people to take the greatest possible care when they are out in the countryside, both in terms of cigarettes, but also those temporary barbecues that we know are causing risk of fires," he added.

News.title: Jasper Carrott says family is 'so proud' of Lucy Davis after cancer diagnosis
News.content:
Actor and comedian Jasper Carrott has spoken about his pride and love for daughter Lucy Davis after she announced she has incurable breast cancer.

The actress, best known for playing receptionist Dawn Tinsley in BBC sitcom The Office, has received an outpouring of support since she revealed her diagnosis on Tuesday.

Carrott, one of the most familiar faces on British television over several decades, told BBC News: "This is a very difficult time for the whole family and we have been supporting her in every way possible since her diagnosis.

"We are so grateful for all the support we have had over this trying time and we are very hopeful for her future being what she wants it to be."

He added: "We are so proud of our daughter and love her so much. The way she has conducted herself through many traumatic health issues is a lesson to us all.

"We would request privacy for the coming months, but thanks once again for the love and concern shown by so many people."

Carrott, whose real name is Robert Davis, became a household name in the 1970s thanks to his stand-up comedy and novelty songs.

He has presented programmes such as Canned Carrott, Golden Balls and Carrott's Commercial Breakdown, and acted in comedy series such as The Detectives.

News.title: Cambridge review into Jason Arday post will be independent, university says
News.content:
The University of Cambridge will carry out an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding Jason Arday's appointment and his time at the university, its vice-chancellor has confirmed.

The investigation will be carried out by senior academics from within and beyond Cambridge and will begin "as soon as possible".

Arday resigned as a Cambridge professor of sociology of education last week amid allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements.

The 41-year-old - who became Cambridge's youngest ever black professor in 2023 - denies any plagiarism and said the recent furore had led to "an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack".

In a letter to university staff, Prof Deborah Prentice said she knows there is "anger and anxiety around this damaging and difficult case" and she shares concerns raised by those in Cambridge and beyond.

The letter continued: "Our staff of colour are highly valued, for their scholarship, their achievements, and the contributions they make to the institution and the wider academic community."

Prentice said the case "should not be used to cast aspersions on their work or the legitimacy of their roles at Cambridge".

The findings of the investigation, previously announced on Friday, will inform a review into the process for the appointment of senior academic roles, the university has said.

News.title: Spotify to add label for AI-generated artists and remove them from recommendations
News.content:
Spotify is introducing a new feature that will highlight if an artist has been generated by artificial intelligence (AI).

The streaming service says the AI Persona badge, that will start appearing on some profiles from mid-September, will flag to listeners if an "artist's identity may be AI-generated and does not represent a real person".

The changes are being introduced to give listeners "more transparency" about what they're hearing, Spotify says.

It comes after some music fans made it "clear" to the streamer they don't like seeing a profile that seems to be a human, to then realise it's AI-generated.

AI-generated music has long been a concern for fans and artists.

Musician Alex Winn tells BBC Newsbeat he thinks the incoming feature is a "really good thing".

"It almost separates the people who have created music properly from the people just using AI," says guitarist Winn, who plays in the North East band Swindled.

The musician feels people want to "connect emotionally with music" and he thinks "AI can't really do that".

The 19-year-old also says having the AI label will help people make an informed choice about their listening habits, and he hopes it will redirect users to other artists and help level the playing field.

"Bands are finding it hard to compete no matter what, nevermind with some AI bands taking over," he says.

The BBC previously heard from one frustrated listener, who, after finding his playlists increasingly sprinkled with tracks he suspected were AI-generated, built a tool to automatically label and block them.

Announcing the change, external, Spotify says "true artist-fan connection can only be built on a foundation of trust and authenticity".

"In music, that means listeners need to be able to trust that the artist behind the music is who they say they are," it adds.

"That's more essential than ever in the age of generative AI."

News.title: X-Men star Nicholas Hoult joins cast of Harry Potter TV show
News.content:
Nicholas Hoult, known for his roles in X-Men, Superman and Mad Max: Fury Road, has been cast in the hotly anticipated Harry Potter TV series.

The English actor, 36, will play Hogwarts professor Gilderoy Lockhart - who was portrayed by Sir Kenneth Branagh in the films.

The TV adaptation of JK Rowling's best-selling books will reach screens this Christmas, although Hoult will not be seen until season two.

In the stories, Lockhart was a celebrity author of books such as Magical Me before joining Hogwarts as a Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher in Harry's second year.

HBO announced the casting, external by quoting the title of Lockhart's autobiography and one of his famous lines: "Magical me indeed. Now, how many autographs would you like? Nicholas Hoult has been cast as Gilderoy Lockhart in season two of the new HBO original Harry Potter series."

News.title: How the weather will affect your viewing
News.content:
One of the most spectacular solar eclipses the UK has seen for decades is taking place on Wednesday 12 August.

From around 18:00 BST, the Moon will begin moving across the face of the Sun, creating a partial solar eclipse across the UK.

At its peak, around 90% of the Sun will be covered from London. In Cornwall, as much as 95% of the Sun could be obscured.

Depending on where you are in the UK, it will peak between 19:02 and 19:16 BST.

News.title: After the eclipse, a meteor shower - how to catch a glimpse
News.content:
The best annual meteor shower has once again returned to our skies, and the Perseids dazzling display is set to peak on Wednesday night.

But skywatchers will be treated to not one, but two, impressive astronomical events within just a few hours of each other.

A deep partial solar eclipse will be also visible in the UK in the early evening before the Sun sets and the stars emerge. While the two events are unrelated, their timing makes for an exceptional night of stargazing.

Astronomer Dr Becky Smethurst said it was "the perfect cosmic coincidence of events".

Here is when to look up and where you will have the best views of the meteor shower.

News.title: Early release scheme risks more serious crimes, probation chief inspector warns
News.content:
The chief inspector of probation for England and Wales has told the BBC the early release of thousands of prisoners could lead to "a serious sexual or violent offence or even murder" because of the demands on probation staff to monitor offenders.

The government is set to release 5,000 offenders from October as part of new laws to create more space in overcrowded prisons.

Probation officers supervise offenders after prison sentences and check they follow the terms of their release, such as sticking to curfews and not taking drugs.

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said "protecting the public is our top priority", adding it had invested in probation and hiring trainee officers.

But Martin Jones, His Majesty's Chief Inspector of probation for England and Wales, told the BBC that "ultimately I'm not fully confident that the probation system will be able to cope with this massive work and there's a risk that things will go wrong".

"Probation services are already under unprecedented pressure.

"I mean, they're managing a caseload of 258,000 cases, that's nearly three times the number that are in our prisons, and obviously the early release scheme will be increasing that pressure considerably."

On Tuesday, 50 police chiefs across the UK signed a letter to the prime minister urging him to pursue "every legal option" to prevent the early release of PC Andrew Harper's killers under the scheme.

They called for called for greater consideration of victims when prisoners have their sentences altered, adding: "Families across the country are now facing the distress of learning that offenders may be released earlier than they understood when sentence was passed."

They also welcomed Burnham's intervention on Tuesday, when he said he was "confident" the early release of Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were jailed for 13 years for manslaughter in 2020, in January could be stopped.

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp told BBC Breakfast the early release plans had "put public safety at risk as well as disrespecting victims and undermining confidence in the criminal justice system".

He urged Burnham to "pay attention and listen" to the senior police officers, adding he had "never seen every chief constable in the country write to the prime minister directly in this way".

Philip and Nick Timothy, the Conservative shadow justice secretary, wrote to Burnham on Tuesday urging him to introduce emergency primary legislation in September to amend the Sentencing Act 2026.

The letter said grooming gang perpetrators, including those convicted of indecent assault, and those convicted of the manslaughter of an emergency worker should be exempt from the early release scheme.

News.title: Burnham to chair Cobra meeting on extreme heat as temperatures surge again
News.content:
The Cobra meeting will be attended by ministers from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, Home Office, and Department for Health, as well as the Environment Agency.

It will be the second Cobra meeting this year on heatwaves, after one took place amid high temperatures in June.

A spokesperson for No 10 said this summer was proving "challenging" in the UK, particularly for "firefighters tackling wildfires, farmers working in drought conditions, and NHS staff in busy A&E units".

"We will continue to take the action needed to keep communities safe, protect water supplies and safeguard the environment," they said.

The hottest weather this week is expected on Thursday across the Midlands, Eastern England, London and south-east England, Yorkshire and Humber.

Temperatures could potentially reach 38C which would equal the highest temperature of the summer so far recorded at Lingwood in Norfolk on 26 June.

This would be the hottest August day since 2003, when 38.5C was recorded.

It is also likely to be the fourth calendar month this year to record 35C or more, which is unprecedented.

On Monday, drought officials declared 71.3% of England in drought, meaning there are a total of 45 million people now living in a drought area, with more than 27 million facing water use restrictions.

Firefighters have responded to 966 wildfires across England and Wales this year, including 185 in the first 10 days of August, and 458 in July, according to the National Fire Chiefs Council.

A fire in the New Forest has been burning since Sunday, which started after a van caught fire on the A31 near Ringwood.

Last week, Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said the NHS should be "preparing for summer pressures now in the same way we prepare for winter".

She told LBC Radio plans were in place to respond to higher numbers of people coming in to A&E.

On Tuesday, the Met Office said this summer is on course to be the UK's hottest since records began, with the mean temperature currently at 16.48C set to surpass the figure set just last year.

This is in line with evidence that summers are getting hotter and are likely to become drier because of climate change.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski said the Cobra meeting was just a first step, and a "climate emergency" had led to hundreds of deaths and was "stretching our firefighters, health staff and farmers to the limit".

He called for "concrete action" and said he looked forward to hearing how Burnham intended to "prepare for the threats to come".

News.title: Serious failings found in new military crimes unit, leaked report finds
News.content:
A leaked Ministry of Defence (MoD) report, obtained by the BBC, has highlighted serious failings in a new military command set up to investigate the most severe crimes, including rape and sexual assault.

The Defence Serious Crime Command (DSCC) was launched after the death of 19-year-old Gunner Jaysley Beck. An inquest found the Army's mishandling of sexual assault and harassment complaints made by Beck contributed to her taking her own life, and exposed "systemic failings".

However, an internal review highlighted ongoing concerns with the unit and warned the military still risks failing victims.

The MoD said the findings had been accepted and significant work has been undertaken since.

The DSCC was created in 2022 to investigate serious crimes independently, outside the military's chain of command.

However, the BBC can reveal that an internal review, which was carried out between 21 August 2025 and 12 November 2025 and overseen by a former senior civilian police officer, concluded that if the DSCC was subjected to scrutiny similar to civilian police forces there would be "a significant risk of (it) being graded as inadequate".

In a statement, the MoD said the review was commissioned "to provide honest challenge, identify areas of improvement and to help ensure the highest standards for victims and witnesses".

It added that following the findings, the DSCC had carried out significant work "including further investment in victim and witness support, strengthening governance and safeguarding arrangements and accrediting investigators to nationally recognised policing standards".

The DSCC was committed to transparency, continuous improvement and ensuring victims receive the support and service they deserve, the statement continued.

News.title: Four guilty over torture death of man set alight
News.content:
Four people have been found guilty over charges relating to the death of a man doused in petrol and set on fire.

Tomasz Samel was kidnapped in 2019 from his home in Birmingham by an organised crime group who believed he was responsible for the loss of Â£1m worth of illicit cigarettes. He was driven to the Liverpool area and brutally attacked.

Tobiasz Kozlowski, of Kirby, Merseyside, and Neil Jones, 48, of no fixed address, were found guilty of murder following the death of the 45-year-old who was kidnapped, falsely imprisoned, tortured and set on fire.

Two more men, Kevin Wooden, of Banbury, Oxfordshire, and Kye Arthur, from Bristol, were cleared of murder but found guilty of manslaughter.

All four men will be sentenced on 9 October.

Samel, also a member of an organised crime group, was kidnapped from his Handsworth home by Wooden, 46, of Alma Road, and Arthur, 35, of Copley Gardens, and a third male. They had posed as Interpol officers executing a European arrest warrant.

He died from his injuries in hospital about three months later.

Opening the case earlier prosecutor Harpreet Sandhu KC told the court after he was kidnapped, Samel was "falsely imprisoned, he was placed in a white Peugeot Boxer van and he was driven to Merseyside."

It is there where he was tortured and he seriously harmed.

"As part of that torture his body was set on fire.

He was believed to have been naked and in a seated position when he was set alight, the court heard.

"After he was subjected to that torture, his body is likely to have been dumped in a remote rural location.

"Miraculously he was able to walk to the home of strangers who saw the state he was in and who called for an ambulance."

Samel was given water after knocking at the door of the property near Bickerstaffe.

He was taken to Whiston Hospital in Prescot but died on June 21 as a result of his injuries.

News.title: Scotland's public spending deficit falls as tax take rises
News.content:
Scotland's public spending deficit fell by Â£600m last year to Â£25.3bn after an increase in the amount raised in taxes, figures show.

The annual Government Expenditure and Revenue Scotland (Gers) report compares the tax raised in Scotland with public spending for and on behalf of Scotland.

It said that revenue had grown by Â£6.3bn to Â£98.3bn, an increase of 6.9%, while there was a slower growth in expenditure, which rose by Â£5.7bn to Â£123.6bn - an increase of 4.8%.

The largest increases in revenue came from national insurance contributions, which were up by Â£2.4bn, and income tax receipts, up by Â£1.5bn.

The expenditure of Â£123.6bn is the amount spent by the Scottish, UK and local governments north of the border - as well as a share of spending on shared provision such as defence and debt.

News.title: 102-year-old man in critical condition after alleged pub assault
News.content:
A 102-year-old man is in a critical condition after allegedly being assaulted at a pub.

Emergency services were called to The Crow's Nest pub in Cwmbran, Torfaen, at about 22:25 BST on 1 August, and the man was taken to hospital.

A 56-year-old man from Llanelli, Carmarthenshire, was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm, and has since been released under investigation.

Gwent Police is appealing for witnesses and want to speak to anyone who was in the pub between 22:00 and 23:00 on the night of the incident.

News.title: Six arrested on suspicion of abducting girls
News.content:
Six people have been arrested on suspicion of abducting two girls after they disappeared from a town in Warwickshire.

Police said three men and three women had been arrested and remained in custody after the girls went missing from Rugby and were found in Cornwall on Tuesday.

Two men, 62 and 25, and a 56-year-old woman from Tintagel, Cornwall, were arrested earlier along with two women, 75 and 47, from Rugby and a 42-year-old man from Falmouth.

The girls, aged 11 and 12, had last been seen in the Newbold area of Rugby during the early hours on Sunday before they were found on Tuesday, Warwickshire Police said.

Police said the girls had previously lived in Cornwall and were investigating how they managed to travel more than 200 miles.

They were found "safe and well" by Devon and Cornwall officers after carrying out house-to-house inquiries and the police helicopter.

"The people who are currently in custody are all known to the girls so there was and is no wider threat to the community," Det Ch Supt Jon Belcher said.

Detectives will carry out house-to-house inquiries in Rugby with an increased presence in the area over the next few days.

News.title: PM admits cost of living help is not enough and hints at further support
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he accepts his announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.

Burnham told BBC's Wake up to Money he will deliver an "accumulation of smaller things" that "combine to take the pressure down" on household budgets.

He spoke of an overhaul of train fares and "more public control" of energy, water and housing but did not give details on how he would bring this about.

Burnham has made a number of announcements to help people with the cost of living since taking office, including the removal of VAT from domestic electricity bills and bringing forward an already planned end to 'subscription traps'.

Asked whether the changes he had announced were not significant to people struggling, he said: "I can accept criticism that this isn't enough, because I wouldn't say it's enough.

"But I take an approach to politics where I do what I can, when I can. Just take that little bit of pressure off and address an issue that you know needs addressing.

"It's not the end of the story," he added.

The prime minister, who is embarking on a tour of the UK while Parliament is in recess, said he believed "more public control of essential services" such as water, energy and housing, "would mean we could get to a more substantial answer to the cost of living crisis".

On water, he said it would not be easy to reverse the privatisation of water companies in England and Wales that took place in the 1980s.

"But very much, I'm looking at what can be done. Same with energy."

He also said that, following the return of rail operators to public ownership, he wanted to "remodel the rail fares so that we can get more public benefit for people".

It comes as the government said on Wednesday that people living within 1,600ft (500m) of new upgraded electricity pylons and substations across Britain will receive a Â£250 annual discount on their bills for a decade.

President Donald Trump’s ongoing makeover of the White House and its grounds could ultimately cost more than $900 million, with much of the funding coming from taxpayers, according to a report.

Citing contracts and planning documents, The Washington Post said the administration is preparing to spend a great deal more than the $600 million previously outlined for the construction of the president’s new ballroom in place of the East Wing, which was abruptly demolished last year.

Work is also either planned or ongoing to make improvements to nearby Lafayette Square and to build a new helipad and visitor screening center, all of which could take the cost to $927 million, the records seen by The Post indicate.

However, rather than ask Congress for the funding for Trump’s “modernization” agenda, the administration is reportedly shifting money from federal agencies and private donors into the Executive Residence, a small office responsible for the upkeep of the president’s private home.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump’s White House ‘modernization’ agenda could prove much more expensive than previously thought ( AFP/Getty )

According to public budget records cited by the Post, the administration has directed $875 million to the residence’s account since Trump returned to office in January 2025.

Approximately $500 million of that total came via transfers from the Secret Service and White House Military Office, $305 million from philanthropists and another $70 million from an unidentified source.

Doing so is entirely within the rules – although experts cited by the newspaper agreed the amount money involved was “incredibly unusual”. The office in question is exempt from the transparency rules that apply to other agencies, keeping any contracts it awards confidential.

Responding, White House spokesman Davis Ingle told The Independent in a statement: “President Trump continues to implement long-overdue and necessary renovations to beautify the People’s House as we celebrate our great nation’s 250th anniversary of independence.

“Thanks to the Builder-in-Chief, the White House will be properly glorified and remain in excellent condition for generations to come.

open image in gallery Construction of Trump’s new helipad underway on the South Lawn ( Getty )

“Recent events such as the foiled attack on the historic UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House proves exactly why the East Wing Modernization Project is severely needed for large scale events, which include drone proof structures and drone ports among other critical security enhancements,” Ingle added.

Trump’s ballroom was hit with a fresh setback last week when two judges on the D.C. Court of Appeals ruled that the president must halt above-ground construction until he has secured Congress’s approval for the project.

“Each president is a temporary tenant, not the owner, of the White House and its Executive Residence,” the judges wrote.

“We are aware of no instance in American history in which a president unilaterally and using privately collected funds demolished substantial portions of the White House that Congress authorized to be built and American taxpayers paid for. Until now.”

Both Franklin D Roosevelt and Harry Truman did make extensive repairs to the White House but went to Capitol Hill to secure their funding, as did Barack Obama more recently.

The number of pensioners set to pay tax on their savings will exceed two million for the first time according to new figures, more than quadrupling over the last four years.

Data released by HMRC shows that the number of people aged 65 and older who must pay tax on interest accrued on their savings is forecast to rise from 517,000 in 2022/23 to 2.1 million in 2026/27.

The 300 per cent rise has been blamed on the government’s decision to maintain frozen income tax thresholds, alongside higher savings returns arising from increased interest rates.

Andrew Wright, head of savings at Paragon Bank, which obtained the figures, said: “The personal savings allowance has remained unchanged, so more people are being pulled into the tax net as their incomes and savings interest rise.

“Higher interest rates have been positive for savers, helping them earn more on their money, but they have also increased the likelihood of breaching the allowance,” he told The Telegraph.

open image in gallery The number of pensioners set to pay tax on their savings has exceed two million for the first time according to new figure ( Getty/iStock )

Under current rules, income tax is due on earnings above the personal allowance of £12,570. An exception is applied to Isas, which have a tax-free allowance on up to £20,000 a year.

Basic-rate taxpayers can also keep an additional £1,000 in savings interest from HMRC each year, dropping to £500 for higher-rate taxpayers. There is no savings interest allowance for additional-rate taxpayers.

These savings thresholds remain frozen alongside the main income tax rates.

It means a pensioner holding £30,000 in savings at an interest rate of 4.5 per cent a year, £1,350 would breach the allowance by £350.

This amount would be added to their other income sources – mainly the state pension and any private pensions – to determine how much they should be taxed on overall.

open image in gallery At 2.1 million, over 65s are forecast to make up nearly half (47 per cent) of all individuals liable to save tax on their savings in 2026/27 ( Getty/iStock )

At 2.1 million, over 65s are forecast to make up nearly half (47 per cent) of all individuals liable to save tax on their savings. This is forecast to be worth more than £3.34bn to government coffers in 2026/27, the HMRC data release shows, up from £795 million four years ago.

Mr Wright said that older savers can make the most of government allowances to lower their tax liability within the rules.

He advises: “With savings often providing vital financial security later in life, it is important to regularly review where your money is held. Making full use of your Isa allowance can help protect more of your hard-earned interest from tax and those aged 65+ have the benefit of retaining the full £20,000 cash Isa allowance from next tax year.”

Changes to the Isa system were announced by former chancellor Rachel Reeves at last years’ Budget, reducing the allowance for Cash Isas to £12,000 for all savers under 65. The total allowance remains £20,000 for all individuals, which can also be spread to a Stocks and Shares Isa.

An HM Treasury spokesperson said: “Anyone whose only income is the full new or basic State Pension without any increments will not pay income tax and we are committed to that over this Parliament.

“By keeping the Triple Lock, 12 million pensioners will see their income rise by up to £470 this year, and they continue to benefit from the highest Personal Allowance in the G7.”

Inflation in the United States slowed last month alongside a cooling in underlying price pressures, indicating that elevated oil and gas costs driven by the Iran war have had a limited effect on wider economic prices so far.

According to Labor Department data released Wednesday, consumer prices grew 3.4% year-over-year in July, representing a minor decrease from June's 3.5% rate. Inflation remains above its pre-war level of 2.4% recorded in February. Month-over-month, prices edged up by only 0.1% between June and July.

This subtle reduction may relieve some pressure on inflation-fighters at the Federal Reserve to implement further hikes to their key interest rate. However, cost increases continue to outpace average wage growth, maintaining financial pressure on American households managing higher bills for groceries, fuel, and healthcare—trends that have taken on a high profile in the fast-approaching midterm elections.

Stripping out volatile food and energy costs, core inflation slipped to an annual rate of 2.5% in July, down from 2.6% in June. July's figure matches a post-pandemic low previously reached in January and February, prior to the start of the Iran war.

On Wednesday, gas averaged $4.04 a gallon nationwide, a 16-cent rise from a month ago, according to the motor club AAA ( Getty Images )

On a monthly basis, core prices increased by 0.2% from June to July. Sustained monthly gains around this 0.2% threshold would be low enough over time to bring overall inflation closer to the central bank's 2% annual goal.

Even so, oil prices remain elevated and gasoline costs rose in late July and August, suggesting overall inflation could accelerate next month. On Wednesday, gas averaged $4.04 a gallon nationwide, a 16-cent rise from a month ago, according to the motor club AAA.

Inflation has been pushed higher by a series of shocks to the economy, including tariffs imposed last spring by President Donald Trump, rising gas prices stemming from the Iran war, and a surge in investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure that has boosted computer chip prices. The key question for central bank policymakers and consumers struggling with high gas and grocery prices is how quickly those one-time effects will fade or whether they will lead to persistently rising prices.

Wednesday’s figures could bolster officials at the Federal Reserve who believe the central bank can leave its key rate on hold at about 3.6% while inflation steadily declines on its own as those temporary factors fade.

Overall, price increases have stayed above the Fed's 2% target for more than five years, suggesting that more than temporary factors may be at work. The cost of services such as healthcare, restaurant meals, and car maintenance are on average rising at more than 3% annually, and they aren't particularly sensitive to gas prices or AI investment.

Rising costs for services often reflect higher wages, as companies charge more to offset the cost of higher pay. But incomes aren't growing fast enough to sustain inflation, economists note.

It's a confounding situation that has left many economists — and Fed officials — seeking more information to determine where inflation is headed.

"You've got all these things that are just not the way the economy used to behave," Diane Swonk, chief economist at KPMG, said.

For many consumers, years of sharply rising grocery prices have led them to adopt a wide range of coping strategies, from comparison shopping, to couponing, to cutting back on favorite foods.

Some retailers, such as Walmart, have responded by rolling back food prices, a trend that could have lowered July's inflation figures. Yet many other firms are still passing on higher costs.

Paint company Sherwin-Williams is planning an 8% price increase effective Sept. 1 to offset higher raw material costs, CEO Heidi Petz told analysts late last month. She said that because of the company’s strong relationships with suppliers, it was able to delay price increases until now.

"We are seeing the impact of higher oil and related cost pressures, and we expect continued volatility throughout the balance of the year," she said.

Wednesday's report comes as the Federal Reserve is sharply divided over whether it should hike its key interest rate to combat inflation. The Fed kept its rate unchanged, at about 3.6%, at a meeting late last month. But the vote was 9-3, with three dissenters favoring a rate hike.

And at a July 29 news conference explaining the decision, chair Kevin Warsh was vague about the Fed's next steps, in keeping with his focus on reining in the central bank's previous willingness to signal whether it was prepared to raise or cut borrowing costs.

"If inflation continues to be elevated ... interest rates could well be part of that solution," he said. "But I wouldn't say it's in isolation."

Long-term interest rates rose after Warsh's comments, suggesting investors worried that inflation could worsen in the coming months and the Fed might not lift borrowing costs to fight rising prices.

Complicating matters, the government said last week that employers had cut jobs in July, a sign of potential economic weakness. The Fed typically avoids rate hikes when hiring is faltering, because higher borrowing costs could slow the economy further.

Joe Root has confirmed there will be no curfew in place during his second spell as England Test captain.

A new era of English cricket will begin at Headingley next Wednesday when Root leads the team against Pakistan in the first Test match since Ben Stokes retired from international cricket and Brendon McCullum lost his job as red-ball head coach.

The main controversy at the end of the ‘Bazball’ tenure was an incident in June at London nightclub Rex Rooms, where Stokes and Gus Atkinson were out past a midnight curfew put in place by England men’s managing director Rob Key, which occurred after Harry Brook was fined for an altercation with a bouncer in New Zealand last November.

During an interview on this week’s Sky Sports Cricket Podcast with Michael Atherton, Root said: “There’s not going to be a curfew. I don’t think this needs to be a big deal, to be honest.

open image in gallery Joe Root says curfews don’t work (Steven Paston/PA) ( PA Wire )

“My view on curfews is I don’t think they work, and if you want guys to take responsibility on the field they’ve got to be able to feel they can be grown adults off it and make good strong decisions off it.

“That’s for us as a team to manage well, and self-police well, for me and ‘Flem’ (Stephen Fleming) to manage well in many ways but ultimately you’re grown adults, you know what it takes to play for England, you know what your responsibilities are off the field and we need to make sure we don’t find ourselves with any little situations off the field.

“We should be known for how we play our cricket and what we do on the field, we should be on the back pages of the newspapers and people reading about that sort of stuff.

“Be adults, look after yourselves, look after each other, create a good strong culture when you know when the right time is to celebrate and enjoy a win or to have a sensible beer or whatever, but remember you’re playing for England.”

open image in gallery England’s former red-ball head coach Brendon McCullum with ex-captain Ben Stokes (Robbie Stephenson/PA) ( PA Archive )

Meanwhile, England opener Emilio Gay will get the chance to prove his fitness in a warm-up fixture against Pakistan this week.

Gay made his Test debut earlier in the summer and was primed to open in the upcoming three-match series with Pakistan until he suffered a shoulder injury for Durham in the Metro Bank One-Day Cup against Middlesex on Thursday.

The right shoulder issue will be tested by Gay this week after he was included in a 14-player squad for the Professional County Club Select XI match against Pakistan, which is a three-day fixture.

The warm-up match in Beckenham will begin on Thursday and England spinner Shoaib Bashir is set to be involved.

open image in gallery Emilio Gay suffered an injury scare on Friday, retiring hurt with a shoulder injury while batting for Durham (Joe Giddens/PA) ( PA Wire )

It will represent the final chance for Bashir to impress before England’s new era begins at Headingley on August 19, with Marcus Trescothick in interim charge before Stephen Fleming takes over this winter.

It was announced last week that Dan Lawrence will bat at six in the first Test and the part-time off-breaks of the Surrey all-rounder may result in Bashir running drinks in Leeds.

James Rew and Matt Fisher, who both featured in a much-changed England line-up in the second Test of the New Zealand series at Kia Oval, will also be involved for the PCC Select XI.

Sussex batter Tom Haines will captain the team and 17-year-old Manny Lumsden of Hampshire is part of the squad.

PCC Select XI squad: T Haines (captain), S Bashir, L Benkenstein, C Falconer, M Fisher, E Gay, N Gilchrist, J Hull, M Lumsden, J Rew, J Sales, C Tear, N Thain & S Zaib.

President Donald Trump seems to have finally given up on his pipe dream of serving an illegal third term as president.

The 80-year-old president has repeatedly suggested he would run again in 2028 — even though the 22nd Amendment to the U.S. Constitution places a clear limit on the number of terms one can serve as president. However, when asked by a reporter Tuesday night at Joint Base Andrews if he was “serious” about seeking a third term, Trump seemed to waver.

“Everybody asks me that question,” he began. “And you know that the law is very strong on that. I’d love to run, but the law is very strong.”

Trump continued: “I get asked by everyone. Even tonight, they’re screaming at the event, ‘2028!’ No, everybody wants me to do it, but the law is very strong.”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump told reporters Tuesday that while he’d love to run for a third term as president, the law prohibiting it ‘is very strong’ ( AFP/Getty )

The reporter tried to press the president, asking, “Is that a no?” but Trump had already moved on to the next question.

The president was at Joint Base Andrews Tuesday night after he returned from attending a Patriots Game in Ohio.

Trump has repeatedly flirted with the idea of running for a third term, all while ignoring the fact that the Constitution does not allow it.

In July, during the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner, Trump told reporters he “won three times” and was “gonna do it again,” before putting a red “Trump 2028” baseball hat on his head.

“I’m pleased to announce my intention to, and this is somewhat of a scoop, my intention to run for a fourth term as president of the United States,” Trump said during his remarks at the dinner.

open image in gallery Trump was at Joint Base Andrews Tuesday night while returning from a Patriots game in Ohio ( Getty )

“I will be doing that; I will be making it official. I won three times; now I’m gonna do it again,” he added.

Trump has floated the idea countless times, including during his State of the Union address earlier this year.

“First year of the second term…it should be my third term,” he said, insinuating without evidence that the 2020 election, which he lost to former President Joe Biden, was “stolen” from him.

It all started with an innocent WhatsApp message.

“Has anyone got any spare eclipse glasses? I left it too late and can’t seem to find any!”

Little did I know it but this benign missive, sent to my local community choir group on Monday morning by a nice woman called Sarah, was the unwitting catalyst for what would quickly become a deranged, Race Across the World-style quest to secure a pair for myself. My own personal odyssey, if we want to be culturally relevant.

Within minutes of her original plea, there were multiple replies. “The print shop have got some, I think – heading there ASAP!!!”

“Try the newsagents on Bouverie Road, I got some from there yesterday but they were limited to five pairs per person?”

“This link looks good – currently saying will deliver before Wednesday [prayer hands emoji].”

I’ll be honest – while I’d heard some chatter about the solar eclipse happening on 12 August, prior to this stream of “hot tips” and warm leads I had given it almost zero thought. But the funny thing is, as more messages came pinging in – “sold out online!”; “print shop has run out!”; “newsagent out of stock!” – I suddenly wanted, more than anything else in this solar system, to get my mitts on a pair. The scarcity mindset had officially set in. I struggled to focus on anything else for the rest of the day.

“They’re being stupid – it must be possible to buy them on the internet,” I thought, scornfully. “You can buy anything on the internet. That’s why it’s killing off independent businesses so effectively!”

But, of course, my lovely choirmates weren’t stupid at all. The idiot was me – blithely assuming I’d be able to casually buy a pair two days before the UK’s most complete eclipse event in 27 years.

open image in gallery Persistence pays off: Solar eclipse glasses secured at Old Spitalfields Market ( Helen Coffey/The Independent )

The more I looked online, the more panicked I became. Every single purveyor was either out of stock or advertising a delivery date of Friday 14 August at the earliest, two days after the fact. Yes, even on Amazon Prime. Getting hold of a simple strip of cardboard with black plastic lenses that would ensure I could safely look upon a burning orb 93 million miles away was proving not just tricky but nigh-on impossible.

Still, this was all currently playing out in my humble hometown in Kent. Heading into London to go to the office, I reasoned things would be different there. The Big Smoke, the economic hub of this great nation, would surely be selling specs on every corner.

Alas, the situation in Folkestone was indicative of what was unfolding across the country. A cursory Google search showed that the market in London was just as much shaped by supply < demand and, consequently, the only viable strategy was to comb through a random assortment of Reddit threads and Facebook posts like a detective on the trail of the Zodiac Killer.

Jessops were said to be selling pairs, but whether or not there would be any by the time one arrived was unclear. Greenwich Observatory seemed to be the safest bet, but they warned of limited stocks (and, quite honestly, it was a mission from the City).

open image in gallery Solar Eclipse London is doing strategic ‘drops’ of glasses across London ( Helen Coffey )

There were whispers of some being sold under the counter at a specific bakery by Bond Street tube station, rumours of a single convenience store near Aldgate East that had a fresh batch. Booze and Essential Putney “had 90 pairs this morning”; Snax Wimbledon “just got 300 pairs, apparently”. There was a 2am queue in Whitechapel of insomniac stargazers desperate to get some.

It was while picking through the comments underneath a post from “Muswell Hill Group and Friends” on Facebook in response to the news that Fresh Bakery in Finsbury Park had been flogging them that I realised I had accidentally become part of something – a new tribe of people driven slightly insane by a dearth of resource. “Anybody know if it is open now and if they have two pairs in stock??” wrote one anxious soul. “Driving all the way from Muswell Hill.”

And it was while dissecting a separate social media thread based on the keywords “solar eclipse glasses”, “where”, “buy”, “TODAY, FOR THE LOVE OF GOD” that I happened upon my best, most tangible lead yet: an underground WhatsApp group called Solar Eclipse London.

That’s where things truly got weird. This mysterious enterprise, whose WhatsApp community had only sprung into being on Sunday, seemed to have “ISO 12312-2 certified” eclipse inventory up the wazoo and was deploying it strategically across London. Different locations at different times; limited “drops”, with hype built by trailing cryptic clues about the next ballpark area without details of the exact whereabouts.

I realised I had accidentally become part of something – a new tribe of people driven slightly insane by a dearth of resource

“Finsbury Park, we’re coming soon.”

“We have a big surprise for everyone. There is a location with over 2,000 waiting for you all. Will reveal at 2.30pm.”

“Hint being sent below”, with a picture of the glasses against a backdrop of Big Ben.

And, my personal favourite, “The location rhymes with Chutney??”

The marketing was flawless, as was the entrepreneurial nous; within the space of a few hours, the WhatsApp community had grown from under a thousand-strong to over 7,000 (and by the end of the day it had hit 9,000). And then they hinted Liverpool Street was the next station for a forthcoming “shipment”, which just so happened to be around the corner from my office (#blessed). The exact location, however, would be shared on their Instagram – with instructions to “FOLLOW AND LIKE!”, another excellent marketing ploy for engagement – and pairs would be limited to two per person. Each one would cost £5, cash only. Oh, it was on.

I grabbed two colleagues to ensure we could obtain the requisite number of pairs and headed out into the unknown, refreshing the Insta account every 10 seconds like a woman possessed. Finally, aha! “Old Spitalfields Market”. Still vaguely imprecise, but enough to go on.

open image in gallery See ‘em and weep: solar eclipse glasses have sold out across the UK ( AFP/Getty )

The nearer we got, the more suspicious we felt. Was this all a weird prank? Was someone going to jump out and shout “Punked!” in our faces, like a Noughties Ashton Kutcher, as we stumbled around the precinct?

But any reticence disappeared once we spotted that most British of spectacles: a queue. And not just any queue. This one was long, winding, and stretching into the distance as far as the eye could see. Word had obviously spread quickly and, within minutes, the line had grown so long I could no longer see the end of it.

No point wondering how the heck hundreds of people had arrived before us – witchcraft seemed to be the only plausible explanation – we were in it now.

“This is the second location I’ve tried today,” shared the man directly behind us in the queue, with a mildly manic, desperate air. “Finsbury Park sold out this morning – I’ve just been waiting around for the next drop!”

I briefly wondered whether, if I managed to obtain some and he didn’t, I’d be altruistic enough to give up mine to this more deserving soul. No, came the disconcertingly cold answer from deep within. You snooze, you lose.

This is the second location I’ve tried today – I’ve just been waiting around for the next drop! A desperate man in search of eclipse glasses

Still, there was a conviviality about the whole thing – a curiously carnivalesque spirit. People in the queue caught eyes and smiled shyly, or exchanged tales of their previous attempts to obtain a pair by trekking the width and breadth of London based on little more than hope and hearsay. Perhaps it was being drawn together around the same wholesome event, but a similar feel to that of the World Cup prevailed among these stressed yet jubilant Londoners: we were experiencing another common cause to unite us in these increasingly divided times.

We shuffled forward excruciatingly slowly, every passing minute cranking up the tension another unbearable notch. Unlike some of the other WhatsApp updates, this one had failed to include the number of spectacles on offer. There could be 30, or 300, or 3,000; there was no way of knowing.

After 20 minutes of inching along, we could finally see the front of the line. This, I knew, would be the exact moment they ran out of stock – when we were in first spitting, then touching, distance. The universe’s sick sense of humour all but guaranteed it. We were eight people from the front now. Five. Three. But, wait… They weren’t going to run out! The universe was on our side!

As we arrived at the kiosk, handed over our crisp, £10 notes, joyfully took our strips of cardboard gold and punched the air in triumph, I felt what can only be described as a shot of pure exhilaration.

Sure, it was more work than clicking “next day delivery” on Amazon – but a victory earned through the thrill of the hunt? That tastes all the sweeter.

News.title: How to safely view the UK solar eclipse with just two pieces of card
News.content:
