Most people underestimate how much light a pair of sunglasses blocks out. A typical dark pair removes around 80 to 90% of the visible light reaching the eye.

Safely looking directly at the Sun requires reducing the light reaching the eye by a factor of around 100,000, meaning roughly 99.999% must be removed. Ordinary sunglasses can let around 10,000 times too much visible light through.

That is especially important on Wednesday 12 August, when the Moon will pass in front of the Sun, creating a deep partial solar eclipse across the UK. Timings and the amount of the Sun covered will vary by location. In Bristol, the eclipse begins at about 6.17pm and reaches its maximum at around 7.12pm. Viewers in Cornwall will see roughly 95% of the Sun covered.

Sunlight can injure the eye without causing pain or any obvious warning at the time. Solar retinopathy occurs when intense light damages the retina, the light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye. Symptoms can appear several hours after exposure and include blurred or distorted vision or a dark patch in the centre of your sight. Many people recover over the following weeks or months, but some can be left with lasting changes to their vision.

open image in gallery The safest way to look directly at the eclipse is with proper solar-viewing glasses or a handheld solar viewer that meets ISO 12312-2, ( AFP/Getty )

The safest way to look directly at the eclipse is with proper solar-viewing glasses or a handheld solar viewer that meets ISO 12312-2, the international safety standard for filters designed for looking directly at the Sun. Ordinary sunglasses are covered by different safety standards and are not designed for direct viewing of the Sun.

Solar viewers are thousands of times darker and use filters designed to reduce visible, ultraviolet and infrared radiation to safe levels.

An ISO number printed on the glasses is not, by itself, proof that a pair is safe, because counterfeit products are sold online. Buy from a reputable supplier whose products have been properly tested, and inspect the filter before use. Do not use glasses with scratches, tears or other damage. If you can see ordinary objects through them indoors, do not use them.

About the author Panos Maghsoudlou, NIHR Academic Clinical Lecturer in Ophthalmology, School of Cellular and Molecular Medicine, University of Bristol. This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

Put eclipse glasses on before looking towards the Sun and remove them only after turning away. Children should be supervised throughout, particularly if adult-sized frames do not fit securely.

Never look at the Sun through binoculars, telescopes or camera lenses while wearing eclipse glasses. These instruments concentrate sunlight and can damage both the filter and the eye. Any optical equipment used to view the Sun needs a proper solar filter securely fitted over the front of the instrument.

Colander cameras

If you are reading this on the day of the eclipse and local shops have sold out of eclipse glasses, what do you do? Reach for the colander.

A colander does not filter sunlight. Its holes act as tiny pinhole cameras, projecting small images of the Sun onto another surface. Stand with your back to the Sun, hold the colander so its shadow falls onto a sheet of white paper or pale ground, and look at the projected spots of light. During the eclipse, those usually round spots will become tiny crescents. Never look through the holes towards the Sun.

open image in gallery Illustration of camera obscura in Gemma Frisius’ 1545 book De Radio Astronomica et Geometrica ( Leonardo da Vinci, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons )

The method is remarkably old. More than 2,000 years ago, an ancient Greek text traditionally associated with Aristotle described how an eclipse viewed through leaves, a sieve or gaps between the fingers produced crescent-shaped patches of light. Centuries later, the 11th-century mathematician and pioneer of optics Ibn al-Haytham investigated how the image of an eclipse formed when sunlight passed through a small opening into a darkened space. And in 1545, astronomer Gemma Frisius published an illustration showing a solar eclipse being observed using the same camera obscura principle.

If you don’t have a colander, though, a simple eclipse viewer can be made from two pieces of card. Make a small hole in one piece, stand with your back to the Sun and let the sunlight pass through the hole onto the second piece. You will see a tiny image of the Sun, which will become a crescent as the Moon moves across it.

The principle is always the same: keep your back to the Sun and look at the projected image rather than directly at the Sun.

So enjoy the eclipse, but watch it safely. The British Isles will not see an eclipse this close to totality again until September 2081, and the next total solar eclipse visible from the UK will not arrive until 2090. It is a rare sight, and one worth seeing without putting your vision at risk.

News.title: Wisconsin beats back socialist surge with defeat of Hong for governor — who lacked support from Bernie and AOC

The Democratic primary for governor in Wisconsin ended in the narrowest of victories for David Crowley, the Milwaukee county executive, on Wednesday as far-left progressive Francesca Hong came up short.

Her defeat was a sour pill for the newly energized left wing of the Democratic Party, but one that followed a smashing victory by Wisconsin Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan over the far more centrist Rep. Angie Craig in the state’s race for U.S. Senate, giving progressives their second victory in a Senate contest in a week.

Neither wing of the Democratic Party will come away from Minnesota’s race feeling anything close to dominant. Crowley appeared on track to best Hong by just over 3,000 votes, less than half a percent dividing the two. With 95% of the vote counted Crowley had 313,321 votes to Hong’s 310,110 as of Wednesday morning.

Centrists will breathe a sigh of relief knowing that the party’s general election candidate for the Minnesota gubernatorial race this fall won’t be directly saddled with the political baggage of a self-imposed “socialist” label or the comparatively fringe positions on policing and other issues held by the Democratic Socialists of America, of which Hong is a member. Republicans are still aiming to paint all Democrats as socialists, but Crowley’s defeat of Hong will make that label harder to stick with many voters.

But at the same time, the strength of Hong’s campaign can’t be ignored, especially given her near-total lack of national support outside of endorsements from two far-left House members, Ro Khanna and Ilhan Omar.

open image in gallery Francesca Hong led comfortably in polling leading into Tuesday but ultimately fell short ( Getty )

open image in gallery David Crowley won a narrow victory after previously dropping out of the race ( AP )

Neither have the same kind of pull as Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) or Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY), both of whom declined to endorse in the race. Sanders did not endorse gubernatorial candidates this cycle, while Ocasio-Cortez has played a selective game with her own endorsements as she charts her own potential future ambitions.

Tuesday’s results were especially disappointing for the DSA and many progressives in large part due to the polling suggesting that Hong was running away with the vote beforehand.

Supporters of the assemblywoman were excited heading into Tuesday, only to see Crowley (who’d only resumed his suspended campaign weeks earlier) quickly reaching his required benchmarks as Hong failed to take the lead.

open image in gallery Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez both campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan but declined to wade in to the Wisconsin contest ( Getty )

It wasn’t just the two most prominent progressives in American politics who left Hong’s campaign on read. Playbook reported that ahead of Tuesday’s primary, none of the rising progressive stars who descended on Michigan to support Abdul El-Sayed traveled further west to help Hong cross the finish line, with the exception of Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who focused his national, mostly male audience of younger progressives on Hong’s campaign in the final weeks.

His presence may have energized the left, but also conceivably could have contributed to the image of the candidate as a left-wing firebrand.

Hong’s success and failure can both be linked in part to the DSA brand. Concerns about the label and her electability clearly played into the ability of Crowley, who’d previously dropped out of the race, to martial such support for his bid in such a short time after Hong’s closest rival, Mandela Barnes, dropped out.

Her struggle to explain a past comment dissing Thanksgiving as a “colonizer” holiday that gained national media attention only accelerated the pace of questions about her electability in a purple state.

DSA volunteers were crucial to the success she did have, however, and her coming within inches of the nomination speak to the ability of candidates like Hong to remain truly competitive even when abandoned by the growing progressive coalition in Washington.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register, or login to an existing, telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.

When you see a + in the tracker it indicates how many other games start at that time.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, one exception is this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football will launch in the two weeks leading up to the start of the Premier League. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games.



What counts as a Save?

A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

Sports.title: Leicester takeover update with former Premier League champions up for sale for just more than cost of Alexander Isak
Sports.content:
A BROCHURE on the valuation of Leicester City has reportedly been sent to potential investors.

The Srivaddhanaprabha family, who own the club, are said to be looking for £222m for the entire portfolio, but a deal could be closer to £148m.

As reported by The Athletic, Global investment bank Citigroup has drafted the brochure.



It is titled Project Lineup and delves into Leicester’s assets, including its women’s team, academy, King Power Stadium and the £100million Seagrave training base they moved to five years ago.



Belgian sister club OH Leuven is also featured in the list of assets available.

The club’s recent drop into League One and woeful recent losses are the reason the deal could be nearer £148m.

It is mind-boggling to think that Aleksandar Isak cost just less than this figure, as he completed a £130million record British transfer to Liverpool.



The late Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha bought Leicester for £39m in 2010, cleared their debts and saw the club win promotion to the top flight four years later.

Winning the Premier League against the odds in 2015-16 was one of the greatest sporting stories of all time.

But over the last four accounting reports since 2021, Leicester have recorded losses of £92.5m, £89.7m, £19.4m.

Most recently the club has racked up losses of £71.1m as they slipped from the top eight of the Premier League to suffer three relegations in the last four years.



In February, Leicester were also docked six points by the English Football League for breaching financial rules.

It came after they were charged by the Premier League in May for a profit and sustainability (PSR) breach in the three years up to 2023-24.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Despite the club’s recent turmoil, they are expect to attract a number of potential suitors.

The club has a string of assets, which also include the Belvoir Drive training ground now used by the women’s team.

There is also the land the club acquired for £11.6m outside King Power Stadium that was earmarked for development as part of a stadium expansion plan.



The plans were shelved after Leicester’s relegation from the Premier League at the end of the 2022-23 season.

The property portfolio is valued at £204m, as of 2025, broken down into the stadium’s £74m valuation, Seagrave at £121m and Belvoir Drive at £9m.

Sports.title: Man Utd given major injury boost as Lisandro Martinez returns but trio expected to miss Leeds clash tonight
Sports.content:
LISANDRO MARTINEZ trained with Manchester United on his first full day of pre-season with the club.

Martinez was the final World Cup participant to arrive at their training camp at Carton House in County Kildare after Argentina reached the final.



The 28-year-old was forced off in the first half in the New York finale against Spain with an apparent thigh injury but it was not serious.

SunSport revealed that Martinez was expected to be fit for the start of the season and he reported for United duty in Ireland on Monday night.



Martinez, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo are unlikely to be involved against Leeds United at Croke Park tonight as they have only had a handful of training sessions.

But the trio are likely to get at least half-an-hour against Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Wroclaw on Saturday.



It remains to be seen whether United coach Michael Carrick will put Martinez into the starting XI for their Premier League opener at Hull City on August 22.

Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven have started in all four of United’s pre-season matches but Heaven was culpable for Paris Saint-Germain’s opening goal on Saturday.

Heaven was replaced by Leny Yoro at half-time as Carrick effectively started an audition process for the young centre backs to partner Maguire at Hull.

Yoro had started the first three friendlies at right back as Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui were still away following their World Cup exploits.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Mason Mount did not feature in United’s first two sessions in Ireland after he sustained a foot injury in the 1-1 draw with PSG.

Mount came off after 20 minutes in Gothenburg but jogged to the sidelines and was walking freely after the game.

Multiple sources say Mount is fine but United are managing his recovery carefully given his injury history.

Mount, 27, has played 72 games for United in three years, averaging only 24 appearances per season.

The former Chelsea player has sustained ten separate injuries that have caused him to miss matches since he signed for United for £60million in 2023.

Sports.title: Top-flight European club risk home games being postponed due to FUNGUS leaving pitch ‘practically unplayable’
Sports.content:
CELTA VIGO could be forced to call off their LaLiga season opener – after a FUNGUS has ruined their pitch.

The Spanish side, who handed Altay Bayindir an escape route from Manchester United last week, are scheduled to get their campaign underway with a clash against Osasuna on Sunday.



But the playing surface at the Estadio Abanca Balaidos has been ravaged by a fungus.

Celta Vigo have contacted LaLiga and Osasuna to raise concerns about the condition of the pitch, which has been described as “practically unplayable”.



And with the showdown just a matter of days away, there are fears that there is not enough time to treat the turf.

LaLiga technicians jetted into Vigo this morning to inspect the pitch and decide whether the contest needs to be postponed.

A report is set to be sent to the Spanish top-flight’s chiefs before the final call is made.

But Osasuna do not want their season to be thrown into disarray before it begins.

They are pushing for the encounter to go ahead as planned despite their rivals’ worries.

Celta Vigo are fearing the fungus issue will also cause problems in the coming weeks.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

They are in line to host Athletic Bilbao in another domestic game on August 30.

And their second team, Celta Fortuna, are on course to hold home matches at the Estadio Abanca Balaidos.

Postponing the season opener will result in Bayindir having to wait for his debut.

The Turkish shot-stopper, 28, was allowed to leave United on loan following Karl Darlow’s arrival at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Former Barcelona and Spain wonderkid Ansu Fati lifts lid on amazing MUSIC career and is ‘working on several songs’
Sports.content:
ANSU FATI revealed he is pitch perfect not only in football but in the music studio as he lifted the lid on his passion for singing.

The former Barcelona whizkid was sold permanently to Monaco this summer for £9.3million.



When he is not on a football pitch, he is in the music studio having already released one track called Sea Como Sea on Spotify, YouTube and Apple Music last month.

The song’s name means Whatever It Takes and he has also released an Amapiano version of the track, which has 1.1MILLION views on YouTube.



Fati says he is currently working in the studio and plans to release new music soon.

He said: “Singing is a hobby. I’ve always loved music, and people who know me know it’s something I’ve had since I was a child. But football is my passion, and I can’t compare it to anything,

“I have several songs I’m working on, and the idea is to release them soon.”

Fati has hailed his love for music for hauling him out of some dark periods of his life.

He was once dubbed the next Lionel Messi and handed Barcelona’s iconic number 10 shirt.

But his career was blighted with devastating knee injuries and subsequent surgeries that robbed him of regular game time.

Sports.title: Roberto Martinez ‘in talks to become new Netherlands boss’ despite World Cup failures with Portugal and Belgium
Sports.content:
ROBERTO MARTINEZ has held talks over the vacant Netherlands national team job.

The former Premier League boss, 53, is available after leaving Portugal following their World Cup exit.



Dutch football chiefs are after a new boss as they look to replace Ronald Koeman, who departed after his men lost to Morocco on penalties in the round of 32.

According to De Telegraaf, Dutch technical director Nigel de Jong has spoken to Martinez regarding the role.



Former Manchester City midfielder De Jong is said to have travelled to Malaga to meet with Martinez face-to-face.

Martinez has extensive experience of international football, having managed Belgium for six years before spending the last four with Portugal.

The ex-Everton manager guided Belgium to a third-place finish at the 2018 World Cup, agonisingly losing 1-0 to eventual winners France in the semi-finals.

They also lost to eventual champions Italy at Euro 2020, this time at the quarter-final stage.

Martinez departed the role following a disappointing group stage exit at the Qatar World Cup four years ago.

With Portugal he lost to France on penalties in the quarter-finals at Euro 2024, before a late 1-0 defeat to Spain in the round of 16 at this summer’s World Cup.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The Netherlands are believed to have been turned down by several domestic candidates.

Local reports suggest that the likes of Arne Slot, Erik ten Hag and Peter Bosz do not want the role.

This could lead to Dutch football chiefs turning to a foreign manager for the first time since Ernst Happel in the 1970s.

Confirming that he would not be taking the job, ex-Liverpool chief Slot said: “Over the past few weeks, and particularly the past few days, various reports have appeared regarding the vacancy at the Dutch national team, suggesting that I had withdrawn from the process after lengthy negotiations, including regarding salary and contract duration.



“That speculation is incorrect. We simply never reached that stage of the talks.

“At this stage of my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day. Something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team.”

Last week, former Manchester United boss Louis van Gaal suggested that he could return for a fourth stint as Dutch national team manager.

The 74-year-old has been out of work since stepping down as Netherlands boss following the 2022 World Cup amid a battle with prostate cancer.

Having last year confirmed that he is cancer free, Van Gaal said: “I always want to help the KNVB (Dutch FA), just as I wanted to do at Ajax.



“And with such a squad, there are of course possibilities.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I also think that the Netherlands could potentially still become European or world champions, because 95 per cent of the squad plays abroad and often at good clubs.”

Van Gaal added: “I have already been national coach three times, so if I ever do something as a trainer again, you probably shouldn’t look for it in the Netherlands. Although you never know with me.”

Sports.title: Man Utd name nine academy stars on pro squad list but snub Godwill Kukonki, 18, sparking uncertainty over his future
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED youngster Godwill Kukonki faces an uncertain future after being left off the club’s latest professional squad intake.

The young defender has yet to feature in first-team pre-season prep this summer, leaving his situation at Old Trafford up in the air.



Kukonki, 18, was left off United’s latest pro contract squad list, which featured nine academy players who signed first-year terms.

Albert Mills, Louie Bradbury, Jacob Watson, Neithan Barbosa, Charlie Hardy, Cameron Byrne-Hughes, Jayden Ngwashi, Nathaniel-Junior Brown and Rafe McCormack all sourced new deals.



Well-placed sources said the club are working on the remaining deals separately, but chose to announce the nine finalised agreements together on Wednesday.

Kukonki arguably featured more prominently for the Under-18s last season than most of those listed, with the exception of Mills, Brown and JJ Gabriel.

A new contract has not been ruled out, but Kukonki is on a slightly different timeline as he enters what would currently be a third-year scholar agreement.

While Kukonki’s pre-season plans were disrupted, Michael Carrick has been impressed by fellow centre-back and Under-18 captain Dan Armer, whose stock has risen internally this summer.

SunSport understands that Armer signed a pro deal last Friday, before flying out with Carrick’s squad for the pre-season friendly against Paris Saint-Germain.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



Armer was an unused sub in the 1-1 draw, with Harry Maguire playing a full 90 minutes ahead of the season opener against Hull City next Saturday.

Kukonki has instead taken part in Under-21 training, he did not feature in their match against Altrincham Town on July 31.

Kukonki was included in Michael Carrick‘s squad for the 2-1 defeat at Newcastle in March and was named on the bench on seven occasions by ex-United head coach Ruben Amorim.

Although United offered Kukonki a contract extension in March 2025, the complete lack of mention on the club’s retained list points toward a potential summer exit.

At 6ft 5, Kukonki spent a significant developmental time playing as a left back last season to build his versatility and ball-carrying skills.



Following the arrival of a new scholar class last month, Kukonki is one of the last remaining players from the 2024 intake and he turns 19 next February.

Standard Premier League and FA Youth Scholarship agreements are typically two-year contracts signed at age 16, covering a player’s Under-17 and Under-18 seasons.

However, rules allow clubs to offer or extend scholarships into a third year under specific development circumstances or extended terms.

United are hopeful about 17-year-old Noah Ajayi signing a pro deal, with clubs in Germany interested.

Meanwhile, full back Yuel Helafu was another surprise omission, but he signed his scholar deal a year later than Kukonki and is a year younger.

Sports.title: ‘My body switched off’ – Youri Tielemans ready for gruelling Man Utd season despite worrying World Cup fitness issue
Sports.content:
YOURI TIELEMANS’ body “switched off” at the worst possible moment at the World Cup.

The new Manchester United star’s two goals had capped an improbable Belgium comeback against Senegal in a two-hour epic.



They then steamrollered the United States in the round-of-16 six days later.

But, during the warm-up for the quarter-final with Spain, Tielemans had to withdraw from the starting XI in worrying circumstances.



Looking back on the incident, he said: “We played 120 minutes against Senegal, and from there we had less time in between games.

“So we played the US, and then three days later we played against Spain. In the warm-up, my body just switched off for some reason.”

That did not stop United meeting Tielemans’ £35million Aston Villa release clause just days after the tournament.

And, with Michael Carrick‘s side back in the Champions League this season, there will be another gruelling season in store.

But Tielemans, 29, assures that he 100 per cent fit and ready for the demands of playing for one of the world’s most scrutinised clubs.

Tielemans stresses: “Now, I do not think I am a player that absolutely needs a rest.



“Obviously, there are a lot of games and the manager needs to manage the team, but when I am good, I am good, you know.

“Unfortunately, my body is, when it does not go well, then I will know straight away and I will alert the manager, but it does not happen often.

“It was just that last game, it was just an overload of too many games, too many minutes, and unfortunately my body could not cope with it anymore.”

Tielemans looks anything but fatigued as he breezily enters a meeting room at Carton House in County Kildare.



He is struck by the number of journalists queuing up to shake hands and jokes about remembering everyone’s names.

At the end of the chat, he checks that a colleague is called Steve, before revealing he was merely joking.

Tielemans is clearly relishing the challenge of representing United.

His domestic and European pedigree should benefit his new club in their first season back in Europe.

Tielemans managed the demands of domestic and European duty in all three seasons with Aston Villa, playing in the Europa Conference League, Champions League, and then the Europa League.



He captained Belgium and has winner’s medals from his seven-and-a-half years with Leicester and Villa, hoisting as many trophies as United in that period.

On his maiden appearance for United against Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday, Tielemans was gently on Bruno Fernandes’ case after he wasted his classy through-ball.

A debutant for Anderlecht aged 16, Tielemans has enough miles on the clock to immediately assert himself as one of the United squad’s leaders.



Tielemans explains: “When you are on the pitch, whether you are 15 or 29 like myself, I think to help each other you need to talk.

“The more you talk, I think the better the team can understand what you need, what others need. I think that is just normal and natural for me to just talk on the pitch.

“But the leadership qualities are maybe there. I just try to be myself, and it all comes in a natural way. I do not try to boss anyone around, you know, because no one likes that anyway.

“So I just try to be myself, be natural, and then obviously with good performances it helps that others follow.”

Tielemans rejects the suggestion he could mentor 22-year-olds Kobbie Mainoo and Andrey Santos.



He stresses: “Those two young players already have a lot of experience and to mix that together, I think we can do good things.

“Andrey has been great. He has been adapting very well, but we have a very good group, a very tight group, and you can tell that he has gelled in very well, very quickly as well.

“You can see his qualities, when he is on the ball, but also off the ball you can see the qualities that he has got to recover the ball and then play forward.



“So I think he is a very good midfielder.”

The natural aim for this success-starved United side is to challenge for honours.

Tielemans helped Leicester lift the FA Cup for the first time ever in 2021, before Villa ended a 30-year trophy drought in May.

United’s wait for a 21st title is ticking towards 14 years, but their players have been queuing up to emphasise they are ready to challenge this season.

Tielemans agrees: “Well, that is always the aim. We want to win football games, but it is a process.



“Like I said, I have only been here for ten days, and in ten days there is a first Premier League game where we can actually test ourselves and see where we are at.

“But every game is going to be important, and to actually fight for titles, or for the league, or whatever, it is a long run.

“It is consistency over the line, and yeah, we are going to have to deal with that before we can speak of winning something.”

Carrick’s fingerprints are already all over this United midfield. Tielemans, Santos, Mainoo and Mason Mount are technical-based players, if not physically imposing. As Carrick was himself.

“He has got his structure,” Tielemans confirms. “He wants to have the ball, he wants to press in certain ways.



“It might be different from what you are used to, what I have been used to before. But it is logical things, in my opinion.

“It is just smelling football, and that is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht. So for me, nothing changes, but it just needs to gel together.

“Then when you follow those principles, then you can add your offensive qualities, especially in the last third where everything is a bit more in freedom, without obviously overcommitting and keeping the defensive line in place, then I think we can do good things.



“It is keeping the ball, but then it needs to achieve something, and hopefully goals.

“When you see our front line, we have got players of tremendous quality, and if they can add goals and we as midfielders can bring the ball to them so that they can create something and score goals, then that is the goal.”

Tielemans played the ball to Fernandes seven times in his half-hour cameo in Gothenburg. “Yeah, it is really natural,” he says of their collaboration.

“He is a guy that can find space easily, and yeah, I just try and find him so that he can move forward.

“I just try and play forward as much as I can, like I said, either to Bruno or the front line, to try and put them in positions that they can attack with freedom and that they can create and use their qualities.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Then obviously defensively trying to keep the structure, trying to keep the defensive line together, so being that link between the defence and the attack. I think that suits me the best.”

After switching off at the World Cup, Tielemans is well and truly switched on.

Sports.title: Man Utd failed to sign Youri Tielemans TWICE before shock summer swoop as £35m ace speaks out on Marcus Rashford reunion
Sports.content:
NEW MANCHESTER UNITED signing Youri Tielemans has revealed the club tried to sign him on two previous occasions.

Tielemans, 29, joined United from Aston Villa for £35million last month after his release clause was triggered.



The Belgium international has spent seven-and-a-half years in the Premier League with Aston Villa and Leicester City, scoring in Europa League and FA Cup final triumphs.

United wanted Tielemans when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Erik ten Hag were in charge but it was third time lucky for the midfielder this summer.



He revealed: “There have been two times that I spoke with the club, but it did not achieve anything, so I was just very calm about it.

“It was not Anderlecht, it was way after. I did not speak with [Solskjaer], no.”

Tielemans confirmed no other clubs were interested in signing him before United moved for the Belgium captain after a £35m deal for Atalanta midfielder Ederson collapsed.

The former Leicester talisman did not expect to leave Villa, having helped them qualify for the Champions League and win the Europa League.

“It was mainly my agent that was dealing with it,” Tielemans added. “I was more focused on the World Cup, which was a big thing for me.

“So I left it all to him and then when it was time and when it was accepted and acceptable, I would say, then I was made aware.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I am very calm about it. When a move comes up, then if it needs to happen, it will happen.

“At the times that I have been linked with the club before, it did not happen, but it is what it is.

“I just keep working, keep doing my thing on the pitch and then it happens.”

Tielemans spoke with United coach Michael Carrick and knew Jonny Evans and Harry Maguire from his four-and-a-half years at Leicester.



Maguire signed a new United contract in April and Evans joined the coaching staff in January after retiring from playing last year.

“You always want to know what the manager thinks of you before you sign,” Tielemans admitted.

“And I think it is really important to have a good relationship with the manager.

“But unless the clubs agree, you cannot really speak to him. So I spoke briefly before, and I had a great connection, and then most of the talks came in after.



“He (Carrick) wants me to be free on the pitch, to try and organise the team as best as possible. “Obviously, he has got his principles, and I just try and do what he asks, but then add my qualities to it.

“I think it is a great achievement for any footballer to end up here. It means you have done well in your career, that the club is following you, first of all, and then to end up here.

“But it does not end there, you know. I just want to be successful, but it is a process, you know. It is only my first 10 days or so here, and I want to win games.”

Tielemans is also keen to reunite with Marcus Rashford after their time together during the latter’s four-month loan at Villa last year.



“He was great,” Tielemans enthused. “There had been so much talk about him and bringing pressure and the media around him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But I thought he was just so good. He was very humble, he was just hard working, and from the first training you could tell his touch, his acceleration was just amazing.

“That was just what we needed at the time at Villa as well, so he did many good things in that time and hopefully he can bring them here.”

Sports.title: 8 transfers that could happen in the next week with Man Utd and Arsenal busy
Sports.content:
The Premier League's Big Six have dominated the summer transfer window so far, splashing out to raid the division for the best players.

Manchester City signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116million. Chelsea signed Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117m. Tottenham signed Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £100m. Arsenal signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m.

Those are among the biggest transfers of the window so far, but there are certain to be more with 20 days left until the deadline on September 1. While the past few weeks have seen intriguing deals touted - think Vinicius Junior to Arsenal, Bradley Barcola to Liverpool or Enzo Fernandez to Man City - there are plenty of others which are actually close to completion.

Here Mirror Football goes through the transfer which you can expect to see wrapped up in the next week.

‌



Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

Cristian Romero to Atletico Madrid

After sensational links with Arsenal, Romero is set to land at a club he appeared destined for. The Argentina international is poised to link up with his compatriot Diego Simeone in Madrid after a £34m deal was agreed with Tottenham.

Spurs have signed Marcos Senesi and Jan Paul van Hecke this summer in preparation for the sale of their captain. The 28-year-old was handed the Spurs captain's armband last summer, when he signed a new four-year contract, yet will leave following his extended post-World Cup break.

View 5 Images Cristian Romero is close to leaving Tottenham (Image: Florencia Tan Jun/UEFA via Getty Images)

Lewis Hall to Manchester United

Newcastle are trying their best to hold onto their left-back after losing Tonali, Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon. But The Sun claims that United haven't given up hope in the pursuit of their first-choice transfer target as they look to provide competition for Luke Shaw. Importantly, it is now claimed that Hall wants to join the Toon exodus and leave for Old Trafford.

‌



United are monitoring other targets, with Club Brugge's £30m-rated Joaquin Seys another option along with Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander, who could cost £14m.

View 5 Images Lewis Hall is a key target for Manchester United (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Rodri to Barcelona

The World Cup-winning captain is keen to leave Manchester City and join Barca, where he's agreed personal terms. Real Madrid remain interested in signing the Ballon d'Or winner, but Barca are in pole position, despite having seen one bid rejected already.

"Out of respect for Madrid, as they have been class, Rodri informed them that his decision is to join Barca," Rodri's agent Pablo Barquero told a Spanish radio station five days ago.

‌



City haven't given up hope of keeping Rodri yet are looking for replacements, with £85m-rated Lille star Ayyoub Bouaddi chief among them. Enzo Maresca wants a reunion with Enzo Fernandez, who Chelsea don't want to sell and have therefore slapped a £120m valuation on him.

Lamine Camara to Crystal Palace

Monaco have rejected a club-record €50m (£42m) bid from Palace for the Senegal international. Manchester United and Chelsea are reportedly monitoring Camara, a 22-year-old midfielder, but Palace will return to try and land their man.

Gabriel Jesus to Napoli

View 5 Images Gabriel Jesus is heading to the Arsenal exit (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Jesus' agent was spotted at Napoli's training ground last week - even if he did try to pass it off as something else - and Arsenal are open to selling the Brazilian. With Romelu Lukaku and Lorenzo Lucca potentially heading for the exit, Napoli could fork out around €20m (£17m) for Jesus, who has slipped down the pecking order behind Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz at Arsenal.

‌



Arsenal have so far only managed to move on Leandro Trossard (£17m to Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (£14.7m to Porto), Karl Hein (£2.5m to Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (£7m to Everton) this summer and know further exits are required.

Djed Spence to Inter Milan

Spence shot to prominence during the World Cup, yet has an uncertain future at Spurs, who have signed Andy Robertson on a free transfer and have Pedro Porro, Destiny Udogie, Souza and Ben Davies as full-back options.

Positive talks took place between Spurs and Inter Milan on Tuesday and the Italian side reportedly believe a total package of around £30m (€35m) could be enough to land the versatile defender. They want a player capable of playing wing-back and Spence appears to fit the bill.

View 5 Images Djed Spence will leave Spurs this summer (Image: Eston Parker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

‌



Julio Enciso to Ipswich

Gary O'Neil managed Enciso at Chelsea's sister club Strasbourg last season and wants the Paraguayan to follow him to Suffolk. The Tractor Boys are understood to have reached an agreement for the 22-year-old, who previously spent time on loan with the club in 2025.

His fee could surpass the club-record £24m they paid Toulouse for Emersonn earlier this summer.

Matteo Ruggeri to Aston Villa

Villa have sold Lucas Digne to Paris Saint-Germain and want Ruggeri as his replacement at left-back. They have made significant progress over a deal which should be worth around £21.4m (€25m).

Ruggeri's departure to Birmingham could free up the funds required for Atleti to sign Romero.

‌

Sports.title: Youri Tielemans sends clear Marcus Rashford message to Michael Carrick after Man Utd reunion
Sports.content:
Youri Tielemans is enjoying being reunited with Marcus Rashford at Manchester United and believes he can make a big impact if given the chance at Old Trafford this season.

Rashford is back in the fold at his boyhood club, returning this week to first-team training after spending the last 18 months out on loan and being ostracised by former United boss Ruben Amorim. The academy graduate, whose long-term future remains in question, spent last season on loan at Barcelona, who rejected the chance to make the move permanent for £26million.

Before then, the England international played alongside Tielemans for Aston Villa in the second half of 2024-25, moving to the Midlands at a time when Rashford was making headlines off the pitch after a tumultuous falling out with Amorim.

Under intense scrutiny, Rashford played his part in Villa's run to the Champions League quarter-finals - losing to eventual winners PSG - and Tielemans admits being impressed by the impact he made in a short period, amid intense scrutiny.

‌



"He was great," he said. "There had been so much talk about him and bringing pressure and the media around him, but I thought he was just so good. He was very humble, he was just hard working, and from the first training you could tell his touch, his acceleration was just amazing. That was just what we needed at the time at Villa as well, so he did many good things in that time and hopefully he can bring them here."

Rashford isn't the only familiar face to Tielemans at United, having also played with both Harry Maguire and first-team coach Jonny Evans at previous club Leicester City.

"I played with Harry for just a bit less than six months and it was great at the time," he added. "You could see him and Jonny had a great partnership. Harry was younger at the time and Jonny was guiding him a bit more, but you could see his qualities on the ball.

"Defensively, he is rock solid, so I think he has improved a lot over the years as well. On Jonny, Jonny has always been a main character. He has always been trying to educate young players and he welcomed me at Leicester, and now here.

‌



"It is a bit weird to see him as staff member, to be honest, but no, it is going great. He knows me, he knows what I need and what I can bring to the team, so it helps me as well."

View 2 Images Youri Tielemans of Manchester United in pre-season action against PSG (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

For Tielemans, joining United is a case of third time lucky, having previously held talks over a move to Old Trafford twice before his switch this summer.

"It is a great achievement for any player to end up here," he says. "T here has been two times that I spoke with the club, but it did not achieve to anything.

‌



"When a move comes up, then if it needs to happen, it will happen. At the times that I have been linked with the club before, it did not happen, but it is what it is."

Sports.title: Cristian Romero nears Tottenham exit as transfer fee agreed amid Arsenal interest
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero nears Tottenham exit as transfer fee agreed amid Arsenal interest

Cristian Romero is close to leaving Tottenham, with the final stages of transfer negotiations progressing following interest from Arsenal, Inter Milan and Barcelona

View 2 Images Cristian Romero is close to leaving Tottenham (Image: Florencia Tan Jun/UEFA via Getty Images)

Cristian Romero is poised to join Atletico Madrid after the Spanish side agreed to pay £34million for the Tottenham captain. Romero has attracted interest from Arsenal, Inter Milan and Barcelona, but will join Diego Simeone's side this summer.

‌



The 28-year-old has always appeared likely to leave Spurs this summer following the arrivals of Marcos Senesi and John Paul van Hecke from Bournemouth and Brighton respectively.

‌



His availability has sparked plenty of interest, with Tottenham's north London rivals Arsenal even contacting his representatives to discuss the possibility of the most controversial transfer in recent Premier League history.

‌



Inter Milan appeared to be the other most likely destination for the Argentina international. The Italian giants have agreed a £34m fee with Spurs, but not personal terms with the centre-back.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

Atletico Madrid always seemed like the perfect fit for Romero, whose playing style suits his compatriot and soon-to-be manager Diego Simeone. Almost everything has now been agreed, according to reports in Spain, and the deal will go ahead.

‌



The deal will bring to a close the possibility of him following in the footsteps of Sol Campbell and William Gallas by moving between Arsenal and Tottenham. The Gunners enquired about his availability in their search for defensive reinforcements following the news that William Saliba will miss the start of the season due to a back injury.

Arsenal have also been linked with Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa and Barcelona's Jules Kounde. And a move for Kounde could rely on Tottenham, with Barcelona reportedly targeting Spurs' Pedro Porro as their preferred replacement for the Frenchman.

View 2 Images Cristian Romero hasn't returned to Tottenham since the World Cup (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

‌



Romero was handed the captain's armband and signed a new four-year contract with Spurs last summer. Speaking on the weekend, manager Roberto De Zerbi kept his cards close to his chest, insisting Romero was still planning to return to Spurs following an extended break after the World Cup.

"I texted with Cuti yesterday to make a plan for when he comes back to London," De Zerbi told reporters in Sydney. "[I did not speak to him about] the transfer market. That's not my job. I know there are many solutions in the transfer market."

Tottenham have invested heavily in the summer transfer window after narrowly escaping relegation to the Championship. Van Hecke and Senesi have been joined by big-money moves for Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, while Andy Robertson has also arrived on a free transfer.

Article continues below

While money has been banked through the departures of Luka Vuskovic, Will Lankshear and Manor Solomon, Spurs still need some more departures, like Romero, to balance the books.

Sports.title: Netherlands make shock move for ex-Premier League boss after Arne Slot snub
Sports.content:
Netherlands make shock move for ex-Premier League boss after Arne Slot snub

The Netherlands are looking for a new manager after parting company with Ronald Koeman and have found a new contender for the role following failed talks with Arne Slot

View 2 Images Arne Slot walked away from the Netherlands job

Roberto Martinez is in talks to become the next manager of the Netherlands, a month after leaving his role with Portugal. Martinez left Portugal after they were knocked out of the World Cup by Spain in the last 16 - but could be set for a swift return to international management.

‌



The Netherlands parted company with Ronald Koeman after they were knocked out of the World Cup in the last 32 by Morocco in June. The penalty shoot-out exit was a painful way to end the tournament and Koeman stepped down from his second spell in charge.

‌



Arne Slot had appeared heavy favourite to succeed Koeman following his departure from Liverpool at the end of last season. But talks with the KNVB (Royal Dutch Football Association) did not lead to a contract offer.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Cristiano Ronaldo marries Georgina Rodriguez as football icon shares ring picture READ MORE :

Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

Slot has since explained that he withdrew from the process due to his desire to stay in club football. De Telegraaf now reports that Martinez is in the frame to take over the side.

The 53-year-old started out in club management, with stints at Swansea, Wigan and Everton, but has spent the past decade in international football. He spent six years with Belgium before joining Portugal in 2023.

‌



Martinez led Belgium to third place at the 2018 World Cup and No.1 in the FIFA world rankings, but left after being knocked out in the group stages of the 2022 World Cup. He won the Nations League with Portugal last year before this summer's disappointment in North America.

View 2 Images Roberto Martinez is available after leaving Portugal (Image: Zhizhao Wu/Getty Images)

Despite being criticised for his conservative playing style, it seems he is the KNVB's second choice for the Netherlands gig after Slot ruled himself out.

‌



"Over the past few weeks, and particularly the past few days, various reports have appeared regarding the vacancy at the Dutch national team, suggesting that I had withdrawn from the process after lengthy negotiations, including regarding salary and contract duration," the former Liverpool boss told Voetbal International.

“That speculation is incorrect. We simply never reached that stage of the talks. At this stage of my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day. Something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team.

“And (this is) why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like. I have enormous respect for the national team and for the KNVB and can only be positive about the professional manner in which the talks proceeded that week.

Article continues below

“For now, I believe that club football still has a lot to offer me. It would be a great honour to represent my country as national coach one day. However, this was not the right moment for me.”

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle offers bleak reality check - 'This is a vacuum'
Sports.content:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle offers bleak reality check - 'This is a vacuum'

Newcastle have undergone a major overhaul this summer, with Matthias Jaissle taking over from Eddie Howe as manager and a series of key players leaving in the transfer window

View 3 Images Matthias Jaissle offered a heavy does of realism (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle has tempered expectations around his side this season in his first press conference after taking over from Eddie Howe.

‌



Jaissle has inherited into a tricky situation on Tyneside following a succession of high-profile exits. Howe walked away after nearly five years in the hot seat, while Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes were sold and Kieran Trippier also departed.

‌



Newcastle banked nearly £250million from those transfers, but have opted to sign young unproven players with potential as replacements. Ewen Jaouen, Bazoumana Toure, Sean Steur, Aladji Bamba and Lukas Hornicek have arrived to work under Jaissle.

‌



The 38-year-old German was hired from Al-Ahli and is under no illusions over the task facing him. "We are in that transition phase," he said. "The players who have left were great characters, great players, experienced players. This is now a vacuum.

Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

"We have to adjust something in the squad by signing these profile of players, or other players need to step up and fill these positions and these leadership roles.

"We are aware of what we need and the squad that we want. Internally, everyone is aware of that, and we are working on the solutions."

‌



Newcastle saw a move for Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg fall through recently and remain on the lookout for experience in the transfer window.

The Magpies finished a disappointing 12th in the Premier League last season under Howe and Jaissle has refused to state their ambitions this season. "This will not happen overnight, especially when you now have such a big transition phase," he said.

View 3 Images Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes left for Arsenal (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



"You need to have a clear goal of where we want to go to. Then, if you have that synergy with the fans, the players and the staff to go there, then I’m pretty sure it will be a successful story. But we need time now. We can only do our best day by day, breaking it down with the goal long ahead.

"We are ambitious. But it makes no sense to promise you anything, because I don’t know how things look in half a year or one year. What we can control, we will control.

"Cutting the tasks down on a daily basis, doing the best job, and then we go in the right direction - and that is going to be successful."

‌



View 3 Images Matthias Jaissle has a rebuilding job on his hands (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Jaissle will be a contrast to the reserved Howe on the touchline, with his animated style likely to come to the fore. "I will not change my style because that's my personality," he said.

"On the touchline, I am emotional, but I need to respect the box [technical area] a bit more. I'm a bit scared. I hope in the beginning the referees can maybe close their eyes here and there a little. I need to learn that.

Article continues below

"I had a long touchline in Saudi Arabia, so I think the GPS would be quite high if I had worn it!"
