Sports.title: Tielemans: I did not expect to leave Aston Villa for Man Utd this summer
Sports.content:
'Not really, no' - the perhaps surprising answer from Manchester United’s summer signing Youri Tielemans when asked whether he expected to leave his former club Aston Villa in this window.

It is easy to forget Man Utd swiftly and covertly signed a player with eight years of Premier League experience at what feels like the height of his footballing powers due to a generous release clause of just £35m.

In his first interview since joining the club, Tielemans has opened up about just how the move came around, especially having been of interest to Manchester United on a few occasions in the past as well.

"There has been two times that I spoke with the club, but it did not achieve anything so I was just very calm about it," Tielemans said.

"It was mainly my agent that was dealing with it, I was more so focused on the World Cup which was a big thing for me. When it was time that it was accepted and acceptable, I would say then I was made aware.

Image: Tielemans signed a five-year deal with Man Utd

"I was not expecting much [a summer move], to be fair. I was just focused on my football, focused on the World Cup, trying to perform as best as I could for my country. Then every summer something can happen."

Tielemans joined Villa as a free agent after leaving Leicester when they were relegated to the Championship. For some reason, a move to the conventional 'top six' never seemed rumoured or close during his time at either of his previous clubs - which is why his move to Manchester United was deemed a surprise.

But did he think the opportunity had passed him by? "Not really, because I know that at Villa we did amazing things," Tielemans explained.

Image: Tielemans made his first appearance for Man Utd against PSG

"We achieved the Europa League win which was great for the club but there are still clubs above Aston Villa, and Manchester United is one of them.

"Especially at this moment, there is a very positive mood in and around the club so I am just hopeful that we can have a great story together.

"Aston Villa is a great club and I owe them the world. They have put me back at my best level so I am very thankful."

Reuniting with Evans and Rashford

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo were among more Manchester United players returning for pre-season training.

Although Tielemans is still getting used to his new surroundings, he will have felt at ease knowing one member of staff very well in particular - Jonny Evans.

The former centre-back spent four and a half years with Tielemans at Leicester and is now a key member of Michael Carrick's backroom staff.

When I asked just how nice it felt to be reunited with his former team-mate, he couldn't resist a huge smile.

Image: Jonny Evans played with Tielemans at Leicester, and is now a coach at Man Utd

"Jonny has always been a main character," Tielemans said. "He has always been trying to educate young players and he welcomed me at Leicester and now here.

"It is a bit weird to see him as a staff member to be honest, but it is going great and he knows me, he knows what I need and what I can bring to the team so it helps me as well."

Another relatively new team-mate Tielemans spent slightly less time with was Marcus Rashford. The pair spent six months together when the England international was on loan at Aston Villa for the second half of the 2024/25 season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Marcus Rashford being fully reintegrated into the Manchester United squad after his loan at Barcelona came to an end earlier this summer, Sky Sports News' Danyal Khan explains how the England forward's return can benefit the club.

There is a lot of attention on the Man Utd winger's return to the club as well as what he can offer this team, Tielemans only has fond memories of their time at Villa Park together and is looking forward to more of them.

He said: "He was great. There had been so much talk about him and bringing pressure with the media around him, but I thought he was just so good.

"He was very humble, he was hard working and from the first training session, you could tell, his touch, his acceleration was amazing.

"That was just what we needed at the time at Villa as well so he did many good things and hopefully he can bring them here."

World Cup, his injury and Balogun's red card reversal

Image: Tielemans was Belgium's captain at the 2026 World Cup

Tielemans has had an eventful summer, even before his surprise move to Manchester United.

He captained Belgium at this summer's World Cup, who were knocked out in the quarter-finals by eventual winners Spain. Tielemans was unable to play in the quarter-final after picking up an injury in the warm-up, but for any Man Utd fans concerned whether he has any lingering injury concerns, he is more than ready for the new season.

Tielemans said: "It was just an overload of too many games, too many minutes and unfortunately my body could not cope with it anymore.

"We played 120 minutes against Senegal and from there, we had less time in between games. We played the USA three or four days later, then three days after that, we played against Spain. In the warm-up, my body switched off for some reason."

Before his injury, the midfielder played a key role in Belgium's World Cup campaign, scoring two goals in their dramatic win against Senegal in the round of 32.

Image: Belgium beat the USA 4-1 despite the controversy surrounding Folarin Balogun's suspended red card

However, perhaps the most eventful game was their round of 16 tie against the USA. In what proved to be one of the most controversial decisions of the tournament, USA striker Folarin Balogun's red card was suspended for the tie, although in the end it did not matter as Belgium went on to win 4-1.

"Originally we were surprised by the decision to revert the red card and his suspension," Tielemans said.

"Now for us, it did not really change anything other than the preparation leading up to the game because it is a different type of player than the other player that was meant to play.

"Other than that, we were very calm and we just accepted our fate and tried to have a good game."

Sports.title: What next for Birmingham City? Why Davies is changing his approach
Sports.content:
Birmingham City is a football club transformed. Over 20,000 season tickets have been sold for the forthcoming Championship season, with 14,000 more on the waiting list. Fan parks surround St Andrew's these days. The buzz around the place is palpable.

There are grand plans to reconnect England's second city to the club that bears its name, unlocking its true potential. Supporters clubs are springing up around the world, a product of Tom Brady's presence. And all the talk is of trying to be Premier League ready.

Given this context, with an ambitious ownership and a success-starved support, it is understandable if Birmingham are in a hurry. Excitement brings expectation, not just internally but externally. There is the sense of a club going places. But it takes time.

On reflection, maybe last season was a moment for the club to breathe rather than a case of lost momentum. After all, you must go back 14 years to the 2011/12 season, when Birmingham were in Europe, for a better finish than the 10th-place effort of 2025/26.

"It was our first season back, which people found hard to remember at times," Birmingham manager Chris Davies tells Sky Sports. He is not talking about the club's supporters - "they have been great" - but everyone. This is a man carrying a lot of hopes and dreams.

"One thing I did learn was that I can handle it," he says. "I can handle the ups and downs." There had not been too many of the latter as Birmingham won the League One title with a record-breaking 111 points, their possession football proving utterly dominant.

Last season was more testing. "You can know about the Championship but to feel it is something different." England's second tier asked different questions. Davies and his team did not always have the answers. Plan A worked only some of the time.

"We came up from League One playing total football, having 80 per cent possession with a lot of circulating the ball, a lot of dominating the ball. It was really effective for us because we just controlled games pretty much the whole way through," he explains.

"In the Championship we were very technical in our recruitment of some smaller players, more technical players, and we tried to use that style. It had really good days and it had days where we just didn't have enough punch, especially away from home."

In that context, opening the season with a hard-fought Carabao Cup win at Swansea in which Birmingham scored the only goal having had 39 per cent of the ball was more than just satisfying. It suggested that his Blues side have added different elements to their game.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Carabao Cup first-round match between Swansea and Birmingham

The scorer, August Priske, is a robust young target-man added in January who looks to have benefited from that half-season in the Championship. The 22-year-old Dane also netted the opening goal against Barcelona in front of a packed St Andrew's last month.

"Jhon Solis, Carlos Vicente and August came in at the same time and that little six months that they did have is their initiation to what English football is like, what the Championship is like, and now they are ready to go. They have all done very well."

Vicente, a combative Spanish winger, provided the assist for Priske's goal at Swansea. Solis also scored against Barcelona with the Colombian already proving a popular figure with the fans. He adds presence to Birmingham's midfield just as Priske does up top.

"When I reflected on the season, I thought for us to take the next step and progress, physicality is going to be really important. The game now is a lot of man-to-man pressing, a lot of set-piece emphasis. You need the physical capacity to deal with it."

That thinking has shaped Birmingham's summer too. Supplementing those winter additions, the club have brought in Dael Fry. The expectation is that a 6ft 4in centre-back with nearly 300 Championship appearances to his name will be able to adapt quickly.

The intention is to add to what Davies has already built, rather than pivot completely. "As a team that can keep the ball, it is a lot easier to then move into a more pragmatic or direct style than being a team that only knows how to play pragmatic or direct football."

That change actually began during the closing weeks of the last campaign. Birmingham were in 17th place in mid-April, but Davies used the brief international break in the spring to make some of these adjustments to their style of play. They went more direct.

Image: Christoph Klarer's passing sonar shows how Birmingham have become more direct

"I started thinking about being a little bit more flexible with the shape we were using and how we were positioning ourselves, but focusing more on more direct play, more transitions and more set-pieces if possible. So we sort of finished the season that way."

Birmingham ended the campaign on a five-game unbeaten run, earning that top-10 finish and taking some belief into the summer.

"It is a fine balance because we don't want to lose what we're good at. What I won't come away from is the pressing. I don't think any team last season in the Championship really played through our press consistently. I thought it was really effective for us."

But there will be tweaks once Birmingham win the ball back. "I think that hopefully is something that we can have as a weapon that we can use a little bit more. When we get the ball, just to go forward that little bit quicker, hopefully win more set-pieces."

That explains another addition behind the scenes. Birmingham have brought in a specialist set-piece coach in Scott Fry, with Davies identifying dead-ball situations as an obvious way that his team can become genuine promotion contenders this season.

Solis scored from one against Barcelona. Priske's winner against Swansea came after a set-piece found Vicente and he squared the ball for the striker. In other words, this emphasis on set-pieces is already making the difference. And Davies has been doing his sums.

"We have a set-piece coach and the idea is to score more from them. We needed to score 70-odd goals really to be in among those top teams last season." Crucially, that was the total hit by the top six but not the rest of the Championship. Birmingham scored 57.

The task this time around is to find those extra 13 goals somehow. "If six or seven of those can come from set-pieces and two or three can come from counter-attacks, then you only need another two or three from your general football. So it is absolutely doable."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jude Bellingham discusses his love of Birmingham and his love of cricket

Absolutely doable. That sums up the mood. Last time, they were learning about the Championship. Now they know. "It was not just me, several players had never played in it before. Now they have 40 games in the bank. They know what it is like away at Millwall."

At the training ground, Davies has tried to strip back the buzzwords that once adorned the walls. No more gimmicks is the mantra now. Leaner and meaner, like the squad. The feeling is that there is more continuity now, that this Birmingham are ready to kick on.

Craig Gardner has left as director of football but the club has played down the impact, leaning on the experienced Mike Rigg. Commercially, Birmingham continue to grow, with the biggest revenue of any Championship club not reliant on parachute money.

After storming up and then stabilising, the next step awaits Birmingham City. And now, it feels like everyone is ready for it. "I am confident that we can keep progressing. That is the big thing," says Davies. "We just need to keep moving forward and getting stronger."

Sports.title: Championship play-off changes, new managers & star players - the EFL is BACK!
Sports.content:
The 2026/27 EFL season is here!

We kick off on Friday night with Wolves vs Blackburn Rovers, and every Championship, League One and League Two game is LIVE this weekend!

But what have we got in store for the new campaign? We take a look at some of the key stories...

Championship

From top six to top eight... a new play-off system has arrived!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Simeon Gholam explains all you need to know on how the play-offs have changed this season in the Championship

The most significant alteration to domestic football in decades has happened over the summer, with the Championship play-offs expanding from a top-six spot to a top-eight position this season, presenting clubs with more opportunity for promotion.

What has (and hasn't) changed?

1st and 2nd are automatically promoted as normal.

3rd and 4th still qualify for the semi-finals.

5th vs 8th and 6th vs 7th in one-off eliminator ties at the home of the side who finishes higher up the league.

The winners of the eliminator ties progress to the semi-finals, to face 3rd and 4th in two-legged ties with the second leg at the home of the side that finishes higher up the league.

One other key thing to note is that, whatever happens, 3rd will face the lowest-ranked team remaining in the semi-finals. So if 8th beats 5th, and 6th beats 7th in the eliminators, 3rd will face 8th and 4th will face 6th. There is no pre-set path for the semi-finals before the eliminators.

in the semi-finals. So if 8th beats 5th, and 6th beats 7th in the eliminators, 3rd will face 8th and 4th will face 6th. There is no pre-set path for the semi-finals before the eliminators. As per usual, the winners of the two semi-finals meet at Wembley for a place in the Premier League.

Are the relegated clubs automatic favourites?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kevin Nolan and Darren Moore tell the EFL Show why Jarrod Bowen is key for West Ham's hopes for an instant return to the Premier League

It did not take long for West Ham and Wolves to be installed as favourites for an immediate return to the Premier League.

The Hammers are playing at this level for the first time in 14 years, and have kept hold of head coach Nuno Espirito Santo and key asset Jarrod Bowen.

Both are familiar with this level. Nuno won the Championship - with Wolves - in 2018, while Bowen played in it with Hull City before he left for east London.

Wolves, meanwhile, replaced boss Rob Edwards with the relatively unknown quantity of Cesar Peixoto in the summer. But the quality in their squad could prove telling, with Andre, Mateus Mane, Santiago Bueno and Hugo Bueno sticking about.

They have also added Raul Jimenez and Kieran Trippier to the bank. Experience and class.

It is Burnley where a bit more uncertainty lingers. They have appointed a new head coach in Nicky Hayen, a 45-year-old Belgian who has previously managed Club Brugge and Genk.

But it is worth remembering the Clarets have won promotion in their last two Championship seasons - both times with 100+ points. They are experts at this level.

According to the Sky Sports supercomputer, West Ham and Wolves are the two favourites, with Burnley in fourth just behind Middlesbrough...

Middlesbrough go big to try and get over the line

It was some campaign for Middlesbrough last season. They spent more days in the top two than any other club, but managed to finish fifth.

They were then the victim of the Spygate saga, lost to Southampton in the play-off semi-finals, were reinstated to the final, then lost at Wembley to a stoppage-time Oli McBurnie goal for Hull City.

But any potential hangover looks like it has already been left behind with some of their work in the transfer window.

Owner Steve Gibson has taken his chequebook out and spent serious money to strengthen. Striker Will Lankshear has already made his mark with the winning goal against Wrexham in the Carabao Cup. He scored 11 goals for a struggling Oxford side last season and arrives from Spurs.

Sebastian Berhalter comes in, having last been seen playing for the USA at the World Cup, while goalkeeper Radek Vitek from Manchester United is also an eye-catching addition. He impressed on loan at Bristol City last season.

Kim Hellberg and some Boro fans may be wondering where this backing was in January when they were crying out for reinforcements, but it has certainly led to a swell of excitement at the Riverside about what's possible this season.

Can Southampton escape Spygate scandal?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports' Mark McAdam before the FA charge, Southampton boss Tonda Eckert revealed the challenges he has faced after the Spygate scandal that resulted in their expulsion from the Championship play-offs

It was the story that dominated the landscape of last season. A shockwave went around the footballing world when Southampton were expelled from the play-offs after their role in the Spygate scandal.

But the club were quick to back Tonda Eckert, and although an FA charge still hangs over the boss, they have tried to move on and heal the wounds caused by the damage.

Fears of a player exodus have been quelled, with only midfielder Shea Charles departing so far, and the club has brought in goalkeeper Daniel Peretz and striker Cyle Larin permanently, after both starred on loan in the second half of last season.

They will have to overcome a four-point deduction. But they came from a long way back last season with a remarkable run in the second half of the campaign, and they certainly have the quality to challenge.

Managerial changes in the Championship

There are also a few other managerial changes to make a note of. Tony Mowbray is back at Blackburn Rovers four years after he left the club, while Watford have brought in Alessio Dionisi.

Elsewhere, Michael Skubala left Lincoln City after leading them to promotion to join Bristol City. While his exit opened the door for the Imps to make the unique move of appointing joint-managers in the role. Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw take the reins at Sincil Bank.

League One

Will Leicester turn things around?

Image: Leicester City manager Russell Martin

For just the second time in their history, and just 10 years after they won the Premier League title, Leicester City have found themselves in League One.

Russell Martin has taken the helm, as they look to end a miserable run of back-to-back relegations. He also has work to do in winning over some doubters, after miserable ends to his spells at Southampton and Rangers in his last two roles.

The addition of experience has been the aim of the summer, with the likes of Liam Cullen, Conor Chaplin and Wes Burns already joining.

A new dawn for Wednesday and who else could compete for promotion?

The Chansiri era is finally over at Sheffield Wednesday, and there has been a swirl of optimism around the club under new owner David Storch, despite relegation.

Henrik Pedersen, who led the Owls through the grim 2025/26 season, has been given the opportunity to see if he can get more out of a squad that is actually built to compete.

Louie Barry is an eye-catching addition. Injuries have blighted his progress but he has shown what a star he can be at this level for Stockport County, while Barry Bannan is back home after his stint at Millwall.

Luton are quite fancied under Jack Wilshere after a positive run in the second half of last season.

As are Plymouth Argyle, who have been exceptional so far in 2026, just missing out on the play-offs.

Managerial changes in League One

Image: Aaron Ramsey has taken his first permanent managerial role at Oxford United

There has been a particularly notable appointment at Oxford United, with Aaron Ramsey taking his first permanent managerial role to replace Matt Bloomfield, who surprisingly departed in the summer.

It has not been an easy start for Ramsey, however, as he has already had to deal with a transfer embargo which has left him unable to make any additions at the relegated club.

Elsewhere, Daniel Stendel has returned to Barnsley, Martin Drury has taken charge at Huddersfield Town and Jimmy McNulty left Rochdale to join Stockport following the departure of Dave Challinor.

Bromley's first season in the third tier!

Bromley were promoted to the EFL for the first time in their history in 2024, and it took just two seasons for them to seal promotion from League Two.

The Ravens won the title last season, and will now compete in the third tier of English football for the first time. It has only been 11 years since they were promoted to the National League for the first time.

They have been installed as the favourites for relegation, but Andy Woodman's side have defied the critics before and will be keen to do so again. Don't rule out anything at Hayes Lane.

All change at York and Rochdale

After 10 years away, York City are back in the EFL!

But it has not been all smooth sailing since. A couple of weeks before the start of the season, manager Stuart Maynard - who led them to promotion with more than 100 points - departed the club.

His replacement Scott Lindsey has not proven popular so far. In his first game in charge York exited the Carabao Cup at the preliminary phase, with fans booing and calling for the return of Maynard.

Not quite the return the Minstermen would have wanted to League Two.

The side they edged to automatic promotion in the National League, Rochdale, have also lost their manager after fighting their way through the play-offs.

McNulty moved on to Stockport, and they have dipped into non-League to appoint their new manager, with Ian Watson joining from National League North side South Shields.

Will Salford City finally get over the line?

Image: Macaulay Langstaff is one of the summer arrivals at Salford City

It is seven years now since Salford City were promoted to League Two, and still they have not managed to get over the line.

Last season was the closest they have come, losing in the play-off final to Notts County. Manager Karl Robinson has since departed, with Peter Cklamovski taking his place, having most recently been in charge of the Malaysia national side.

They have gone big in the transfer market, too. Macaulay Langstaff and Luke Molyneux have already arrived. Could this be the year the club owned by Gary Neville and David Beckham finally reach League One?

Managerial changes in League Two

Elsewhere, there are a lot of new managers to keep an eye on. Chris Hogg has come in at Northampton Town, while another relegated club in Rotherham United have appointed Alex Bruce.

Darrell Clarke takes charge at Tranmere Rovers, Lee Grant is at Walsall and Hayden Mullins will lead Newport County this season.

Sports.title: Sky Sports agrees deal to show Laver Cup from London's O2 in September
Sports.content:
Sky Sports has agreed a deal with Trident8 to show all three days of the Laver Cup from London's O2 arena this September, as 12 of the world's best men's players compete in the annual Europe vs 'Rest of the World' showdown.

World No 2 Carlos Alcaraz and Wimbledon finalist Alexander Zverev will be in action for Team Europe, while USA pair Ben Shelton and Taylor Fritz will lead the charge for Team World under the stewardship of captain Andre Agassi.

Hosted by presenter Gigi Salmon, Sky Sports will broadcast all 12 matches across day and night sessions on Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26, followed by a single concluding session on Sunday September 27. There will also be a reporter on the ground keeping fans abreast of all the news from the weekend's action.

Alongside broadcast rights, fans in the UK and Ireland will also be able to catch up on all the action with clips and highlights available across Sky's digital and social platforms.

Team Europe vice-captain and Sky Sports Tennis expert Tim Henman said: "It's great news the Laver Cup will be on Sky Sports.

"It's a unique opportunity to see the best players in the world coming together to represent Team Europe and Team World at the iconic O2 arena.

"Fans can expect plenty of drama, passion and rivalry, both on and off the court."

Live tennis is available all year on Sky Sports, including the Cincinnati Open beginning on Thursday August 13 and the US Open from Sunday August 30.

Sky Sports will broadcast over 4,000 matches and 80 tournaments this season, which are also available to stream with NOW and the Sky Sports app.

Watch the ATP and WTA Tours and US Open from August 30, live on Sky Sports or stream with NOW and the Sky Sports app

Sports.title: Jodar on course for tennis history as Rybakina fights past Osaka
Sports.content:
Spanish teenager Rafael Jodar is on course to break the record for the fastest rise into the top 10 of men's tennis after beating Arthur Filis in the quarter-finals of the Canadian Open.

Jodar came out on top in a rain-affected contest on Tuesday to win 7-6 (7-5) 6-3 to ensure he will move up to at least 11th in the ATP rankings, having started the year in 165th.

The 19-year-old will face American Brandon Nakashima in the semi-finals on Wednesday night, live on Sky Sports Tennis, where victory could see him smash Boris Becker's current record of 210 days to go from breaking the top 100 to being in the top 10. Jodar would do it in just 140 days.

However, Jodar also requires defending Canadian Open champion Ben Shelton to lose to Learner Tien in the other semi-final.

Shelton, a two-time Grand Slam semi-finalist, swept out Jakub Mensík in straight sets 6-3 6-1 in 72 minutes and is yet to drop a set in this tournament.

Image: Ben Shelton is the defending Canadian Open champion (Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press via AP)

Should Jodar and Shelton meet in Thursday's final, a win for Jodar would also see him move into the top 10 and make history.

"I played a very high level against a tough player like Arthur," said Jodar after beating Filis.

"I had to give my best to win this match. It worked perfectly, staying calm in those important moments of the match, those pressure moments."

Image: Rafael Jodar (left) reached the quarter-finals at the French Open earlier this year (Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press via AP)

Rybakina battles back to beat Osaka

Elena Rybakina rallied back after losing the opening set to defeat 11th-seed Naomi Osaka 4-6 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 and advance to the semi-finals of the WTA Canadian Open in Toronto.

Osaka came flying out of the blocks by breaking in the opening game which was enough to win the first set, before both players twice exchanged breaks in the second which Rybakina won on a tie-break.

The Kazakh made the decisive break in the seventh game of the last set and went on to win arguably the match of the tournament.

Image: Elena Rybakina would be just four ranking points behind Aryna Sabalenka if she wins the Montreal title (Julian Avram/Icon Sportswire/AP)

"Super happy. It was a very difficult match. In the first set [I made] a few mistakes, a poor start," said Rybakina, who could overtake Aryna Sabalenka as world No 1 later this month.

"It was a really tough one but I'm glad I could turn it around, I don't yet know how, but I think my serve helped me a little bit."

Rybakina will play Coco Gauff in the semi-finals after the American received a walkover in her quarter-final when her opponent Belinda Bencic withdrew due to a hip injury.

The other semi-final sees Iga Swiatek take on Elina Svitolina for a place in Thursday's final.

Watch the ATP and WTA Tours and US Open from August 30, live on Sky Sports or stream with NOW and the Sky Sports app.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Ffos Las hosts six-race card
Sports.content:
Don't miss a moment from Ffos Las on Wednesday, with all six races live from 3.37pm on Sky Sports Racing.

4.37 Ffos Las - Narrjoo headlines following promising debut

Narrjoo headlines a field of seven in the Meyer Timber EBF Maiden Stakes.

Simon and Ed Crisford's representative finished second to exciting Godolphin newcomer Jassas when impressing on debut at Doncaster last month and will be tough to beat if he can run to the same standard. This 200,000gns son of Ten Sovereigns has future entries in the Champagne Stakes and Goffs Million, which indicate how highly he is thought of at Gainsborough Stables.

Drum Bay and Isabella de Vega both similarly caught the eye on their respective debuts, and should provide a good level of opposition to Narrjoo for Ralph Beckett and Ed Walker respectively.

The most intriguing newcomer comes in the form of the 200,000gns two-year-old Mehmas colt Engraved, who could run well first time up for the James Fanshawe team.

3.37 Ffos Las - No Half Measures' half-sister clashes with Eskimo Pie

Eskimo Pie seeks her first success in the Faucets The Bathroom Specialists Maiden Fillies' Stakes but will have to get past No Half Measures' half-sister Mystic Veil, who makes her debut.

Eskimo Pie finished a good seventh in the 2025 Queen Mary Stakes before running lame on her final start at two in the Princess Margaret. Her first start at three was promising, but she subsequently underperformed in her next two tries. She was bumped when looking to challenge at Newmarket the last day and very much sets the standard at her peak for the Jane Chapple-Hyam team.

The Ed Walker-trained Mollstar showed a respectable level of form on her third run before being found reportedly lame after her last start in December. Returning from a break here, this filly is an interesting contender under Ashley Lewis.

Mystic Veil is a half-sister to July Cup winner No Half Measures and is trained by Archie Watson - a handler renowned for his success with two-year-olds. She could very well succeed on her first outing and a market watch is essential in the build-up.

Dixie Blue - a daughter of Starspangledbanner - also makes her first start, while Livvy's Edge completes the quintet.

6.10 Ffos Las - Belle Of Kt bids for another success

Belle Of Kt bids for a hat-trick in the Dress For The Occasions Handicap, wish closes the card at the Welsh track.

The admirably consistent mare has found some improvement of late, putting a couple of wins together within the space of eight days. She did not seem to have loads in hand last time out when scoring by a nose, but should put up a bold effort when attempting a hat-trick, with Millie Wonnacott's 5lb claim potentially crucial.

A Daughters Love should prove tough to beat following a facile 10-length victory when bouncing back to form down in grade last time out. She clearly enjoys this course and distance but has been raised 6lb for that victory.

Noble Grace also won over course and distance just two weeks ago, yet in contrasting fashion, battling well in a terrific finish.

Sports.title: 'Everyone can have an opinion' - F1 president responds to regulations criticism
Sports.content:
Formula 1 president Stefano Domenicali says drivers "can have their opinion" and are not being stopped from criticising the sport's power unit regulations.

The 2026 technical regulations have divided opinion with Max Verstappen among those to voice his concerns about the rules which have led to a different style of driving and racing.

Verstappen has previously described the yoyo style of racing - which sees passes then re-passes - as "anti-racing" and joked at last month's Belgian Grand Prix that someone would "probably shoot me outside the door" if he criticised the rules.

The Red Bull driver clarified a week later in Hungary: "I've spoken my mind about these regulations already a long time, and in the beginning, most people were saying, 'ah, he's complaining; he should shut up'.

"But I have to say that the last few races, more and more people are seeing the same thing that I could see coming already a long time, and it's not about me not liking not winning anymore.

"It's just because I care about the product, and because I've said it many times, and at one point that's also enough, right? But of course, when people keep asking you, then yeah, maybe it's not appreciated always, but I'm just speaking. I'm just speaking my mind because you see certain things coming, and then sometimes people say, 'yeah, but this was a great race'.

"I say, 'yeah, but it's not really realistic the way we are racing'. And then you arrive to some tracks, and yeah, you're driving on not a lot of horsepower for F1 standards, and it's a little bit painful, which I could see coming already for years. It's then, of course, not the most exciting. But at one point, I'm also a little bit just fed up with repeating myself because it's already hard enough just having to drive it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton went wheel to wheel in a feisty scrap at the Austrian GP

Domenicali says he would prefer to discuss things behind closed doors to find solutions but respects all the drivers' opinions.

"You know me, we are not here to put tape on the mouth of anyone. The beauty of our sport is that everyone can have an opinion, but the opinion is an opinion," he said.

"There is someone who has the duty to have a line. There are certain drivers that prefer, of course, certain things. That in the process we have highlighted the need to be constructive in that respect."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen shocked Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Domenicali: F1 is bigger than any driver

In March, Verstappen stated he was considering his future in the sport if the regulations did not change for next year, such was his dissatisfactions with the new power unit rules which have more electrical power compared to previous seasons.

The current split is nearly 50-50 between internal combustion and electrical power but the FIA announced in May it had agreed with the teams to change this to 58-42 for 2027 and 60-40 for 2028.

Since then, Verstappen has not suggested he will walk away from F1, although questions remain over whether he will drive for Red Bull or another team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater assesses what Verstappen's next move could be and whether the Red Bull driver may head to McLaren or Mercedes

Domenicali said: "Max is an incredible driver. I've stated so many times that maybe I'm getting older to repeat that!

"Max is in a situation where if he loves Formula 1. We discuss together the regulations for the future. I have an incredible relationship with him.

"F1 is big enough for him to be part of us, but of course he will decide his future, the way that he prefers to do. The sport will look ahead but my opinion is that Max will stay with us, and I really hope so, and that's what I'm stating. The sport is big, much bigger than anyone else, all of us."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hamilton and Charles Leclerc went head-to-head in their Ferrari's at the Chinese GP

Every F1 event this season has been sold out with record crowd attendances in Australia (484,000), Canada (360,000), Austria (320,000), Silverstone (564,000), Belgium (400,000) and Hungary (310,000).

Domenicali pointed to the continued growth of F1 and a conversation he had with filmmaker and creator of Star Wars, George Lucas, which shows the majority of fans are "not interested in how you drive the car" but instead whether there is overtaking or not.

"I had an incredibly interesting discussion with George Lucas on Saturday. He was in Hungary, and he was giving me an incredible view on how the new fans are watching Formula 1," he said.

"He gave us an incredible clearance to see how we can really simplify things because the new fans are not understanding the truth, what is behind the scenes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard Alpine's Franco Colapinto as he pulls off an incredible double overtake on Pierre Gasly and Liam Lawson at the Belgian GP

"They are fascinated by the fact that there is a lot of action. There is definitely the need for those who are so focused on that to have the right information.

"But, for the vast majority of the people, trust me, they just want to see what is happening on the track, not interested in the angle of throttle or the percentage of brake pressure on how you can take and overtake a driver.

"For example, the incredible overtake of Max on Lewis at Turn 1 in Hungary, that was a piece of art, if I may say, that these people just want to see and just connect to the quality of the drivers."

Sports.title: Dubois on collision course with Turkish rival? MVP announce Turhan signing

Caroline Dubois could settle her rivalry with Elif Nur Turhan after the Turkish world champion signed for Most Valuable Promotions.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 6: Chelsea
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 3rd (NB: this is not necessarily Billy Munday’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 10th

Prospects

After a season of struggle and regression, with two head coaches and two spells under a caretaker, there is cautious optimism that this campaign will bring something like stability. Much of that optimism centres around the appointment of Xabi Alonso, an elite manager with something to prove. There is also an expectation that the young players brought in as part of BlueCo’s £1.8bn splurge in recent years are beginning to come into their best years. There is no European football to complicate the schedule and a return to the Champions League by finishing in the top four or five would suffice for now. More importance will be placed on the domestic cups after a season without trophies.

Alonso’s squad is more rounded than what Enzo Maresca or Liam Rosenior had at their disposal. Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers bring quality to positions where Chelsea were lacking it – at centre-back and out wide. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson – the “uncs” as Tosin Adarabioyo has called them – will contribute as much off the pitch as on it. The signing of Marco Palestra, a specialist wing-back, suggests Alonso wants to be tactically flexible. He has used a back four and a back three in pre-season.

What about Cole Palmer? For so much of his time at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea’s form has been tied to his. When he has struggled to be 100% fit, the team have suffered too. After being omitted from England’s World Cup squad, Palmer had a seven-week break and sought advice from a specialist on the groin injury that hampered him last season. “I got bored after six weeks,” Palmer said after returning for pre-season. “I was sat in Marbella thinking: ‘I want to go back in.’” With the prospect of linking up with Rogers and João Pedro, who has also had a good rest, Palmer has plenty of reasons to be excited.

Off-field picture

July ended with Chelsea being fined £10m and receiving a suspended transfer ban over multiple violations of transfer rules under the ownership of Roman Abramovich. An appeal from the club saved them from a six-point deduction. Chelsea were deemed compliant with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules for the three-year period ending in 2025 despite posting an English record £262.4m pre-tax loss for the 2024-25 season. They have not been cowed by failure to qualify for Europe and have spent over £300m on new signings. For the fourth year in a row, Chelsea look likely to start the season without a front-of-shirt sponsor.

Owner-fan relationship

Supporter protests against the ownership of Todd Boehly’s BlueCo have been a frequent sight on matchdays, including before May’s FA Cup final defeat by Manchester City. There have been reservations about the club’s youth-oriented transfer policy from the start and last season’s failings prompted the co-owner Behdad Eghbali to admit the need “to add more ready-made players” to the squad. Whether fans were expecting the arrivals of Welbeck and Henderson is another question. The introduction of a ticket ballot system for home games has also been unpopular with regular match-going supporters.

The manager

It was a bit of a coup for Chelsea to secure Alonso’s services this summer, especially given the Liverpool job was available. The Spaniard has a reputation to rebuild after his dream job at Real Madrid ended in the sack after six months. “I got a scar, now it is healed,” he said. Alonso’s record of developing young players, such as Florian Wirtz, at Bayer Leverkusen while simultaneously delivering silverware is a match made in heaven for the Chelsea hierarchy. One detail to note: Alonso has been appointed as manager, rather than head coach like his predecessors. He has also brought in Austin MacPhee, Aston Villa’s set-piece guru.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Chelsea broke the British transfer record to pry Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Chelsea went one better than Manchester City’s £116m signing of Elliot Anderson by bringing in Rogers, who had been linked with Arsenal, for a new British record fee of £117m. Although he started England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina on the right wing, Rogers has thrived for Aston Villa playing largely off the left and should slot in there nicely at Chelsea. The 24-year-old has proved himself in the Premier League and his best-buddy relationship with his former Manchester City youth teammate Palmer is a major plus. “I can see them linking really well,” Alonso said.

Stat attack

Has anyone checked Chelsea haven’t built a squad of Benjamin Buttons? The average age of their starting XI has decreased over the past three seasons when they were already the youngest team in Premier League history. You can see why they signed Henderson and Welbeck.

Set for a breakthrough

Robert Sánchez is still Chelsea’s No 1 but he may face serious competition this season from the 21-year-old Mike Penders. The goalkeeper, who was third-choice for Belgium at the World Cup, was signed from Genk in 2024 and spent last season on loan at Strasbourg in Ligue 1. The comparisons with Thibaut Courtois, who Chelsea signed from Genk at a similar age, are obvious. Like Courtois, Penders is 6ft 7in and therefore has a massive reach, but he also earns plaudits for his passing. Chances will come in cup competitions, but the clamour for Penders to be first choice might become hard to ignore.

World Cup impact

Enzo Fernández had a rollercoaster of a World Cup. Chelsea’s vice-captain popped up with crucial late goals for Argentina in the knockout stages, including a winning header against Egypt and the equaliser against England. But the abiding memory was his part in Argentina’s unsavoury approach in the final against Spain, where he received one yellow card for dissent and another for sending Pau Cubarsí flying. Real Madrid said in July they had “no intention” of pursuing a move that Fernández seemed to covet earlier this year when he said he would “love” to live in Madrid – comments that earned him a two-game ban under Rosenior. How about living in Manchester? City have been linked.

Sports.title: ‘It’s a nice hobby’: Manchester United’s Janina Leitzig on goalkeeping and gardening
Sports.content:
With some parts of England gearing up for a fifth heatwave of 2026, the new Manchester United goalkeeper Janina Leitzig, a keen gardener, is sympathetic to the precarious health of this reporter’s tomato plants. “You’re not used to so little rain, are you?” she observes. For the time being, after her summer move to Manchester, the former Germany youth international does not have a garden of her own, but she reveals that, during her three-and-a-half-year spell at her former club Leicester, homegrown vegetables were her pride and joy.

“I love to do some gardening. Back home, everyone has their own vegetables and it’s just better, it tastes better,” she tells the Guardian. “Being away from home and away from family, of course you have your football friends, but still it can be quite lonely sometimes if you come home from training, so it was really nice to have a garden and to spend time outside. It’s not too much effort, it’s just a nice hobby.”

The 27-year-old got her outdoor fix with a spot of surfing in Cornwall this summer during the off-season, but now the serious business of pre-season is well under way. Her new club Manchester United are heading to La Manga for a training camp between 14 and 19 August, where the focus will have to be less on runner beans and more on running drills.

Leitzig, the former Bayern Munich and Hoffenheim keeper, was sitting down for an interview before it was known that the Spanish coach Eva Olid was to become United’s new manager, but explained why swapping Leicester for United was appealing to her.

“It’s such a big club and it’s such a big honour to be here,” Leitzig says. “I think, for every player, it’s really interesting if you have an offer from Manchester United. First of all, the team is so nice. The characters in here – you can tell it’s a really good and strong team. The training quality is really high. The building and the facilities [at Carrington] are really good; it’s really professional here. [When] the conversations were going on [with United], they just gave me a really good feeling.”

View image in fullscreen Janina Leitzig during a training session at Carrington. Photograph: Poppy Townson/MUFC/Getty Images

Leitzig has signed a contract with United until 2029, after the disappointment of relegation with Leicester last term, but says she has nothing but fond feelings about her former club, who she initially joined on loan in January 2023 before signing permanently that summer.

Looking back at what she learned in the East Midlands, she says: “It was such a special time for me. It was supposed to be only half a year and then it ended up being three-and-a-half. I think that says a lot about how much I liked it there. The people are great and the club is great. Obviously we had some tough times and unfortunately the relegation last season was really, really tough and it really hurt, because the club deserves to be in a better position, but I really hope that the girls will do well and I see them soon back in the WSL. It would be great if they could come back up quickly.”

During her time in England, Leitzig has observed an evolution in goalkeeping styles, and she is in a thoughtful mood when discussing what the future might look like for keepers, tactically. On the modern trend of keepers playing out from the back, she says: “To be fair, there was one phase where everyone wanted goalkeepers to play with the feet and I think it’s still really important, but I think there was a phase where it was too much. I think it was a bit over exaggerated at times, so I think it’s coming back now to be more about the basic stuff.

“Obviously you have to switch play and you have to be good with your feet under pressure, but I think the game is going to be more [about] trying to get the ball as quick as possible in the opposite half to then keep the pressure up there and not to try to take such a high risk. It’s going to be interesting. I think, because I’m German and Manuel Neuer [her idol] is German, I learned quite early to play with both feet and I was an outfield player initially, so I’m feeling confident about playing with the ball. But saving shots is the best part of goalkeeping.”

The United States keeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce played in 21 of United’s 22 WSL matches last term and Leitzig says they will enjoy working together and helping each other. “They [United] said it’s like a competition [to start in goal]. Obviously it’s really important to have strong goalkeepers, because you never know what happens in the season. I will just give my best, I’ll try to bring quality, and then it’s the manager’s decision to decide who’s going to play. But it’s really important that we are a good goalkeeper team, that we support each other and push each other because then everyone can get better.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United, who finished fourth last term, will get the new WSL season under way on the opening night, away to London City Lionesses on 4 September. Leizig concludes by looking ahead to that showdown and says, with fire in her eyes: “To have the first game of the season Friday evening, 7pm, floodlights, it’s just something you’re really excited for. Working in the pre-season you think: ‘When can the [games] finally start’, so I’m really excited for that game.”

Sports.title: Barcelona make improved £51m bid for Rodri as Manchester City target Fernández
Sports.content:
Barcelona have made an improved bid to Manchester City of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri. This follows Barça’s initial offer of €45m that was rejected out of hand by City.

The Spanish club’s new offer – which may include add-ons – is close to City’s valuation for the 30-year-old who captained Spain to the World Cup and won the Ballon d’Or in 2024.

As the midfielder has declared a preference for Barcelona it seems it is inevitable he will leave. In preparation City are targeting Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández as a potential signing though the west London club’s valuation of around £120m may be too high.

Chelsea are understood to be intent on that price for the attacking midfielder so any transfer may include add-ons. Enzo Maresca is keen on Fernández after working with him for a season-and-a-half at Chelsea before his tenure ended in January.

The 25-year-old was a key member of Maresca’s team that finished fourth and won the Europa Conference in 2024-25 and the Fifa Club World Cup last summer.

If City were to sign Fernández, a World Cup winner with Argentina in 2022, another midfielder could be offloaded, with Tijjani Reijnders a possible candidate to depart.

As Rodri is intent on a move to Barcelona the arrival of Fernández, Chelsea’s captain, would add seniority and leadership to Maresca’s squad and a player whose combative style would offer an edge to City’s play.

City have so far recruited Elliott Anderson for £116m from Nottingham Forest and are close to the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi for around £85m from Lille.

Chelsea are thought to have enquired about Bournemouth’s Alex Scott as a replacement for Fernández should he leave.
