World.title: Putin warns of tit-for-tat seizures of European vessels
World.content:
If European states seize vessels with Russian cargo, Moscow will respond in kind ‘wherever necessary’, says Putin.

Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has threatened to seize European vessels if European states follow through on plans to seize more commercial ships with Russian cargo.

Putin delivered the warning on Wednesday while on board a Russian cruiser off the Pacific island of Sakhalin, where Russia’s navy was conducting a drill. He said Russia would be ready to carry out its own seizures “wherever we deem it necessary and appropriate,” according to Russia’s TASS news agency.

The statement comes after several European countries intercepted ships suspected of being part of Moscow’s so-called “shadow fleet”, carrying Russian oil in contravention of European sanctions.

New sanctions passed last month permit European Union members to sell the oil or any other cargo seized from the ships.

Putin appeared to reference the sanctions, saying some countries are trying to “restrict the movement of vessels belonging to our economic operators” and recently “came up with the idea of possibly seizing our ships and selling off property stolen from us”.

“If these plans are put into practice, we will have to respond in kind,” Putin said in comments carried by Russia’s RIA Novosti news agency, calling the moves “piracy and robbery”.

He said “relevant instructions” had already been delivered to Russia’s Ministry of Defence and Pacific Fleet, the naval fleet responsible for Russia’s maritime military interests in the Pacific.

NATO ‘making inroads in Asia Pacific’

Putin also accused the NATO military alliance of making inroads into the Asia Pacific region and heightening tension in the Arctic. “NATO is making inroads into the ‌region, new military-political blocs are being formed, and new weapons systems that pose a threat to Russia are ‌being deployed or are slated for deployment,” the Russian leader said.



Russia’s naval exercises in the West Pacific come a week before joint US-South Korean war games, designed to simulate a possible invasion from North Korea.

Tensions are high in the region amid accusations from Kyiv and Seoul that Pyongyang and Moscow are further intensifying their military cooperation.

On Tuesday, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of using North Korean missiles in a deadly air raid across Ukraine. A day earlier, he had warned that Moscow was receiving more ballistic projectiles and troops from its ally Pyongyang, a development he said posed dangers not only for Ukraine but for countries in East Asia.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has already sent thousands of troops and plentiful supplies of weapons to support Putin’s four-year invasion.

World.title: Lebanon ends executions: Where does the death penalty still exist in 2026?
World.content:
Three-quarters of the world has abolished the death penalty in law or in practice, according to Amnesty International.

Lebanon has become the first country in the Middle East to abolish the death penalty.

On Tuesday, a majority of the 128-member parliament voted in favour of scrapping capital punishment. Death sentences will be replaced with life imprisonment with aggravated hard labour.

Lebanon has observed an unofficial moratorium on executions since January 2004, but its courts have continued to issue dozens of death sentences.

At the end of 2025, 85 people were facing death sentences, according to the Lebanese Ministry of Justice’s Directorate of Prisons.

Which countries still have the death penalty?

According to the latest Amnesty International report on death sentences and executions, as of December, close to three-quarters of the world’s countries had abolished the death penalty in law or practice, meaning they have not carried out executions for the past 10 years.

Some countries have abolished the death penalty for “ordinary crimes” only, which refers to exceptional crimes such as those committed under military law or those committed in exceptional circumstances

Overall, this includes:

Abolition for all crimes: 113 countries

Abolition for ordinary crimes only: nine countries

Abolition in practice: 23 countries

Retention: 54 countries

The map below highlights where each country stands on capital punishment:

Amnesty International’s monitoring of worldwide use of the death penalty recorded 2,707 executions in 2025, up 78 percent from 1,518 in 2024. Amnesty attributed that spike primarily to executions in Iran, which more than doubled from 972 in 2024 to at least 2,159 in 2025.



Amnesty’s figures exclude what it says are thousands of executions that have been carried out in China. Executions were carried out in 17 countries, consistent with the historical lows seen since 2018.

World.title: Iran refutes Trump’s claim to ‘control’ Hormuz: What’s the latest in talks?
World.content:
Iran declares Hormuz closure until US meets its demands and changes its ‘behaviour’ as global energy prices tick higher.

Iran has refuted President Donald Trump’s claim that Washington has “total control” of the Strait of Hormuz, saying the critical waterway will remain closed until the United States accepts its demands and changes its “behaviour”.

According to the semi-official Tasnim news agency, Mohsen Rezaie, the newly appointed head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, told China’s ambassador to Tehran, Cong Peiwu: “As long as America does not change its behaviour and does not accept Iran’s conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened.”

The Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of global oil and natural gas is shipped during peacetime, has emerged as a key flashpoint in the US-Israel war on Iran, with peace talks stalled until the question of its management is resolved. Iran closed the strait shortly after US-Israeli bombing of Iran began at the end of February.

It currently says it is only talking to Oman, whose territorial waters the strait also passes through, about the future management of the waterway.

Commercial shipping remains severely disrupted in the strait, with attacks on vessels continuing on Tuesday when US forces targeted a vessel they said was headed for an Iranian port, in the Gulf of Oman.

At the same time, six people were killed in a Houthi attack on a Saudi cargo vessel in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, according to Yemeni authorities, in what is being described as the first deaths from Houthi attacks on shipping since the US-Israel war on Iran began.

So, is the war entering another dangerous phase? And is there still a diplomatic route out?

What has Trump said about the Strait of Hormuz?

“We totally control the Strait of Hormuz. We have control over it; nobody else, only us,” Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews on Tuesday.



On the ground, however, the situation is more complicated. United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said shipping remained at reduced levels and attacks and “harassment activity” persisted in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran and the US both maintain blockades in and around it.

Iran, meanwhile, has made clear that it does not intend to reopen the waterway unless Washington meets its demands for the lifting of sanctions, the release of frozen Iranian assets and compensation for attacks, among other things.

Writing on X, Rezaei also demanded an end to the US’s naval blockade on Iranian ports as well as a region-wide ceasefire, including in Gaza and Lebanon.

What has happened in Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb?

A US Navy MH-60 helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles at a Panama-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman after the vessel allegedly attempted to violate the US blockade of Iranian ports, US Central Command (CENTCOM) reported. The strike disabled the ship’s steering gear.

The M/V Vela Nova had ignored warnings before a helicopter fired missiles into its engine room, disabling it, CENTCOM said. The US military did not report any casualties among the crew.

The war has now also spilt into another key maritime passageway in the region, the Bab al-Mandeb at the entrance to the Red Sea off Yemen and Saudi Arabia’s western coast, where the Iran-backed Houthis have been targeting Saudi shipping amid renewed fighting in Yemen. Saudi Arabia has announced a new maritime alliance in a bid to secure the waterway.

On Tuesday, six people were killed in a Houthi attack on a cargo vessel in the strait, Yemeni authorities claimed.

Four crew members on board the Egyptian-owned Tihamah were killed, along with two Yemeni rescuers who were responding to the attack. Ten others were injured. The Houthis have yet to directly comment on the attack.

Later in the day, Houthi-affiliated media reported that the ship was carrying Saudi military equipment.

Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb are both critical maritime chokepoints. Besides the one-fifth of global oil and natural gas trade through Hormuz, about 11 percent of global oil and 8 percent of liquefied natural gas (LNG) trade passes through Bab al-Mandeb.

The conflict has badly affected traffic through the waterways, sending oil prices spiralling.

The number of vessels tracked passing through the Strait of Hormuz fell to a one-week low on Tuesday.

Shipping data from Kpler, cited by the Reuters news agency, showed eight vessels transiting the strait, below the 10-day average of about 12 and the lowest daily tally since August 5. Before the war, about 130 ships passed through the strait daily.

Could open warfare begin again?

The latest attacks in Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb strongly indicate that the conflict is not winding down.



Despite both appearing open to talks last week, the US and Iran have escalated their rhetoric in the past few days.

On Monday, US President Donald Trump said he would demand compensation from Iran for deaths and injuries linked to conflicts and attacks over several decades after Iran last week issued new demands for reparations for the US-Israel war.

However, US media have reported that the country may be running low on weapons, particularly air defence interceptors used in Patriot and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) air defence systems, which could pose a threat to US forces and its allies in the region.

Trump and other US officials have denied this.

Meanwhile, on Tuesday, an Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) adviser said it was developing the capability to conduct operations on “enemy soil”. Until now, Iran has been limited to carrying out strikes on US military assets and energy infrastructure in neighbouring Gulf countries and Jordan.

“We need to be able to move the operations to the enemy’s soil, whenever this is needed and ordered,” he said, according to Iranian state TV.

What’s the latest on Oman-Iran talks for Hormuz?

Last week, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said negotiations with Oman for future management of the Strait of Hormuz, with new shipping lanes, have made progress and are in their “final stages”.

Iran says it is not talking directly to the US about this – only Oman, with which it proposes sharing management of the strait.

On Tuesday, Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said he had heard positive messages from both Tehran and Muscat regarding the reopening of Hormuz.

What are the prospects for a broader US-Iran peace deal?

Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi travelled to Tehran on Tuesday to meet Iranian officials as part of efforts to persuade Tehran to resume negotiations with Washington under the interim Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) brokered by Islamabad and Qatar in June. This is due to expire next week.

The vague wording of the MoU, under which Iran had agreed to keep Hormuz open for at least 60 days, caused it to fall apart because of disagreements about who had control over the strait. Iran then fired on several ships taking a route through the channel that it had not approved.

The visit is Naqvi’s sixth trip to Iran as part of diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war.

On whether any future talks between the longtime foes will succeed, analyst Negar Mortazavi said the key question is whether the escalatory rhetoric from both sides is “opening negotiating positions or actual red lines”.

“If both sides are prepared to compromise, there is still a path towards ending the conflict and reopening the strait,” Mortazavi, senior fellow at the Center for International Policy, told Al Jazeera.

“If they are not, Hormuz could remain restricted and the confrontation risks becoming another prolonged, open-ended conflict in the Middle East.”

World.title: Pogba suffers new injury setback with Monaco future now in doubt
World.content:
Former France and Manchester United star Paul Pogba suffers latest injury setback, sparking rumours about his future with Monaco.

Paul Pogba’s future with Monaco could be in doubt after he suffered another injury setback.

The former Manchester United and Juventus midfielder suffered a new injury to his left thigh on Tuesday during the first day of Monaco’s training camp in England.

The 2018 French World Cup winner suffered the injury as the Ligue 1 club trained at the English national football centre at St George’s Park after beating Liverpool in a friendly on Sunday.

The 33-year-old midfielder was only returning to group training after a long spell of right-knee problems.

Pogba has played only one half of football for Monaco in this preseason.

According to several sources close to the matter, the new injury shows Pogba is some way off the level of fitness required to begin the French league season.

There has been widespread speculation that Monaco have begun talks with Pogba’s representatives about buying the player out of the remainder of his contract, which is set to expire at the end of the new season.

After serving 18 months of a four-year ban for doping, Pogba played just six Ligue 1 matches for Monaco last season, totalling 115 minutes on the pitch.

Pogba started his career with United in the English Premier League before the manager at the time, Sir Alex Ferguson, released the midfielder on a free transfer in 2012 after a dispute with the player’s agent.

Juventus stepped in for the then 19-year-old, and he won four consecutive Serie A titles with them and reached the Champions League final before re-joining United in 2016 for a world record transfer fee at the time of $120.2m.



He returned to Juventus on another free transfer in 2022 before his release in 2024, during his ban. Monaco stepped in to hand the Seine-et-Marne-born player his first taste of senior football in his home country in 2025.

Pogba’s last appearance for France came in 2022, in a 5-0 victory over South Africa in an international friendly. It was the last of his 91 caps, during which he scored 11 goals for the team.

His World Cup-winning moment came with France when they defeated Croatia 4-2 in the final of the Russia 2018 tournament, with Pogba scoring his side’s third goal.

World.title: Trump confirms he switched planes after Nato summit because of possible threat
World.content:
President Donald Trump has confirmed that he secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month due to a possible threat.

"I go by Secret Service and the military. They wanted me to go in a different flight, different plane," Trump told reporters. "I just have to do what they say."

The revelation comes after reports that Trump boarded Air Force One on 8 July in view of television cameras, before hiding in a catering truck to be transported to a military aircraft.

The last-minute switch has raised questions about whether those left on the decoy plane were in danger, but Trump said on Tuesday the jet he boarded instead could have been at "greater risk... because that would be the plane, I think, that they would be more likely to go for".

Officials told the BBC's US partner, CBS News, that the US had detected a credible Iranian threat to fire a missile at the plane. The New York Times reported that US intelligence had information of a person near the Nato summit who had been seen with a shoulder-fired missile.

Journalists and some White House staff on board did not know the US president had been smuggled out as part of an elaborate ruse in response to a possible Iranian threat.

World.title: Trump's dramatic plane swap hints at personal stakes of Iran war
World.content:
"I got him before he got me. They tried twice. Well, I got him first."

That was President Donald Trump's observation, made to ABC correspondent Jonathan Karl, in a phone conversation the day after he launched the US military campaign against Iran in February.

An Israeli airstrike, conducted with US approval and co-ordination, had just killed the Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and other top Iranian leaders â and Trump drew a direct line from that attack to threats and alleged plots the Iranians had made against him in previous years.

Trump has refrained from similar remarks in the ensuing six months of warfare, but Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has echoed the view.

"Iran tried to kill President Trump, and President Trump got the last laugh," he said in March, noting that an unnamed Iranian who he said led an assassination unit had been killed in US strikes.

These comments hint at the personal nature of this war â and the concerns by the president and his security team of the threat Iran still poses to his safety.

Those concerns were dramatically illustrated by this week's revelation that Trump secretly switched to an alternate aircraft on his flight back from the Nato summit in Turkey last month. He left the media and most of the White House staff to depart on the presidential Air Force One 747 jet, which became, essentially, a decoy.

World.title: Woman pulled alive from rubble 36 hours after Colombia quake
World.content:
A 32-year-old woman, who had been trapped under rubble for 36 hours following the 7.4-magnitude quake which shook western Colombia, has been rescued alive.

Daniela Largo was pulled from beneath a collapsed building in the city of Pereira after a 10-hour-long rescue operation.

Firefighters finally managed to reach her via a tunnel they dug below four concrete slabs under which she had been buried.

At least 188 have died in the quake, according to official figures, and hundreds remain missing.

In Pereira, a city in Colombia's coffee-growing region, 79 people are confirmed to have died, the second-highest number after Cali, where 95 are dead, according to figures by the Association of Colombian Capital Cities (Asocapitales).

Largo's mother told AFP news agency that a local resident had heard her daughter cry out for help from beneath the rubble.

Once emergency workers had arrived at the site, they were able to locate Largo with the help of a small camera.

However, her rescue was complicated by the fact that four heavy concrete slabs were blocking the way.

Local firefighters aided by colleagues deployed from the capital, BogotÃ¡, and the disaster response team of the national police force had to dig two tunnels to reach her.

Through one opening, dug from above, they were able to provide Largo with oxygen. But it was only through a second tunnel, dug from below, that they were able to free her.

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella celebrated her rescue on social media, describing it as "news which fills us with hope".

Largo's mother said that "at home, her 12-year-old son is waiting for her".

In Pereira, at least 92 buildings collapsed. Fifteen people are known to be trapped and another 37 have been reported missing, according to Asocapitales.

In Cali, Colombia's third most populous city, more than 200 people remained trapped as of 16:00 local time on Tuesday.

World.title: Israeli settlers besieging Palestinian families in West Bank village
World.content:
Israeli settlers have been besieging two Palestinian families in their homes in the occupied West Bank since Sunday, with the families saying their supplies were running out and rights groups urging the authorities to step in.

On Wednesday Israeli security forces were reported to have withdrawn from the Jewish settler outpost in the village of Qusra near Nablus, following clashes with a crowd of extremist settlers. About a dozen settlers are said to remain at the site.

After the Palestinian homeowners made their initial report to the Israeli army, the first soldiers who arrived at the scene were filmed praying with the settlers.

The Abu Ridi and Hassan families have been posting on social media appealing for help after their water and power supplies were cut off and their food stocks ran low.

The latest developments come as a top UN official told the Security Council in New York on Tuesday that "the West Bank is at breaking point".

All settlements are illegal under international law. Outposts are set up without official Israeli authorisation.

Palestinian security camera footage shows settlers tearing down a wall outside the Abu Ridi family's home on Sunday evening and using the stones to block the road.

This left seven people - including two young girls â unable to leave their homes while other Palestinians could not reach them. They live in what is known as Area B, part of the West Bank under Palestinian administrative control and Israeli security control.

Posting on Facebook, Qusay Abu Ridi said the situation was critical, "especially as we are completely isolated."

He wrote: "We are living in our own home, on our own land, and we are asking for nothing more than the right to live safely and with dignity."

On Monday, Israeli settlers blocked Israeli journalists from the left-leaning Haaretz newspaper from trying to reach the Palestinian properties. The reporters said Israeli soldiers at the scene refused to help them when their car was blocked for two hours. They were told the area was a closed military zone, however the order was not enforced on the settlers.

A day later the Israeli human rights group Yesh Din urgently appealed to the head of the Israeli military's Central Command for the army to protect the besieged residents, evacuate the settlers' outpost and hold the settlers accountable.

Late on Tuesday, a Palestinian ambulance was finally allowed to reach the families, delivering food and taking one child away for medical treatment.

At about the same time, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) put out a statement condemning the establishment of the new outpost. It said that entering and seizing Palestinian homes was "illegal, reprehensible, and unacceptable activity".

When the head of its Central Command, Maj Gen Avi Bluth and other senior officers arrived at the scene early on Wednesday they are said to have met residents and voiced their "grave concern".

Afterwards, Palestinian security camera video shared with the BBC showed confrontations between Israeli soldiers and border police and a large crowd of settlers. The security forces used tear gas and stun grenades.

In other footage, the Israeli forces appear to have confiscated the canopy under which the settlers were sheltering, while leaving their other equipment.

"Border Police forces evacuated the tent and are working to evacuate the civilians who were staying there. The incident is still ongoing," the IDF stated.

It said it was decided that "disciplinary action would be taken against the security personnel involved, who were documented at the site several days ago".

The Palestinian village mayor, Abdel Azim Wadi, told the BBC that local residents had seen "a clear and sustained pattern of targeting Qusra". Last month a newly completed mosque was set on fire with graffiti in Hebrew sprayed nearby.

That settler attack was one of many that followed on from an incident in the Palestinian village of Tal. After Israeli settlers attacked Tal, it triggered an escalation in which six people were killed - four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers â one of whom acted as a security coordinator for a nearby Israeli settlement.

In July, settlers also surrounded a Palestinian home in the village of Jalud, near Qusra, for more than two weeks. Afterwards, the owners fled and settlers took over the property where they remain until now.

"Settler violence has reached unprecedented levels," the UN's Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Ramiz Alakbarov, told the Security Council in a briefing on Tuesday.

He gave what he described as "the sobering human toll" and mentioned that the Nablus Governorate in particular had been hit hard recently by violence.

According to the UN's figures, 76 Palestinians â including 18 children - have been killed in the West Bank this year, by Israeli forces or settlers. At the same time, three Israelis â including one civilian â were killed in confrontations with Palestinians and in an alleged ramming attack by a Palestinian in the West Bank.

Since January 2023, 127 Palestinian communities in the West Bank have experienced full or partial displacement, including 47 that have been entirely displaced, affecting more than 6,390 Palestinians, the UN says.

It has registered that in 2026, about 3,800 Palestinians, nearly half of them children, have been displaced due to settler violence, demolitions and evictions.

Speaking at the UN meeting, Israel's Ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon dismissed the idea that settlements were an obstacle to peace. He said that they would remain and continue to grow as his country had biblical, historic and legal rights to the land.

He said that the Security Council "must understand a simple truth: we are not going anywhere."

World.title: Danube river's low water levels reveal remains of WWII soldiers and motorcycle
World.content:
The bodies of two World War Two German soldiers have been found in Budapest's Danube river, due to record-low water levels after an intense drought.

Found alongside their remains were the identification tags of the two soldiers, a largely intact German army Wehrmacht motorcycle, a wedding ring and a Kuban shield - a combat badge of the Wehrmacht, the German War Graves Commission said.

The remarkable finds have sparked hope that some families could finally discover the fates of their ancestors, more than 80 years on from the war.

"Now begins a puzzle, in which we will try to determine the identity of the two dead," Arne Schrader, of the German War Graves Commission, told German newspaper Bild.

The wreck in the Danube was reportedly discovered on 2 August, when a passersby reported part of the motorcycle protruding from the rocks on the riverbank in downtown Budapest.

The team also found anti-tank mines, leading to the temporary closure of the riverbank as a bomb disposal unit was deployed.

Some of the items found in the river, notably the identification tags and motorcycle, are remarkably well-preserved due to the mixture of harbour sludge and oil found on the river bed, the German War Graves Commission said.

The commission is a German non-profit organisation that searches, recovers and buries the war dead on behalf of the German government.

The motorcycle is thought to be a DKW NZ 350-1 model, the organisation said, which was produced specifically for wartime use from 1944.

The commission added that of the two tags found, one belonged to a Wehrmacht soldier, and the other to a member of the Waffen-SS, which was declared a criminal organisation responsible for war crimes at the Nuremberg Trials.

World.title: Zhu Rongji, who helped turn China into a trading giant, dies at 97
World.content:
Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji, who spearheaded China's entry into global trade and laid the foundation for its explosive growth, has died at the age of 97.

He served in the country's second-highest office from 1998-2003 and played a leading role in securing its entry into the World Trade Organization, opening Chinese factories to the international market and drawing foreign investment.

He was one of the most important economic reformers who moved local tax powers to the central government, closed or privatised failing state firms and promoted home ownership.

Many in China remember him as a tough and pragmatic leader who delivered double-digit growth and wa rarely afraid to speak his mind.

In 1998, he said China was facing "many potential crises that could erupt at any time...

"Ordinary people are discontent about us in many ways. Especially, there is corruption among officials, the gulf between rich and poor and the way some local officials act like tyrants."

He labelled rogue bankers as "half-wits" and said the dams and flood dykes lining the Yangtze River were as "flimsy and porous as tofu dregs".

Under his leadership, which helped stabilise the economy and tackle corruption, China began transforming into a manufacturing powerhouse, leaving behind its status as a Communist outsider.

Though he faced criticism because those reforms also led to 30 million lay-offs over five years, and with huge growth came more inequality.

Chinese state media describe Zhu Rongji's life as one of "revolution, struggle and brilliance".

He was born in the central province of Hunan in 1928 and earned a degree in electrical engineering before joining the civil service.

He joined the Communist Party in 1949, but was purged twice - first after criticising Mao Zedong's economic policies as "irrational" and being labelled a "rightist", and again during the Cultural Revolution.

Zhu was brought back into the fold after Mao's death, and by 1991 had risen to the role of vice-premier in charge of China's economy.

He took the role of premier seven years later.

World.title: Wisconsin result dents winning streak for Democratic Party's left wing
World.content:
David Crowley is projected to have won a primary election to become the Democratic candidate for Wisconsin governor, in a surprise result that dents a winning streak for the party's left wing.

Crowley, the more centrist candidate, has secured a narrow victory over Francesca Hong, according to a projection by the BBC's partner, CBS News.

Anti-establishment Democrats across the US had previously notched up victories that have rattled the party leadership in Washington. That trend continued in another closely-watched Democratic contest in Minnesota.

But in Wisconsin, the governor's race in November will be contested by Crowley and Tom Tiffany, who easily won the equivalent Republican contest.

Crowley, the chief executive officer of the state's Milwaukee County, posted on X to say it was time to "get to work".

He reiterated that his missions were "making life more affordable, strengthening our schools, creating good-paying jobs, and making sure opportunity reaches every corner of our state".

Tiffany, meanwhile, currently serves as a US congressman and has the backing of US President Donald Trump.

He has also highlighted affordability issues, running on a platform that includes lowering taxes, supporting farmers and improving healthcare.

The state's political matchups are expected to be closely fought during November's midterm elections, which have also wider implications for the control of the US Congress.

The Hong-Crowley contest for the Democrats was just one of several closely-watched races that were held on Tuesday, and there was good news elsewhere for those on the party's left wing.

In neighbouring Minnesota, candidate Peggy Flanagan secured the Democratic nomination for the upcoming US Senate race, defeating her more centrist opponent Angie Craig.

Meanwhile, in South Carolina, Darline Graham Nordone advanced to a run-off vote later this month in a special Republican primary for the US Senate which was held following the death of her brother, Senator Lindsey Graham.

She will face off against Democrat Annie Andrews to fill the vacant seat.

World.title: Singapore and S Korea pull Trader Joe's seasoning over poppy seeds
World.content:
Singapore and South Korea have pulled Trader Joe's Everything But the Bagel seasoning from e-commerce platforms because it contains poppy seeds.

While they do not naturally contain opiates, poppy seeds are banned in both countries because they can get contaminated with opiates by fluid in the poppy plant during harvesting.

More than 20 online listings of the popular seasoning have been removed, Singapore's Central Narcotics Bureau said on Wednesday.

Last week, Seoul authorities said the seasoning tested positive for morphine and codeine, which are opiates found in the plant's sap.

Apart from poppy seeds, the product also contains sesame seeds, sea salt, minced garlic and minced onion. It was released by American grocery chain Trader Joe's in 2017.

Authorities in Singapore have urged anyone who has bottles of the seasoning to dispose of them.

"Singapore adopts a strict policy of zero tolerance towards controlled drugs," the narcotics bureau said, according to a CNA report.

"The possession, consumption, importation, exportation, manufacturing and trafficking of any controlled drug, even in trace amounts, is an offence under the Misuse of Drugs Act," it said.

In South Korea, investigators say some people brought the seasoning back home as souvenirs from their overseas trips before listing it for resale.

Some did so without realising it contained controlled substances, while others did so knowingly, according to a report by The Korea Herald.

"Even if a product is legally sold overseas, it may be classified as a narcotic substance or a prohibited import in Korea, so particular caution is required," a police official said.

World.title: #OsunDecides2026: Meet candidates seeking to govern ‘State of the Living Spring’
World.content:
With 13 political parties fielding candidates for Saturday’s governorship election, the race for the Osun State Government House has entered its decisive phase.

Across the state’s 30 local government areas, the candidates are criss-crossing communities, selling their records, programmes and political promises to voters ahead of the poll.

Although 14 candidates were initially on the ballot, barely a week before the election, Adesina Adeyemi-Doro, the candidate of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), withdrew from the contest and endorsed the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji. Mr Adeyemi-Doro will still be on the ballot despite his withdrawal.

The contest has increasingly taken the shape of a three-way battle involving incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party, Mr Oyebamiji of the APC, and Najeem Salaam of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

About 2.4 million people are eligible to vote at the 3,763 polling units, spread across the 332 wards in the 30 councils, for their preferred candidates on Saturday. The voters have a coterie of candidates drawn from different professions and endeavours of life to choose from. Among them are accountants, administrators, social scientists, bankers, economists, entrepreneurs, medical practitioners, estate developers and others.

Here are the 13 candidates on INEC’s list from whom voters will choose who will govern them for the next four years, beginning on 27 November.

Ademola Adeleke (Accord)

Ademola Adeleke, the incumbent governor and former senator, is a businessman and administrator. He was born on 13 May 1960 in Enugu, south-east Nigeria. His mother was Igbo from Abia State, while his father, a former senator, hailed from Ede in Osun State.

Mr Adeleke attended Jacksonville State University, Alabama, United States, where he majored in criminal justice and minored in political science. But after much controversy, he got enrolled at Atlanta Metropolitan State College, also in the US, where he earned a BSc in criminal justice in 2021.

He was executive director of Guinness Nigeria Plc and group executive director of Pacific Holdings Ltd.

Mr Adeleke hails from a political family. His father, Ayoola Adeleke, was a Second Republic senator, representing Oyo East on the platform of the defunct Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN). His late elder brother, Isiaka Adeleke, was the first executive governor of Osun and a former senator, while his younger brother, Adedeji Adeleke, is a businessman and founder of Adeleke University.

The governor is also the uncle of Nigerian musician David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido.

Mr Adeleke became governor in 2022 after defeating the incumbent, Gboyega Oyetola, in a keenly contested election. He secured 403,371 votes to Oyetola’s 375,027 and won in 17 of the state’s 30 local government areas.

The victory was particularly significant because Messrs Adeleke and Oyetola had previously faced each other in the 2018 governorship contest, which Mr Oyetola won by a very narrow margin.

Before becoming governor, the 66-year-old represented Osun West District in the Senate from 2017 to 2019. His entry into electoral politics was also closely linked to the influence of the Adeleke family.

The family connection remains an important part of his political identity.

Mr Adeleke’s political rise has therefore combined personal popularity, family name recognition and grassroots mobilisation.

Bola Oyebamiji (APC)

Bola Oyebamiji, aged 60, popularly known as AMBO, is a banker, economist, public administrator and politician from Ikire in Irewole Local Government Area of Osun State.

Mr Oyebamiji holds an OND and HND in banking and finance from The Polytechnic, Ibadan, Oyo State and later obtained a master’s degree in Public Administration from Lagos State University.

He bagged another master’s degree in Business Administration from the University of Ado-Ekiti.

He is also a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Bankers.

His career spans the private and public sectors. He worked in the banking industry before moving into government and became the managing director of the Osun State Investment Company, now associated with Omoluabi Holdings.

He subsequently served as Commissioner for Finance under the administrations of former Governor Rauf Aregbesola and his successor, Gboyega Oyetola. His long involvement in managing the state’s finances has made fiscal management a central component of his political profile.

His public-service career later extended beyond Osun. President Bola Tinubu appointed him managing director and chief executive officer of the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA) in 2023. He resigned from the position in November 2025 to pursue the governorship race.

His political profile is also closely connected to the APC establishment in Osun. His years in government under Messrs Aregbesola and Oyetola place him within the political structure that controlled the state before Adeleke’s victory in 2022.

Najeem Salaam (ADC)

Najeem Salaam, 61, hails from Ejigbo. The man, popularly called “Iwaloye,” holds a doctorate in political science from the Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife.

He is an author, having co-authored a book, Rudiments of Government and Politics. It is a textbook used by students studying government and politics.

The ADC candidate is a former Speaker of the Osun State House of Assembly and a long-standing grassroots politician. He served as Speaker during the administration of former Governor Rauf Aregbesola and became a prominent figure within the progressive political bloc in Osun.

Mr Salaam’s emergence is significant because he represents a third political platform in a race otherwise dominated by the rivalry between Mr Adeleke and the APC.

His political strength comes largely from his long experience in Osun politics and his association with Mr Aregbesola, under whom he served as Speaker.

He has promised to prioritise workers’ welfare, education, youth empowerment, security, local enterprise and public confidence in government. He has also made electricity one of the key issues in his campaign, saying he has been engaging investors and stakeholders in the power sector to seek solutions to the state’s electricity challenges.

Olanrewaju Farinloye (AA)

Olanrewaju Farinloye is the candidate of the Action Alliance (AA). At 40, he is among the youngest candidates in the race.

INEC’s final list records his qualifications as the General Certificate of Secondary Education (GCSE) and the Certificate in Commercial and Economic Studies (CCECS). He is contesting alongside his deputy, Fadahunsi Olaniyi.

Olajide Esan (AAC)

Olajide Esan, 39, is one of the youngest candidates in the race. He is an entrepreneur and car dealer and emerged as the African Action Congress (AAC) candidate through a consensus arrangement at the party’s primary in December 2025.

Mr Esan is also a geographer. He studied at Osun State University, where he obtained a degree, and has described his professional interests as including Geographic Information Systems (GIS), spatial analysis and entrepreneurship. He has presented himself as a youth-oriented candidate and is popularly associated with the description “Youth Governor.”

His campaign has focused on economic diversification, agriculture, mining, and technology, as well as reducing the state’s dependence on federal allocations. His deputy is Bello Yekeen.

Yemisi Opawoye (ADP)

Yemisi Opawoye is the African Democratic Party (ADP) candidate and the only woman in the governorship race.

INEC records her qualification as a Bachelor of Education. She spent her professional life as an academic and is a retired school principal.

At 84, she is also the oldest candidate on the final list. Her candidacy adds an unusual dimension to the race, given both her age and experience in education.

She is paired with 43-year-old Atanda Babatunde as the deputy governorship candidate.

Adewale Adebayo (APM)

Adewale Adebayo is a prominent real estate developer and CEO of Tri Edge Real Estate.

He studied the mechanics of public administration and economic policy and is a former chairman of the Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) in Osun State.

He served as the immediate past Osun State Chairman for the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), managing state-level party structures and grassroots organisation. In June, Mr Adebayoe received the endorsement of former Osun Governor Olagunsoye Oyinlola and members of the Kabiru Turaki-led faction of the Peoples Democratic Party in the state.

Jimoh Naheem is his deputy governorship running mate.

Clement Adesuyi (APP)

Clement Adesuyi is the governorship candidate of the Action Peoples Party. He emerged as the party’s candidate in December 2025 after being the sole aspirant at the party’s primary. He secured the affirmation of 39 delegates.

His manifesto is centred on the promise of transforming the state through investment in youth empowerment, health, education and infrastructure.

Masilo Adeleke (BP)

Masilo Adeleke is the Boot Party candidate.

He is a graduate of the University of Ilorin and contested the 2023 senatorial election but lost.

The party selected Aresa Adenike as its running mate

Taofeek Adeleke (NNPP)

Taofeek Adeleke is the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) candidate known for advocating inclusive governance, human-centred leadership, and grassroots development.

His campaign has placed considerable emphasis on education, healthcare, security and infrastructure. In July, he described education as one of the foundations of sustainable development and said his campaign was built around an “Education for All” message.

He is contesting alongside Adeyera Adesola as his running mate.

Saliu Oyelami (PRP)

Saliu Oyelami, popularly known as Orisunlagba, is the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) candidate.

He is a medical doctor with more than two decades of experience in medical practice. His professional career has included work at Osogbo Muslim Hospital and the University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital, as well as medical practice in Taraba State.

Mr Oyelami is also the chief medical director of Shifauk Hospital Group.

His educational background includes studies at the University of Ilorin and the International University of Africa in Khartoum, as well as training in journalism at the International Institute of Journalism in Abuja.

The PRP candidate was a prominent governorship aspirant under the Action Democratic Party (ADP) in 2018, but he stepped down for another candidate before the final ballot.

In 2022, he also contested the Osun State gubernatorial election as the candidate for the New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP).

His running mate is Adewale Solomon.

Olalekan Ogunsakin (YPP)

Olalekan Ogunsakin is the Young Progressives Party candidate, with Taye Oyetola as his running mate.

Outside of politics, he describes himself as an accomplished Nigerian-American physician-scientist, pathologist, board-certified toxicologist, and medical educator.

He earned a medical degree from Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU) in Ile-Ife, Nigeria, with a focus on healthcare awareness.

He also obtained a PhD from Tulane University School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine, specialising in pulmonary system research and earning the prestigious Tulane 34 award.

Olufemi Adesuyi (ZLP)

Olufemi Adesuyi is the Zenith Labour Party candidate, with Abdulsalam Olamide as his running mate.

He is a registered building contractor based in Akure, Ondo State. He operates Engr Adefemi Adesuyi Building Contractors, a business specialising in interior and exterior structural detailing, home ceilings, painting, wall screeding, and Plaster of Paris (POP) installations.

What voters are saying

While political parties and candidates are presenting their respective programmes, voters are assessing the contenders based on what they believe each candidate can offer the state.

For Bolanle Waheed, the APC candidate is the strongest among the major contenders because of his perceived relationship with the federal government.

“Among the major candidates contesting the Osun governorship election, I consider the APC candidate the strongest because I believe he has the backing of the President. I think this could give him better access to federal support and opportunities that could benefit Osun State,” Mr Waheed told PREMIUM TIMES.

However, he said the most pressing issue for him is the lack of employment opportunities in the state.

“The biggest issue I want the next governor of Osun State to address is unemployment and the lack of employment opportunities,” he said.

Mr Waheed said the next administration should focus on attracting companies and industries to Osun to create jobs for residents.

“I believe the government should focus on attracting and establishing companies and industries in the state to create more jobs for citizens, as many people are currently unemployed,” he said.

Despite his preference for Mr Oyebamiji, Mr Waheed said the candidate’s association with previous APC administrations gives him some reservations.

“Although the APC candidate has experience from serving in both the Aregbesola and Oyetola administrations, I have some concerns about this,” he said.

“The Oyetola administration was not favourable to many people in Osun State, and since the APC candidate was part of that administration, I am not completely convinced that he would do much differently from his former boss.

“However, I still think his experience and relationship with the federal government could be useful if he genuinely prioritises job creation and economic development.”

For Biodun Ogunlana, however, the incumbent governor remains the strongest candidate.

“Among the major candidates contesting the Osun governorship election, I consider Ademola Adeleke the strongest,” Mr Ogunlana told PREMIUM TIMES.

He attributed Mr Adeleke’s advantage to incumbency, name recognition and his grassroots network.

“On incumbency and popularity, Adeleke is widely seen as having the advantage of incumbency, name recognition and a strong grassroots base, especially in Osun West,” he said.

“He defeated an incumbent in 2022, which is often cited as evidence of his electoral strength.”

World.title: NDPC begins forensic probe of UNILAG, Lotus Bank, Hackerbella over alleged unlawful use of students’ data
World.content:
The Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) has commenced a forensic investigation into the University of Lagos (UNILAG), Lotus Bank and Hackerbella Ltd following public complaints alleging the use of students’ personal data to open bank accounts without a lawful basis.

The investigation was disclosed in a statement signed by the commission’s Head, Legal, Enforcement and Regulations, Babatunde Bamigboye, on Wednesday.

According to the statement, Vincent Olatunji, the National Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer of the Commission, directed the investigation team to undertake a comprehensive assessment of the circumstances surrounding the collection, use and disclosure of the affected students’ personal data.

The investigation also aims to assess the roles and responsibilities of each party involved, according to NDPC.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Olatunji also directed the investigation team to assess the general data protection compliance obligations of the parties in line with the provisions of the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (NDP Act), and the potential risks posed to the rights and freedoms of the affected data subjects.

The investigation will, among other things, cover Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs); the lawfulness and transparency of any credit-scoring or profiling activities; the use of automated decision-making systems; and the adequacy of privacy notices.

It will also cover the assessment of data-sharing arrangements; lawful bases for processing; data minimisation; purpose limitation; retention policy; and appropriate technical and organisational safeguards for data subjects’ rights.

“The NDPC reiterates that institutions entrusted with the personal data of students, staff and other members of their communities have a heightened responsibility to ensure that such data is processed lawfully, fairly, transparently and securely,” the statement read.

NDPC further warned Nigerian tertiary schools and other educational institutions that are yet to comply with its existing data protection compliance directives to do so immediately.

World.title: Senate gives Seplat Energy, others 48-hour deadline
World.content:
The Senate has issued a 48-hour ultimatum to Seplat Energy, Network E&P Nigeria Ltd and other oil firms to appear before its Public Accounts Committee.

The directive followed the companies’ failure to attend Tuesday’s investigative hearing in Abuja to answer audit queries contained in reports reviewed by lawmakers.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that other companies handed the ultimatum include All Grace Energy Ltd and Aradel Energy.

The audit queries are contained in the 2021, 2022 and 2023 reports submitted by the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Chairman of the Senate committee, Abdul Ningi, criticised the absence of the affected companies, describing their conduct as disturbing and unacceptable.

Mr Ningi particularly faulted a letter from one company, which reportedly argued that the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) remained its sole regulator.

He said the position reflected a misunderstanding of the Senate’s constitutional oversight powers and obligations under Nigeria’s democratic framework.

“The Senate and, by extension, the National Assembly, is the custodian of Nigerian law and has power to invite anybody or agency,” Senator Ningi said.

He added that Sections 88 and 89 of the 1999 Constitution empowered lawmakers to summon individuals, organisations and agencies for explanations on public matters.

Another senator, Shehu Kaka urged the committee to invoke its constitutional powers against the defaulting firms if they continued to ignore invitations.

“Having failed to honour invitation of this committee two consecutive times, the Managing Director of Network E&P Nigeria Ltd and others must appear.

“They should appear before us unfailingly on Thursday this week or risk the full invocation of legislative powers against them,” Mr Kaka said.

Dubri Oil defends reported $3.25 million debt

Meanwhile, Dubri Oil Company Ltd appeared before the committee and defended a reported $3.25 million royalty and gas flare debt.

A representative of the company, Soyode Olusoji, said the debt arose from reconciliation issues between Dubri Oil and NUPRC.

According to him, the audit report was prepared while discussions and reconciliations between both parties were still ongoing.

NAN reports that NEITI alleged, based on information submitted by NUPRC in 2025, that Dubri Oil owed $3.25 million.

The audit report listed $2.378 million as gas flare liabilities and $646,605.55 as debts linked to oil production activities.

Mr Olusoji told the committee that the reconciliation process had since been concluded and no outstanding debt remained against Dubri Oil.

He submitted supporting documents to lawmakers and requested a thorough review before any decision was taken on the query.

The committee assured that all documents presented would be examined as part of its ongoing investigation into the audit findings.

World.title: Osun 2026: Police bar Amotekun, vigilantes, hunters, CJTF from election security operations
World.content:
The Nigeria Police Force has barred Amotekun, vigilante groups, hunters, the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF) and other community-based security outfits from participating in security operations during Saturday’s governorship election in Osun State.

The directive prohibits the groups from escorting election materials, guarding polling units, mounting checkpoints or carrying arms as part of election security, with the police warning that anyone who deploys or sponsors unauthorised security outfits for the poll will be arrested and prosecuted.

The directive was contained in a statement issued on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, by the Force Public Relations Officer, Ani Iniedu, as security agencies intensify preparations for the 15 August election.

“The Western Nigeria Security Network (Amotekun), vigilante groups, the Joint Civilian Task Force (CJTF), hunters’ associations, community-based security groups, neighbourhood watch outfits, and all other non-state or quasi-security formations have no role in election security, including escorting materials, guarding polling units, mounting checkpoints, or bearing arms,” the statement read.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The police said only authorised security agencies would participate in the joint election security operation across the state’s 30 local government areas.

According to the statement, the authorised agencies are the Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Nigeria Immigration Service, Nigeria Correctional Service and Federal Road Safety Corps.

It added that the deployment will cover polling units and collation centres, as well as the movement and protection of electoral materials, election officials, voters, observers and journalists.

No to unofficial security outfits

The police specifically warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against engaging, arming or deploying unofficial security outfits during the election.

“Political parties, candidates, and the public are warned against engaging, arming, or deploying any non-state security outfit for election-related purposes. Any member or sponsor of such unauthorised outfits will be arrested and dealt with according to the law,” the statement added.

The directive comes amid heightened tension in Osun State ahead of the election, with the state recording a series of killings, shootings and clashes involving political supporters and other groups during the build-up to the poll.

The police said the restrictions were intended to ensure that election security remains under the control of recognised security agencies and prevent individuals or groups from taking the law into their own hands.

Warnings

It also warned that firearms and other dangerous weapons would not be allowed around polling units and collation centres, except where they are lawfully carried by accredited security personnel deployed for election duties.

It said ballot snatching, voter intimidation, vote buying, clashes between rival supporters, thuggery, obstruction of electoral officials, unlawful possession of electoral materials, hate speech and incitement to violence would not be tolerated.

ALSO READ: Amnesty International seeks adequate security during Osun election

The police said perpetrators and sponsors of such offences would be arrested and prosecuted regardless of their political affiliation or status.

The IGP consequently directed officers and commanders deployed for the election to remain professional, impartial and firm while respecting human rights and the rule of law.

The Force also appealed to traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil society organisations, journalists and accredited election observers to report suspicious movements or activities to security agencies.

It assured residents and other stakeholders that security agencies would provide a safe environment for voters to exercise their franchise without intimidation.

World.title: Police detain armed robbery suspect, recover pistol
World.content:
The police command in Enugu State has detained a 26-year-old male armed robbery suspect, recovered a locally-made pistol and a live cartridge in a citizen-supported operation.

Daniel Ndukwe, the police spokesman in Enugu State, in a statement on Tuesday in Enugu, said the citizen-supported operation took place at Obollo Etiti in Udenu Local Government Area of the state.

Mr Ndukwe, a superintendent of police, said the detention followed receipt of a credible information on 10 August at about 1: 45p.m., alerting police to the suspicious activities of a young man who had arrived at a hotel, purportedly to lodge.

He noted that acting on the information; the suspect’s bag was searched, leading to the recovery of the locally-made pistol and live cartridge.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The spokesman said the suspect was immediately detained and taken into custody alongside the recovered exhibits.

“During preliminary interrogation, the suspect confessed to being a member of an armed robbery gang that specialised in threatening and robbing POS operators of their valuables.

“He also said that his gang members fled the scene upon his arrest. The suspect will be prosecuted in court upon the conclusion of investigations,” he said.

ALSO READ: Police arrest armed robbery suspect, recover firearms

Mr Ndukwe quoted the state Commissioner of Police, Mamman Giwa, as commending the resident who provided the timely information.

The commissioner reiterated the importance of providing the police with credible information on suspicious persons and activities.

He assured residents that efforts were ongoing to identify and detain the gang members that fled, while investigations continue.

(NAN)

World.title: COUP SERIES ROUND-UP: What we know about alleged failed plot against Tinubu
World.content:
Many Nigerians were quick to dismiss last year’s failed coup plot to topple the President Bola Tinubu administration as a ruse. Scanty information from the authorities, at best, painted only a hazy picture.

Others who considered it probable scrambled for details but only got more puzzling questions than answers.

Whether attempted, aborted or successful, coups are steeped in Nigeria’s history, leaving lasting impressions on its landscapes, and considerably shaping its trajectory. After 30 years’ break, another coup suddenly looming on the horizon last year jolted many who were conscious of its historical significance and implications for the nation’s future.

The news about the plot first emerged in October 2025 following the arrest of a group of serving and retired officers in late September. The Defence Headquarters initially described the arrests as part of a “routine internal process” to maintain discipline and professionalism in the military. It later acknowledged that the officers were being investigated over an alleged coup plot.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

When the military finally admitted the plot publicly, only little more than what the public knew through scoops was said. Some more details emerged when some suspects were charged and their trials began at the General Court Martial and the Federal High Court in Abuja, but stubborn questions persisted.

Over 17 days, PREMIUM TIMES rolled out a series of detailed exclusive reports on the plot, uncovering missing pieces of the coup puzzle.

Starting from 25 July to 10 August , this newspaper published a 16-part series, drawing on about 7,400 pages of investigation records, including statements by suspects, bank records, secret notes, chat exchanges, receipts, hotel records and other exhibits.

These reports painted vivid mental images, chronicling for the first time an unbroken line of events – from the conception of the alleged plot to its collapse in September – about the alleged coup.

In sum, the PREMIUM TIMES series revealed the events, key actors, and networks, offering the most detailed account of the plot yet.

From poring over the piles of documents and reporting them in the series, PREMIUM TIMES has endeavoured to provide details of the alleged conspiracy from the accounts of the participants, offering answers to some nagging questions those concerned about the plot have asked for months.

The alleged mastermind and coup motivations

At the centre of the alleged conspiracy was Mohammed Ma’aji, a Nigerian Army colonel who had served in many military formations.

Investigators identified him as the principal coordinator of the plot. His own account as contained in the documents exclusively obtained by this newspaper provides perhaps the clearest explanation of how he came to contemplate overthrowing the government.

Mr Ma’aji said he had twice failed in his bid for promotion to brigadier general—first in 2023 and again in 2024. He said the disappointment contributed to his decision to revive a movement to change the government.

But he also presented the proposed coup as a response to insecurity, pervasive corruption in the country, bad governance, suppression of critical voices of the youth, bad governance, what he considered the poor welfare and working conditions of serving and retired military personnel. He claimed that widespread frustration existed within the armed forces and that the desire for change was genuine.

He wrote of how he incessantly came under pressure from those he called “like minds” within the military.

However, some of the allies offered a less flattering picture of the man.

One officer told investigators that Mr Ma’aji’s alleged relationships with women and his reliance on Islamic clerics and traditional spiritualists made him question whether the colonel possessed the character and judgement required to lead a country. Another participant eventually dismissed him as a “joker” because of his failure to deliver on logistics for the execution of the plot.

Mr Ma’aji was eventually arrested on 29 September 2025 after military authorities allegedly used his long-running promotion ambition as bait. He said he was summoned to meet the then Chief of Army Staff, Olufemi Oluyede, about his promotion and arrived at Niger Barracks believing his career prospects were finally being addressed. But that was the last time he would walk freely.

Why did they want to overthrow Tinubu?

The documents suggest a mixture of personal frustration, military grievances and dissatisfaction with the government as the motivations behind the coup plot.

Mr Ma’aji told investigators that insecurity and the condition of military personnel were among his motivations. His secret notes also show that he wanted a future military government to address what he saw as shortcomings of the Tinubu administration.

The alleged conspirators were particularly interested in the removal of petrol subsidy, which has contributed to the persistent cost of living crisis in the country.

A handwritten document recovered from Mr Ma’aji contained an “Immediate Actions” section proposing a committee to review the fuel subsidy removal, review salaries and wages of military and security personnel, and a mechanism for giving national recognition to fallen military heroes.

For years, military operatives—particularly the junior ranks who constitute the larger percentage of the country’s frontlines—have lamented about poor welfare. Many of them have taken their grievances to social media, actions that were met with condemnation by military authorities.

In what could not be directly associated with the coup plotters’ concerns, Mr Tinubu reviewed soldiers’ salaries, approving up to an 80 per cent increase.

The series also revealed motivational writings kept by Mr Ma’aji, including quotations about courage, success, dreams and the pursuit of goals.

How the coup was supposed to happen

Investigators believed the alleged conspirators had developed an operational plan for the execution of their alleged plot.

The conspirators allegedly divided responsibilities among military officers and civilians. They also purchased vehicles suspected to be meant for use for the operation. Targets included the Presidential Villa, military formations, the residences of senior military commanders, Radio House, Air House and airports.

One officer was allegedly assigned to lead the operation at Aso Villa, while others were tasked with seizing military formations and securing strategic locations. Another was expected to take control of Radio House and deliver a broadcast announcing the takeover.

The alleged conspirators also used coded language. They referred to themselves as “farmers” and the movement as “farming”. While logistics were coded as “fertilisers,” the operation was “digital farming,” clerics were “technical partners,” and the execution day was “harvest.”

Proposed execution dates

There was no final date for the alleged coup when the plot was uncovered.

Three dates repeatedly appeared in the accounts of alleged participants: 27 September, 1 October and 4 October 2025.

In his statement to military interrogators, Mr Ma’aji mentioned “a month after” 1 October, as another “possible D-Day,” the day of execution.

One of Mr Ma’aji’s allies, Abdulkarim Ibrahim, a major, also told interrogators that Mr Ma’aji “mentioned that the availability of troops and equipment would determine which of the dates would be D-Day.”

The proposed execution time, which was referred to as “H-hour,” was between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m., which one suspect said was consistent with the timing of previous military takeovers.

Mr Ma’aji maintained that “no specific day was agreed” yet.

The final date was to depend on the availability of troops, weapons and other logistics.

The significance of 1 October was heightened by the cancellation of Nigeria’s Independence Day parade in 2025. One suspect later admitted mocking President Tinubu over the cancellation without knowing that the authorities were already closing in on the alleged plot.

Logistics and manpower

The alleged conspirators understood that taking over the government would require more than a few officers.

The documents show plans to mobilise troops, gun trucks, ammunition, vehicles and other equipment from different military formations.

Some officers, including Shamsudeen Bappah, a lieutenant colonel, allegedly assured Mr Ma’aji that they could provide troops and equipment.

Mr Ma’aji said the use of Improvised Explosive Device (IED) was suggested to him, but that he ruled it out. He said “it was Maj Iliyasu who said he had some Boko Haram technicians working in the theater to make IED, but I told him that it was not necessary.”

Airports were also considered critical because the conspirators allegedly believed flights had to be stopped during the takeover. The plan included disrupting flight operations in Abuja and Lagos, and two officers were assigned this task: a Nigerian Air Force squadron leader, Noel Zuzu (Abuja) and Sunday Felix, a lieutenant (Lagos).

They also explored recruiting members of the Civilian Joint Task Force and repentant Boko Haram fighters in the North-east. The idea was attractive because some of these people had operational experience and access to weapons through counter-insurgency activities. Ma’aji said the idea originated from Major Ilyasu.

Money, sponsors and Timipre Sylva

One of the biggest revelations was the alleged financing network.

Mr Ma’aji told investigators that former Bayelsa State governor and former Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Timipre Sylva, was the principal financier.

Based on the records reviewed by PREMIUM TIMES, the interrogators believed that more than N5 billion was allegedly pooled in an account connected to the financing of the plot, while N785 million was allegedly transferred for execution before the conspiracy collapsed.

The funds allegedly moved through Purple Waves Limited and a bureau de change operator, who then disbursed money to people identified by Mr Ma’aji. Investigators alleged that some of the money came from proceeds linked to a Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) contract and loans obtained by Purple Waves.

PREMIUM TIMES found from the documents that the transfers of about N474.7 million had been disbursed to individuals and entities by the time the alleged plot was uncovered. These funds transfers took place from 10 to 30 September 2025, coming close to the two of the furthest dates insiders proposed to launch the coup strike.

The money was allegedly used to support participants performing different roles and purchases of items needed for the planning and execution.

Among the alleged recipients were military officers, civilians and Islamic clerics. One officer assigned to the Presidential Villa allegedly received N10 million, while another assigned to airport-related operations allegedly received N5 million.

A retired naval captain, Erasmus Victor, also told investigators that Mr Ma’aji asked him to approach wealthy individuals for financial support.

He said names including FCT Minister Nyesom Wike were mentioned, but he claimed he never approached any potential sponsor and instead told Mr Ma’aji that they had declined.

Mr Victor likely first became acquainted with Mr Wike when he served as the chairman of the Ogu/Bolo Local Government Area of Rivers State between 2018 and 2021 while Mr Wike was the governor.

Spiritual backing

The alleged plot was not entirely built around guns, troops and money.

The investigation records show that Mr Ma’aji allegedly sought the support of Islamic clerics for spiritual protection and prayers.

One cleric, Goni Bukar, was allegedly paid about N50 million in several installments. The records described the payments as being for spiritual support for the alleged operation.

For some participants, the alleged mastermind’s reliance on spiritualists and clerics became a source of concern rather than confidence.

Mr Bappah told investigators that Mr Ma’aji’s involvement with people he called “Malams” contributed to his doubts about the plot.

Could the execution have been violent?

It was clear from the statements of suspects that the suspected coupists intended to make the execution of the alleged plot as bloodless as possible.

Mr Ibrahim, the Army major who wrote in his statement to interrogators that he was assigned the task of making a nationwide broadcast after the alleged coupist’s anticipated takeover, said he cautioned Mr Ma’aji against any bloodshed.

He argued that history had shown successful coups generally relied on securing the cooperation of senior officers rather than eliminating them. Abulrahman Hayatu, a lieutenant-colonel, another insider, was also said to have opposed killing anyone.

Their operational blueprint gleaned from the suspected participants’ statements included interrupting flights, arresting top military officers at home and switching off the Presidential Villa’s power supply to sneak in seamlessly to make arrests.

But Mr Umoru, a Julius Berger Nigeria Plc employee in the Maintenance Department at the Presidential Villa, said he warned that such a sudden power outage would trigger investigations and the detention of workers on duty.

From Mr Umoru’s account, the level of force the alleged coup plotters planned to deploy was dependent on how much Villa insiders’ cooperation they could secure.

Mr Umoru, who shared his own perspective about the planned raid on the Villa in his videoed interrogation session played back in court, said after warning Mr Ma’aji that a sudden power outage at the presidential villa would trigger investigations and the detention of workers on duty, he said the alleged coup leader concluded that he might enter the Villa with force if the insiders failed to cooperate.

Also, the contemplation of the alleged coup planners to recruit Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF) and repentant Boko Haram fighters to support operation during the coup execution meant the end result was unpredictable.

Repentant Boko Haram members and operatives of CJTF, a state-backed militia established to assist security forces in counter-insurgency operations in the North-east, could create a challenge of control for the alleged coup leaders, who were desperately looking for manpower, arms and logistic support.

Bringing them into the plot, meant the alleged coup could take a life of its own as the ragtag group brought for support could go about the operation as they liked.

Propaganda and manufacturing public support

The alleged planners understood that military control alone would not make a new government legitimate.

They therefore allegedly planned a propaganda operation to create the impression that Nigerians welcomed the takeover.

A veteran Nollywood actor, Stanley Amandi, told investigators that he was asked to coordinate public support across the South-east if the takeover succeeded.

His alleged assignment included organising celebrations and engaging social media influencers to spread messages supporting the new government. He was also asked to prepare a budget for the mobilisation.

The plan therefore extended beyond the seizure of government facilities. It allegedly envisaged a parallel information operation designed to influence how Nigerians perceived the takeover.

Who would run the new government?

The conspirators allegedly did not stop at planning the takeover. They discussed what would happen afterwards.

Mr Ma’aji was expected to become Head of Government if the operation succeeded. Other participants were allegedly promised positions. Ilyasu Jamilu, a major, wanted to become an aide-de-camp; Mr Felix was promised a ministerial position, while Mr Bappah requested to head the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

A proposed takeover broadcast was also being prepared.

The alleged regime’s first actions were contained in Ma’aji’s handwritten notes: review fuel subsidy removal, review salaries and wages of military and security personnel, and honour fallen military personnel.

How they communicated

The alleged conspirators were conscious that ordinary telephone calls could expose them, so they used encrypted platforms like WhatsApp and Zangi.

WhatsApp was used for some communications, but many of them said Mr Ma’aji also introduced Zangi, a messaging application considered more secure.

Retired naval captain Victor told investigators that he downloaded Zangi specifically to communicate with Mr Ma’aji and another officer.

The investigators’ examination of these digital communications became part of the evidence used to reconstruct the relationships, discussions and roles within the alleged network.

Doubts, hesitation and regret

Perhaps the most revealing thread running through the 16 reports is that not everyone involved appeared convinced that the coup would succeed.

Some participants said they questioned Mr Ma’aji’s ability to raise money or provide the logistics required for the operation.

Bayawo Abdullahi, a naval lieutenant commander, said he became so sceptical that he stopped responding to Mr Ma’aji’s messages. Yet he later regretted not reporting the plan to authorities.

Mr Victor, who is among six persons facing charges stemming from the alleged coup plot at the Federal High Court in Abuja, said he repeatedly advised Mr Ma’aji against the coup. He added that he also counselled Mr Ma’aji to retire from the military if securing a promotion continued to prove hard. He said further that at one point he suspected that the whole scheme might be a fraud designed to defraud wealthy people, knowing that the victims would not be able to report to authorities.

Mr Bappah said Mr Ma’aji’s alleged promiscuity and reliance on Islamic clerics and spiritual practices caused him to question his ability to lead Nigeria.

Yet several of those who expressed doubts still attended meetings, received money or remained silent.

Alleged conspirators’ recommendations to prevent future coup attempt

Beyond the proposed military takeover, the documents reveal what some of the alleged conspirators believed Nigeria needed.

Mr Ma’aji’s recommendation was elaborate. The disgruntled officer, among other things, called for improved welfare, better education, reversal of fuel subsidy removal and elimination of godfatherism in the military, corruption and budget padding.

Some of them also recommended a platform where personnel can present their concerns without fear of being targeted by senior officers.

But these proposals were attached to a plan to overthrow an elected government rather than pursue change through constitutional means.

Investigation continues

The 16 reports do not establish a completed coup. Rather, they reveal an alleged conspiracy that authorities say was disrupted before execution.

Several suspects are facing prosecution before the General Court-Martial and the Federal High Court in Abuja.

Importantly, defendants before the Federal High Court have challenged the admissibility of their extrajudicial statements and video exhibits, arguing that they were obtained in circumstances that violated legal safeguards. The prosecution has urged the court to admit the evidence.

The allegations against individuals named in the reports therefore remain subject to judicial determination.
