World.title: Iraq Transport Ministry reports 95% completion of Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani met with the Parliamentary Transport and Communications Committee on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to review execution milestones across strategic infrastructure projects, including the Development Road, the Grand Fao Port, and national rail modernization.

During the executive session, Al-Hasani presented technical updates on the 1,200-kilometer Development Road Project, confirming that primary design phases are near completion, with railway engineering blueprints reaching 95% and highway transit designs at 85%.

Key Operational Metrics & Project Milestones

Development Road Project: Designs for the 1,200 km transit corridor are nearly complete (95% for railway tracks, 85% for highways). The MOU executed with Turkey serves as a preliminary framework with no current financial or legal obligations.

Grand Fao Port: Submerged tunnel construction reached 86% completion, alongside advanced structural work across five main container berths.

Rail Network Modernization: Ministry teams are actively pursuing the rehabilitation of the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia railway corridor extending toward the Syrian border.

Maritime Fleet Mobilization: State maritime companies confirmed readiness to deploy Iraqi vessels to transport crude oil and refined petroleum products to support alternative national export strategies.

Administrative & Executive Actions: Al-Hasani confirmed the suspension of Iraqi Airways’ former Director-General and two deputies following an internal investigative audit.

Legislative Alignment: Agreement reached to draft amendments to Transport Law No. 80 of 1983 and establish a joint parliamentary-executive committee holding weekly meetings to update transport regulations.

The meeting highlights Iraq’s strategy to transform into a central logistics bridge connecting the Gulf to Europe, bypassing maritime transit chokepoints.

By pairing the Grand Fao Port’s advancing infrastructure with overland rail links extending north to Turkey and west through the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia line toward Syria, the Ministry of Transport is laying the groundwork for integrated commercial supply chains across Eurasia.

World.title: MP Abdul Jabbar proposes 145 km pipeline to boost Basra crude to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Independent MP and Secretary-General of the Fao–Zakho Coalition, Amer Abdul-Jabbar, proposed a plan on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to construct a 145-kilometer oil pipeline link to transport Basra crude north toward Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal.

Abdul-Jabbar stated via social media that the proposed missing link would instantly increase Iraq’s northern export capacity by 150,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd). To avoid drawing on the federal budget during the ongoing liquidity crisis, he advocated launching a “National Volunteer Effort,” utilizing surplus piping from state-owned enterprises alongside logistical backing from private contractors operating under Ministry of Oil contracts.

Key Technical & Strategy Highlights

Proposed Pipeline Link: A 145 km strategic bypass connecting southern oilfields in Basra directly to northern export routes toward the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Capacity Increase: Designed to boost crude export flows by 150,000 to 300,000 bpd, mitigating bottlenecks caused by Persian Gulf shipping disruptions.

Zero-Cost Volunteer Framework: Proposed execution via a “National Volunteer Effort” using inventory audits of unused piping across state firms and private sector contractor support.

Existing Ministry Export Strategy: Complements Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair’s August 9 plan to export 750,000 bpd to Ceyhan via: 450,000 bpd pumped through the Strategic Pipeline after rehabilitating the PS3 pump station in Najaf and K3 in Haditha. 300,000 bpd transported via road tankers (including 200,000 bpd through KAR Group and 100,000 bpd under a secondary contract).

Long-Term Iraqi-Turkish Energy Framework: Ministry of Oil is finalizing a 1-year interim agreement with Ankara, paving the way for a 10- to 20-year strategic partnership involving Turkish BOTAŞ and BP in developing Kirkuk oilfields.

Abdul-Jabbar’s proposal comes as the Ministry of Oil accelerates alternative land-based export channels to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Minister Khudair previously confirmed that Iraq’s State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) and Turkey’s BOTAŞ are actively inspecting and rehabilitating the northern export system to handle between 500,000 and 750,000 bpd. Implementing the 145 km bypass link could offer Baghdad an immediate, low-cost mechanism to restore crude cash flows while long-term pipeline infrastructure is constructed toward Syria and Jordan.

World.title: Meta meets its own ‘tobacco’ moment in court
World.content:
Oakland – With billions of users around the world, Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media’s big tobacco moment.

After a coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps, four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.

Top prosecutors of those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.

Meta “strongly disagrees with these allegations” and is “confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people,” a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has “listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement.”

Although it’s not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.

“It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s,” Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley’s Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.

While these cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, just like when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.

By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.

– ‘Protecting teens’ –

Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with s featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as “Joe Camel.”

Jury selection begins today in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco and opening statements are expected to begin August 18.

Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach $1 billion.

In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta’s apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as $1.4 trillion, close to Meta’s entire market value which hovers around $1.5 trillion.

Despite the eye-popping number, money isn’t Meta’s biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.

“The huge issue here is reputational harm” and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.

“Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning,” as well, he said.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.

The case could be “the beginning of a broader reckoning” for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.

It will be important to see the “gap” between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.

Meta is “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” Meta told AFP last week.

With so many plaintiffs suing Meta and other social media companies, these lawsuits could potentially “go on for decades,” Joralemon said.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.

World.title: Colombia rescuers find woman alive as quake death toll passes 240
World.content:
Pereira – Colombian rescuers pulled a 32-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building Tuesday, sparking cheers and applause as exhausted crews raced to find more survivors from the country’s strongest earthquake in a century.

Daniela Largo was carried from the wreckage wrapped in a blue blanket as rescuers embraced and relatives shouted out with joy.

The rescue came as soldiers, firefighters and volunteers searched collapsed buildings across western Colombia after a 7.4-magnitude quake killed at least 241 people and injured more than 1,600.

“We were losing hope and then we received a call,” said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.

Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

“Thanks to him, today we’re happy,” she said. “At home her 12-year-old son is waiting for her.”

In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.

As darkness fell, families prepared to sleep in parks as aftershocks rattled damaged neighborhoods where entire blocks had been reduced to rubble.

The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia’s largest disaster responses in years.

“The house came down on top of us. I wasn’t able to get out,” said Beatriz Arcos, who was trapped with her husband and mother beneath their collapsed condominium.

“It took about an hour to get us out.” Arcos said she was hospitalized after a concrete block fell on her back. Her husband and mother were also injured.

In Cali, residents armed with picks, shovels and their bare hands joined firefighters in digging through collapsed buildings.

Rescuers stopped every few minutes to call into the rubble and listen for any response.

“We’re doing this with our hands, with gloves” said volunteer Pablo Cesar Ruiz “It’s sad to see time slipping away.”

In Pereira, army units and sniffer dogs combed through twisted concrete and exposed steel.

At one site, a rescue squad leader abruptly raised his fist, stopping workers so they could listen for signs of life.

Volunteers formed human chains, passing bricks and chunks of masonry hand-to-hand to clear paths into collapsed structures.

– ‘So much effort’ –

For many families, the desperate search was becoming a vigil.

“My aunt lived there. She’s under the rubble,” said Jorge Gonzalez, standing beside a collapsed building in Pereira.

“I arrived yesterday and I haven’t left, and until they find her body I don’t intend to leave here.”

While some families waited for news of missing relatives, others were grappling with the loss of homes, possessions and livelihoods.

“We lost everything,” said Stella Galvis, fighting back tears after escaping the collapse of her home.

“We survived by a miracle, since I managed to get my little boy out and my partner managed to get out too.”

From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.

Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.

On one mound of debris, a young couple climbed over broken masonry searching for belongings.

They recovered a box from inside a child’s bright red bedside table.

Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.

One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.

“We lost everything, but we’re alive,” said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.

“We’ve never had to do this before, to depend on someone else to help us. It’s amazing how life can change.”

Others struggled to come to terms with losing homes built over decades.

“You buy a little house with so much effort, spending 40, 50 years struggling to get yourself that house, you finally get it and in just a few days it all goes down the drain,” said 79-year-old Jaime Alzate.

In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.

Yet amid the destruction, many Colombians mobilized to help.

Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.

“It’s about wanting to help your community, your city and your country,” said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.

President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.

As aftershocks continued to rattle damaged cities, rescue crews pressed on through the ruins, hoping more voices, taps or whistles might still emerge.

World.title: Passengers rescued as second ferry in days catches fire in Indonesia
World.content:
Mataram – A navy vessel and other ships rushed in Wednesday to rescue over 100 people from a ferry on fire off the tourist island of Bali, officials said, in the second such incident in days.

There were no immediate reports of casualties among the passengers and crew, with at least 114 people on board, according to the manifest.

The passenger ferry had been sailing from Bali to the next-door island of Lombok when it caught fire in the early morning hours.

Muhamad Hariyadi, head of the search and rescue agency at Mataram on Lombok island, said the total number of passengers on board was being verified.

He said passengers were evacuated on at least three different vessels, including a navy ship and another ferry.

Search and rescue vessels were at the scene and a helicopter was conducting surveillance from the air.

“As of now, we have not received any report of casualties,” Hariyadi told Metro TV.

“We have approached the ship and confirmed that all passengers are no longer on board,” he added. “We visually see no passengers on the ship.”

Last week, five people died when a ferry caught fire off Java island.

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia — an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that rely heavily on boat connections.

Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi, last month.

Four bodies were recovered, but the search operation ended with 14 others still officially missing.

World.title: Charges dropped against Bondi Beach attack hero
World.content:
Sydney – Australian police dropped assault charges on Wednesday against a man lauded for his bravery during last year’s mass shooting at Bondi Beach.

Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed was hailed as a hero after footage showed him disarming a gunman during the December 14 attack, which killed 15 people at a Jewish festival.

Ahmed was earlier this year accused of stalking and assaulting his father, charges he denied.

Both charges were withdrawn after a brief hearing on Wednesday, court documents showed.

Ahmed ducked between parked cars as the Bondi shooting unfolded, grabbing one of the two gunmen and wresting away his weapon in an effort to stop the killing.

He sustained gunshot wounds in the attack.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese would later meet Ahmed in person, describing him as a “true Australian hero” and an inspiration to all.

World.title: Oil prices rise, stocks mixed ahead of crucial US inflation data
World.content:
Hong Kong – Oil prices rose again Wednesday and stock markets were mixed, with eyes on the release of key US inflation data that could guide the Federal Reserve on its plans for interest rates.

Traders trod nervously ahead of the consumer price index (CPI) figures, which follow a report last week showing the world’s top economy lost more than 20,000 jobs last month, suggesting the labour market was slackening.

With inflation stubbornly elevated above the Fed’s two percent target for more than five years — compounded by the Iran war since February — monetary policymakers are increasingly considering lifting borrowing costs.

The bank’s July meeting saw three board members call for an increase, dissenting from the final decision to hold rates, and investors are betting they will announce one before the end of the year, with some eyeing at least two.

Analysts pointed out that there will be one more CPI release and another jobs report before the Fed’s next meeting in September.

The higher oil prices rise, the more traders expect the Fed to tighten, and a lack of progress in talks between the US and Iran on a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is adding upward momentum.

An announcement from Pakistan’s defence minister that the two were “close to some sort of arrangement” provided a sliver of hope Tuesday, though that later faded.

His remarks came after Washington and Tehran had issued demands for compensation over the five-month war, hardening their positions.

Meanwhile, a US helicopter fired missiles on Tuesday into the engine room of a Panama-flagged cargo ship that attempted to break the American blockade of Iran’s ports, the United States military said.

There was also little major reaction to a report that Iran and Oman were in advanced talks on reopening Hormuz to some maritime shipping.

Both main crude contracts rose Wednesday, and have risen around 14 percent in the past week.

“Crude oil prices have surged in the last few days because the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut, and there are no signs of progress between the US and Iran,” wrote Forex.com’s Fawad Razaqzada.

“The latest headlines around talks between Oman and Iran provided some relief, but we shouldn’t confuse talks with an actual breakthrough. Iran has come out saying that the Strait of Hormuz will remain shut until their conditions are met.”

He said the positions of the US and Iran indicated “any potential deal is still some way off, meaning risks remain skewed to the upside for oil prices”.

Equity markets fluctuated ahead of the CPI release, though Seoul enjoyed another strong day as it claws back some of the huge tech-led losses sustained in July.

The Kospi climbed more than three percent, helped by chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung, which bore the brunt of that selloff.

The gains were helped by strong earnings reports from US AI giants CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer that eased worries about the years-long investment boom that has led many observers to question when firms will see a return.

Tokyo, Shanghai, Taipei, Manila and Jakarta also rose, though Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore and Wellington were in the red.

World.title: How difficult is it to become a doctor or an engineer in India?
World.content:
For a very long time, anyone considered particularly good at studies in India was almost automatically tipped to become a doctor or an engineer.

3 Idiots

made a joke of that national fixation years ago, showing a world in which parents and professors seemed convinced they knew what success ought to look like.

Alternative streams of education have slowly gained popularity since then. The race to become a doctor or engineer, however, has hardly become easier. As the pool of aspirants expands beyond the metros, competition for a coveted seat has only become harder. Many tuition centres, almost like factories, in Kota and other places train students rigorously to pass these coveted exams.

The May 3 NEET-UG examination was cancelled after the paper-leak controversy and nearly 20 lakh candidates returned for a re-examination on June 21. The anger travelled from coaching rooms to Ja

r Mantar and towards Parliament, propelled by the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party.

Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister on July 25. The CBI chargesheet has since named 13 accused, including three subject experts associated with NTA, while CJP has demanded that the testing agency itself be replaced. Similar protests over exam leaks have now erupted in Jharkhand.

The anger that erupted at Jantar Mantar after the leak is merely a reflection of the deeper anxiety over competition for quality jobs and the yearning for a stronger CV, which for many begins with studying at a hallowed institution. How difficult, then, is it to get into a top-tier engineering or medical college in India?

The IIT-NIT funnel

Engineering here means the route to the country's most sought-after public engineering institutions, particularly the IITs and NITs, not every engineering college.





The pathways are slightly different. JEE Main is the direct gateway to the 31 NITs participating in JoSAA 2026, while it also acts as the screening stage for candidates hoping to reach the IITs through JEE Advanced.

NTA recorded 15,38,468 unique candidates appearing for JEE Main 2026. Of the 1,87,389 who registered for JEE Advanced, 1,79,694 appeared in both papers and 56,880 qualified. The JoSAA 2026 matrix provides 18,826

seats.

Put another way, the original Main candidate pool is roughly 82 times the number of IIT seats. Even after reaching JEE Advanced, there were 9.5 test-takers and almost exactly three qualifiers for every IIT place.

How competitive is the field

Not every JEE Main candidate is a serious IIT contender, so the 82-to-one comparison is largely academic. It is a measure of the scale of the field, not an individual's admission probability. Seats are allocated across categories and other reservation rules.

But in both IITs and NITs, the fight is not only for a seat, but also for a preferred stream and college.

Interest in admission wanes considerably as one goes down the value chain. That distinction becomes clearer when one looks at the rest of India's engineering system. The latest Rajya Sabha disclosure by the ministry states that BTech/BE enrolment in AICTE-approved institutions rose to 13.56 lakh in 2025-26. Yet adding up the state-wise vacancies in the same annexure produces 2,52,914 empty seats.

In the same year, 67 AICTE-approved engineering and technology institutions applied for closure or were listed as closed.

So India does not lack engineering seats. What it lacks are the seats students value most in IITs, top NITs and other highly sought-after institutions.

What government told in Parliament

The engineering race does not necessarily end with a BTech for all. For those aiming for an MTech from an IIT, NIT or another premier institution, GATE becomes another competitive gate.

The numbers are substantial. In GATE 2026, 2,11,020 candidates appeared for the Computer Science and Information Technology paper, while 95,752 appeared for Electronics and Communication, 76,385 for Civil Engineering and 69,242 for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence.

Those figures cannot simply be converted into applicants-per-MTech-seat ratios. Candidates can sit more than one GATE paper. For NITs, the pool is still broader.

CCMT 2026 accepts valid GATE scores from 2024, 2025 and 2026. So candidates for these seats can effectively be competing with more than one year's GATE cohort. However, suffice to say, the odds are tough for aspirants.

Medicine has its own hierarchy

Medical education runs on the same preference for high-value seats. For the valid June 21 NEET re-examination, 22,79,743 candidates were registered, 19,99,895 appeared and 11,21,185 qualified. The cancellation itself affected the denominator, with 2,79,848 registered candidates not sitting the re-test.

Against this pool, the NMC's July matrix lists 1,36,939 MBBS seats for 2026-27, excluding Institutes of National Importance such as AIIMS. The NEET test-taker pool is about 14.6 times the listed MBBS capacity, while the number of qualified candidates is about 8.2 times the capacity. These are broad national comparisons, not individual admission odds, since seats are divided across quotas, categories and state eligibility rules.

But the headline number conceals another hierarchy.

Of those 1,36,939 NMC-listed seats, 63,296 are in government colleges and 73,643 are private. Private colleges account for about 54% of the listed capacity. If we compare the NEET re-test pool only with NMC-listed government seats, the candidate pool is roughly 31.6 times the available government capacity.

Level of competition

Government seats are prized because of substantially greater affordability, the reputation of established institutions and, in many large public hospitals, the prospect of extensive clinical exposure.

This year's expansion makes that distinction sharper. NMC approved 9,911 additional MBBS seats for 2026-27. Of these, 7,800 are private and only 2,111 government.

Skewed nature of growth of MBBA seats

Nearly four out of every five newly approved seats were added on the private side. So medicine and engineering are more alike than they look. In both, the real contest is increasingly over which seat, in which institution, and at what cost. There is, however, an important difference between the engineering and medical journeys.

An engineer can enter another fierce competition through GATE for MTech, but postgraduate study remains an optional route for most. For doctors who want to specialise, postgraduate training is much closer to another necessary career gate.

The latest completed NEET-PG examination makes the scale clear. More than 2.42 lakh candidates appeared for NEET-PG 2025, according to the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences.

NEET-PG 2026 is yet to be held and is scheduled for August 30.

And the postgraduate pool is much smaller than the undergraduate universe. The Centre said in July that India had 86,360 postgraduate medical seats in 2025-26. Earlier this year, it said 8,967 additional PG seats, including those in AIIMS and other Institutes of National Importance, had been approved for 2025-26. For some who pursue super-specialisation, there may still be another competitive gate beyond that.

Governments have tried to build capacity

Governments have tried to accommodate more students in quality institutions. Seven IITs have been established since 2014, while approved expansion at five newer IITs is intended to create capacity for another 6,500 students. In medicine, 157 government medical colleges have been approved under one central scheme, with 137 already functional. Separate government programmes have also expanded undergraduate and postgraduate capacity.

But adding seats does not automatically solve the problem. The latest figures placed before Parliament show 15.35 lakh registered allopathic doctors and 7.52 lakh AYUSH practitioners and, assuming 80% availability in both groups, a government-estimated combined practitioner-population ratio of 1:778. Yet the existence of incentives for hard-to-serve areas underlines another problem. Doctors and specialists are not distributed evenly.

So hierarchy exists beyond educational institutions too, which makes the work of policymakers even harder in a large country like India.

How other countries filter their best

In the US, 54,699 people applied to MD-granting medical schools in 2025 and 23,440 matriculated, but candidates generally apply after or during undergraduate study and typically take the MCAT. In England, medicine remains one of the most competitive university routes, with a sizeable socioeconomic gap in acceptance rates.

France pushes much of the filter inside university, with two in five students entering its PASS or L.AS health routes in 2022 reaching medicine or another major health discipline within two years. China's Gaokao had 1.29 crore registrations in 2026, but admissions are distributed across provinces, universities and programmes rather than through a single NEET-style medicine pool. Russia uses another lever altogether, with targeted state-funded medical training linked to future employment and workforce.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Every country has tried different approaches based on the reality of the land. Whether a test like NEET is the best way forward is still being intensely debated. However, for policymakers, the only feasible solution seems to be building more institutions of comparable quality, ones students believe can offer strong education, credible employment prospects and a better quality of life. Simply multiplying seats is unlikely to be enough if aspirants continue to see only a small proportion of them as worth fighting for.

NEW DELHI: A Lok Sabha inquiry committee on Wednesday indicted former Allahabad High Court judge Yashwant Varma in the cash-at-home case.The panel found Justice Varmaâs explanation for the discovery of unaccounted cash at his official residence "evasive" and "unsatisfactory". Its report, tabled in both Houses of Parliament, said all three charges against Varma were proved.The committee said the charges are threefold - firstly, discovery and possession of unexplained Indian currency notes within official premises; secondly, failure to preserve and causing interference with material evidence; and thirdly, furnishing evasive and misleading explanations.The committee examined documentary and electronic material and recorded evidence from witnesses. It also noted that Varma was given an opportunity to respond to the charges and present his defence."The statement of grounds accompanying the charges records the occurrence of fire, discovery of cash, location of the storeroom within the Government-allotted residence, the alleged conduct after the fire, and the explanation offered by the Judge," the inquiry report said."Article I is proved. Substantial unexplained Rs 500 denomination currency notes were found in the storeroom situated within the official residential premises at 30, Tughlaq Crescent, New Delhi.The Judge failed to furnish a satisfactory explanation regarding the presence, source or ownership thereof," it said.On the third charge, the committee said Varmaâs explanation, including his March 22, 2025 response and subsequent statements, did not demonstrate the "candour, transparency and institutional responsibility" expected in the circumstances. It remained evasive and unsatisfactory when tested against evidence from independent officials and other corroborative material.A large amount of unaccounted, partially burnt cash was discovered in the outhouse of Varmaâs official residence following a fire in March 2025. The discovery triggered allegations of judicial corruption, which Varma denied.Following an in-house inquiry ordered by the then Chief Justice of India, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla constituted a three-member panel headed by Supreme Court judge Aravind Kumar under the Judges (Inquiry) Act. The motion for the inquiry was backed by MPs from different political parties.Varma resigned during the inquiry. It remains unclear whether Parliament will proceed with the committeeâs findings, as some legal experts have argued that the Judges (Inquiry) Act can be invoked only against a serving judge.

World.title: 'No force used': Cong defends J'khand govt amid youth stir, accuses BJP of shielding ‘exam mafia’
World.content:
Congress on Wednesday defended the Jharkhand governmentâs handling of the studentsâ agitation over alleged examination irregularities, claiming that no force was used against protesting students and accusing the BJP of attempting to divert the issue.

The Congress ministers said the state government had taken steps to check examination paper leaks even before the students took to the streets. They alleged that the BJP, instead of supporting an investigation by the Jharkhand CID, was demanding a CBI probe to âshield the exam mafiaâ, news agency PTI reports.

"To shield 'exam mafia', BJP wants probe into paper leaks by its 'tool' CBI instead of Jharkhand CID."

The Congress leaders also accused the BJP of adopting a different approach when it was in power in Jharkhand, alleging that the previous BJP government had âcrushed the voice of youthâ during protests.

Cong claims 152 paper leaks since 2015 under BJP

Citing party data, the ministers claimed that 152 paper leaks had been reported across the country since 2015 under BJP rule, but the CBI had investigated only 17 of these cases and there had been no convictions.

The Congress ministers further alleged that the BJP's Jharkhand leadership was acting at the Centre's behest to disrupt the students' agitation. They claimed that gheraoing the state assembly was not part of the protesters' original agenda and alleged that the BJP brought people from other states to disrupt the students' âpeacefulâ protest in Ranchi on August 10.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





What we know

On Monday, students gathered near the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha as part of a march and formed a human chain seeking action on their demands.

The protests intensified after police allegedly used water cannons and force to control the crowd as the protesters moved towards the Assembly. The students have been protesting over alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).

They are demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the alleged irregularities and comprehensive reforms in the recruitment process.

World.title: Hubballi-Varanasi train service to run thrice a week; railway station to get high-tech upgrade
World.content:
The Hubballi-Varanasi train service will soon be increased to three days a week, while the Hubballi railway station will be upgraded with modern facilities, Union Minister for Education, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Pralhad Joshi said on Tuesday.

Mr. Joshi, who met with Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw in New Delhi on Wednesday, said in a press release that he had raised several long-pending demands of passengers from north Karnataka.

On his request for operating the existing Hubballi-Varanasi train (Nos. 07323/07324) three days a week to improve connectivity between north Karnataka and Varanasi, Mr. Vaishnaw assured me that the frequency of the service would be increased soon, Mr. Joshi said.

Modernisation

Mr. Vaishnaw agreed to upgrade the Hubballi railway station with modern and high-tech facilities on the lines of an airport. The upgraded station was expected to have organised parking facilities, a shopping mall, multiplex, modern restaurants and commercial outlets, besides other passenger amenities, Mr. Joshi said.

Mr. Joshi thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Mr. Vaishnaw and Minister of State for Railways V. Somanna for according priority to improving passenger and pilgrim connectivity in north Karnataka.

World.title: NIT-K lays foundation stone for healthcare centre annexe building
World.content:
The National Institute of Technology-Karnataka (NIT-K), Surathkal, recently laid the foundation stone for a new annexe building for its healthcare centre on the campus. The building is being funded by its alumni.

NIT-K Director B. Ravi laid the foundation stone during the institute’s 67th foundation day celebrations in the presence of IIT-Dharwad Director Venkappayya R. Desai, NIT-K Deputy Director Subhash C. Yaragal, deans, functionaries, faculty and staff members, and alumni, including members of the 1986 and 1972 batches along with other alumni donors.

The project has been funded through alumni contributions totaling ₹1.75 crore. The 1986 batch was the largest contributor at ₹1.01 crore, followed by the 1972 batch at ₹29 lakh. Additional support came from individual donors and other batch reunions.

The annexe building will be a ground-plus-one structure spanning approximately 3,100 sq. ft. The ground floor will house an ECG-nebulisation room with three beds, a two-bed casualty ward, a sterilisation room, two resident doctors’ consultation rooms, and ambulance parking. The first floor will include a physiotherapy facility with four beds, three specialist doctors’ consultation rooms, separate restrooms for men and women, and a meeting room.
